title: Bills Trade Deadline Tracker: Every Rumor, Reported Move for Buffalo
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have one more day to make an addition to their roster via trade, as the NFL trade deadline will fall on Tuesday afternoon at 4 p.m. ET.
Sitting at 7-1 after a win over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night, the Bills once again have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations in 2026, and that means general manager Brandon Beane should be aggressive in order to improve his roster. Unfortunately, there isn't any guarantee he'll actually be aggressive.
The focus is clear for Beane. The Bills desperately need to improve their defense that has been terrible this season. Buffalo has given up 29 points or more in five games, and the three games the Bills' defense did play well, they came against the lowly Los Angeles Chargers and two teams that were starting backups, the Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens.
As Beane and the Bills navigate deadline day, you can follow our tracker below for the latest rumors and reported moves Buffalo makes (note: most recent updates are at the top).
Baker open to trade, but Cards won't move him?
Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer is yet another insider reporting that Baker wouldn't mind a trade but the Cardinals don't appear willing to make a move.
"The Cardinals have gotten calls on star safety Budda Baker, who I’ve heard wouldn’t mind being dealt to a contender. Thus far, they haven’t been as receptive to moving him," Breer said.
Free Budda! And, taking it a step further, free him to Buffalo.
In all seriousness, it's hard to believe that the Cardinals won't give Baker what he wants. That would be a major slap in the face to a player who has meant so much to the franchise.
Budda Baker might want a trade, Amani Hooker staying put
Two players linked to the Bills often have been Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker and Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker.
Jeremy Fowler reports that Baker might be open to a trade , but it remains to be seen if the Cardinals want to trade him. Meanwhile, the Titans are keen on keeping Hooker.
"My sense is Budda Baker would welcome chance to play for contender if AZ entertains talks (big if). Tennessee has calls on Amani Hooker but wants to keep him," Fowler reported.
Bills looking for safety, cornerback help
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler is reporting that the Bills "have scanned the safety pool of late."
Both Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer and The Athletic's Jonathan Jones have previously reported the same , although both added cornerback as another position the Bills are looking around for.
"The Bills have made calls on safeties and cornerbacks," Jones wrote
"I had it in my last trade column, and will add it here — The Bills are still looking in to adding a piece on the defensive side of the ball. And specifically at corner and safety," Breer said.
The Bills have not made any trades yet, but we'll update this section if anything happens.
Over his tenure as general manager, Beane has made eight trades during a season. Here's a look at what he has done in the past:
2017: DT Marcel Dareus to Jaguars 2017: WR Kelvin Benjamin from Panthers 2018: OL Marshall Newhouse to Panthers 2019: WR Zay Jones to Raiders 2022: S Dean Marlowe from Falcons 2023: RB Nyheim Hines from Colts for RB Zack Moss, R6 pick 2023: CB Rasul Douglas from Packers 2024: WR Amari Cooper from Browns
Safety: The Bills need a starter here after cutting C.J. Gardner-Johnson . Damar Hamlin is having a nice season, but he's better suited as a backup.
Cornerback: With uncertainty surrounding Davison Igbinosun and Maxwell Hairston, the Bills could use help on the boundary across from Christian Benford. Slot cornerback is another spot where Buffalo could add with Dee Alford's struggles.
Linebacker: An addition at this position makes sense for the Bills because they could use an upgrade over Dorian Williams and it doesn't look like Kaleb Elarms-Orr is ready to be that guy.

title: Why Brandon Beane, Bills Should Not Trade for Defensive Help at NFL Deadline
full_text:
The final hours until the 2026 NFL trade deadline await the Buffalo Bills , and in the midst of their Week 9 battle against the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night, it's decision time for general manager Brandon Beane on whether he wants to improve an ailing defense .
The Jacksonville Jaguars and Chicago Bears are two teams that have swung trades to acquire defenders, whether they're big names or depth pieces, and Beane has been pressured to kingdom come to be as aggressive as James Gladstone, Ryan Poles and other GMs.
However, there are reasons for Bills fans to feel optimistic about their defense, which ranks 23rd in the NFL in EPA per play and 28th in EPA per dropback as of Monday, if Buffalo does not acquire anyone of note before Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline.
Heck of a read by Geno Stone on IGB's interception! I expect the Bills to utilize these Dime groupings with 3 Safeties on the field a lot the rest of the season. pic.twitter.com/4mxHwkZMa6
C.J. Gardner-Johnson's release following his one-game suspension for spitting on Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers came with another reason: Geno Stone, who signed a one-year deal in March . After failing to make the 53-man roster, he joined the Bills' practice squad and made his debut on November 1 against the Baltimore Ravens.
Stone tied for the team lead with six tackles while adding a tackle for loss and a pass defended. He was also partially responsible for Davison Igbinosun's first career interception, tipping a Joe Fagnano pass into the air for the rookie corner to snatch.
Stone was called up from the practice squad again on Monday just before the Bills' game against the Vikings, and if he plays well against Carson Wentz and Justin Jefferson, that may deter Beane from going after someone like Budda Baker .
Davison Igbinosun has quietly been one of the STICKIEST CB’s in the NFL this season. Through six games, Igbinosun LEADS the Bills’ defense with 7 PD’s (T-6th in NFL). The Bills rookie CB might find himself as the team’s CB1 sooner rather than later 😳🔒 pic.twitter.com/Zcr4q4AWqR
Speaking of Jefferson, the Bills' second-round rookie cornerback out of Ohio State , Igbinosun, may have to face him a few times. If he does, it'll be a great chance to present himself to a national audience as someone on the rise.
Igbinosun took the starting cornerback spot opposite Christian Benford from former first-round pick Maxwell Hairston against the Ravens. After three passes defended against the Raiders in Week 6, he tallied another to go with his first career pick in Week 8.
The Bills' defense as a whole rebounded nicely against the Ravens, even if they went up against a third-string quarterback for the majority of the game, and Igbinosun was a main reason for that.
Dorian Williams and Terrel Bernard, the Bills' two main linebackers, have struggled in spots this season , and if they play poorly on Monday night, things may need to change. Buffalo may not have to look outside their organization for help, however.
The answer may come in the form of giving fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr more snaps or elevating Shaq Thompson , who made six starts for the Bills in 2025, from the practice squad.
If Thompson were to be elevated, his experience would mesh nicely with a Buffalo defense that does not have a player whose first season in the league was earlier than 2018.
Regardless, Monday night's game will be very telling as to whether Beane will or will not feel the urgency to make a trade acquisition to aid the defense.

title: Five Winners, One Loser from Bills' Gutsy Road Victory over Vikings on Monday Night
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills dominated on defense, and its offense wore the Minnesota Vikings down over the course of a 23-6 road win on Monday Night Football.
The Bills possessed the ball for an astounding 42:32, holding their second straight opponent under 200 yards of total offense. Buffalo's defense did not permit a third-down conversion on eight attempts.
Meanwhile, going against the Vikings' vaunted defense , the Bills did enough when they had to.
As for the individual actors who led the Bills (7-1) past the Vikings (6-2), here five WINNERS and one LOSER.
It was tough sledding for most of the night, but Cook kept at it. The reigning NFL rushing champion didn't stop grinding, accounting for 107 yards and one touchdown on a season-high 31 carries.
Cook rushed for 47 yards on a fourth-quarter possession punctuated by the running back's five-yard touchdown burst. He has four 100-yard rushing performance through the first eight games.
Latu's first career touchdown reception came with the Bills struggling to gain traction during the first half. Buffalo's fourth tight end hauled in a 25-yard scoring strike on a broken play.
With Allen escaping the pocket, the defense seemingly forgot about Latu, who was waiting alone in the end zone. Rolling right toward the sideline, Allen stopped and fired a beauty for the game's first touchdown.
Much like the first half against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, the Bills' offense looked out of sync through the opening 30 minutes on Monday Night Football. Brady called rushes on seven of the first nine first-down snaps despite repeatedly running into a wall.
After Josh Allen failed on trying to go wide at the goal line against the Ravens, Buffalo foolishly called an outside run on a key 3rd-and-2 inside Vikings' territory rather than opt for a higher percentage play. Running behind backups at left tackle and left guard, Cook was dropped for a two-yard loss while Tylan Grable was called for holding.
Rousseau single-handedly derailed a Vikings' second-quarter possession in Bills' territory. He sacked Carson Wentz on first down followed by a pressure and pass deflection on 2nd-and-21.
After one sack, three quarterback hits and two pass deflections against the Ravens, Rousseau kept the heat on against the Vikings. He also recovered a fumble when a lateral pass to Justin Jefferson went awry.
Bernard has been criticized for appearing slow and out of position in the Bills' new defense , but the co-captain looked like his old self on Monday.
In addition to making a couple nice hits that held the opponent short of the sticks, Bernard made a nice interception and subsequently dropped a second pick. Leading the team with six tackles, Bernard held it down in the middle of the defense.
Playing alongside Bernard, Williams made three tackles in the victory. Furthermore, the inside linebacker was effective in pass coverage, which hasn't necessarily been his strength as a pro.
After Bernard was flagged for a 19-yard penalty that gave the Vikings a 1st-and-10 from the Bills' 37, Williams delivered a true momentum shifter. On 3rd-and-5, Williams intercepted an underthrown ball by Wentz while covering Vikings' tight end TJ Hockenson one-on-one down the seam.

title: Christian Benford Injury Update: Latest News on Bills CB's Status in Week 9 Game
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have an injury concern with cornerback Christian Benford going into the second half of the Week 9 game against the Minnesota Vikings.
Benford suffered his injury right before halftime in the second quarter. It happened on Justin Jefferson's second catch near Buffalo's sideline when Benford tackled the Vikings wideout.
Prior to his injury, Benford had recorded two tackles and one pass defensed, and he was playing lights-out coverage on Jefferson, who did nothing before a few catches to close out the half.
Follow our tracker below for the latest updates on Benford's status for the rest of the game against the Vikings.
UPDATE: Great news for the Bills, as Benford has returned to the game after he was listed as questionable due to his wrist injury.
"Christian Benford is on the field to start the 2nd half.  He was  questionable to return (wrist)," Sal Capaccio of WGR550 said.
The Bills announced that Benford has suffered a wrist injury and his return to the game is questionable.
"Injury Update: CB Christian Benford (wrist) is questionable to return," the Bills said.
Sal Maiorana of the Democrat and Chronicle reports that Benford was carted off to the locker room before halftime, which is a terrible sign.
"Christian Benford just got carted off, arm injury," Maiorana said.
Here's a look at the video of the play where Benford got hurt.
Re: Christian Benford #billsmafia Idk fam what you think? heel to chest? Nothing burger? https://t.co/RJAqiF8HfG pic.twitter.com/8T4A7exGYj
Hopefully it isn't as bad as it looks initially. We'll be on the lookout for more updates on Benford and we'll put them above as they come.
The Bills entered this game with the third-worst pass defense in the NFL, so it doesn't need to be said just how tough of a blow it would be if Buffalo loses it's No. 1 cornerback.
We've seen what kind of impact Benford can make after he was sensational against an elite receiver like Jefferson in the first half. The Bills don't have anyone else on the roster who can do that.
As long as Benford is sidelined, the Bills are likely going to deploy Maxwell Hairston in his place, with rookie Davison Igbinosun on the other side.
This isn't the first time Benford has dealt with an injury this season, as he's missed one game and has been on the injury report multiple times.
Over his first six games, Benford surrendered a completion rate of 55% and a passer rating of 96.1 when targeted.

title: Dalton Kincaid Promises 'It's Coming' as Josh Allen Demands More from Bills' Offense
full_text:
It's hard to believe that a NFL offense scoring a league-high 33.3 points is underperforming, but such is the case with the Buffalo Bills .
When watching them closely, one can see subtle errors that cost the Bills (6-1) points over the course of the game.
There are occasional misses through the air like when Josh Allen overthrew Keon Coleman running wide open deep downfield for a would-be touchdown against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8.
There have been fumbles by stud running back James Cook and notable drops by receivers. There have also been penalties like Dion Dawkins's false start at home against the Ravens and an offensive holding penalty that took a Dalton Kincaid touchdown off the board against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Last time out against Baltimore, following a pretty opening touchdown drive, the Bills' offense appeared disjointed and out of sync for the remainder of the first half.
Buffalo turned the ball over in its own end when tight Jackson Hawes bobbled a pass into a defender's hands. They also turned the ball over on downs in the red zone, failing to score despite facing a 3rd-and-goal from the half-yard line.
"That first half was, in our standards, really bad. We didn't play up to our standard. Weren't throwing it, catching it. Didn't feel like I was doing a good enough job," said Allen. "Obviously, the couple turnovers in the front in the first half, it's not winning football. Sitting there, we're talking with the guys in going into halftime, just saying, 'hey, we're way better than this.'"
Buffalo responded by scoring touchdowns on three of its first four second-half possessions to grab a stranglehold on the game.
"It's just focusing on the details. We went out there, couldn't tell you our second half splits, but that second half is who we want to be," said Allen.
Kincaid dropped what could've been a touchdown against the Ravens, but he bounced back to haul in a scoring strike in the fourth quarter.
Seeing 57 percent of offensive snaps, Kincaid caught four of six targets for 86 yards in the 36-10 win. Still, the tight end knows the offense can be better , and it's only a matter of time before everything clicks.
"We're just waiting for that game when we put it together for 60 minutes. I feel like it's coming, and we're very capable of doing that, but still have success, put up 36 points," said Kincaid.
What better time to put it all together than when challenging the NFL's top-ranked pass defense (154.9) on Monday Night Football. The Bills face a tall task against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 9.
The good news for Buffalo is that Kincaid, wide receiver DJ Moore and wide receiver Keon Coleman will be at full strength.

title: Buffalo Bills vs. Minnesota Vikings Inactives: Who's In, Who's Out for Week 9
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings have released their lists of inactives ahead of the Week 9 contest on Monday night.
The Bills ruled out one player ahead of Monday in wide receiver Joshua Palmer, who has since been placed on injured reserve because of his hamstring injury.
Buffalo entered Monday with five players listed as questionable, including left tackle Dion Dawkins, left guard Alec Anderson, wide receiver Tyrell Shavers (PUP), defensive back Jordan Hancock (IR) and defensive lineman Greg Gaines.
All five of those players are inactive. With Anderson and Dawkins out, that means Tylan Grable will play left tackle and Austin Corbett will start at left guard.
Meanwhile, the Vikings ruled out quarterback Kyler Murray early in the week, and he was joined by wide receiver Jauan Jennings and running back Demond Claiborne.
Minnesota had two players listed as questionable in defensive back Theo Jackson and safety Jay Ward. Jackson is inactive.
Now, a look at the full list of inactives for both teams ahead of kickoff on Monday night.
Buffalo Bills inactives: WR Skyler Bell, S Jalon Kilgore, DE Mike Danna, OG Alec Anderson, LT Dion Dawkins, DL Greg Gaines
Minnesota Vikings inactives: QB Kyler Murray, S Jakobe Thomas, WR Jauan Jennings, CB Chuck Demmings, S Theo Jackson, DL Caleb Banks
The absences of Dawkins and Anderson are massive blows for the Bills' offense, and that's especially true against an elite defense like Minnesota's that blitzes a ton.
The Bills had elevated wide receiver Trent Sherfield and safety Geno Stone from the practice squad before kickoff and they're active for the contest. Sherfield is up because of the injury to Palmer and Stone is taking Kilgore's spot.
With Kyler Murray ruled out for the Vikings, the team will be handing the ball over to Carson Wentz, which might actually be bad news for the Bills because Murray has struggled in 2026.
If Wentz proves to be a better option, he could really dice up the Bills' defense that is giving up the third-most passing yards per game this season.
Here's a fun one: wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr., who was promoted from the practice squad over the weekend, will be suited up for Minnesota.
There was a ton of confusion with wide receiver DJ Moore in the hours leading up to kickoff.
ESPN's NFL Live reported that Moore, who was on the injury report with a shouler issue this week before being officially cleared on Saturday, would be inactive .
However, that turned out to be a mistake and Moore is going to play in Week 9.
"Not sure what was heard on ESPN about D.J. Moore but a league source tells me Moore is fine and expected to play vs. the Vikings," Matt Parrino Syracuse.com wrote.
Sal Capaccio of WGR550 later reported that the network had a "miscommunication" that was the cause of the mix-up.
"From what I understand, the ESPN miscommunication re: DJ Moore stemmed from the last MNF game the Bills played (at Rams) when he was inactive," Capaccio reported.
So, if you see the clip floating around on the interwebs, just now that it is not true and Moore is good to go for Monday night.

title: Panthers' Week 9 Loss to Broncos Sends Clear Message Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Panthers had a chance to send a message to the rest of the league on Sunday as they took on the Denver Broncos. However, the Panthers were defeated by the Broncos 26-21, dropping to 3-5 on the year after losing three consecutive games.
The Panthers proved that they can compete with a good team in the AFC but also showed that there is still a lot of work to be done with this team. Bryce Young threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns, but costly mistakes kept Carolina from coming away with the win.
The Carolina Panthers have until Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET to make a trade . Carolina's general manager, Dan Morgan, must decide whether to add a player to help the team make a push for the playoffs or be patient and continue building through the draft.
That decision was made a little easier on Sunday with the Panthers' loss to the Broncos.
This is still a work-in-progress team that is showing signs of growth in some areas but is still a far cry from being a complete football team. There have been times when the offense has looked very good, but even when Carolina moves the football, mistakes and missed opportunities have made it difficult to finish games.
The defense has given up too many big plays in several games, and there are still questions about whether the team has enough talent to get consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks.
These are issues that will not be resolved by the addition of one player via trade before Tuesday afternoon.
The Panthers have tried to build a team for more than one season over the last few years. Giving up draft picks for a player who may help the Panthers for a few months but then leave in free agency is not in the best interest of a team currently sitting below .500.
While there is some value in exploring possible trades, Morgan should be cautious about overpaying for a player just to win a few more games this season. Carolina's injuries at cornerback have already raised questions about how much the team should be willing to give up for help .
There is a huge difference between making a trade that helps build the Panthers' roster for the future and making a trade to try to win more games this year.
While the Panthers lost on Sunday, they also showed that they are not as far away from competing with the upper echelon of the NFL as their record would indicate. Carolina moved the football well against Denver and had a chance to win the game late.
That gives the coaching staff something to work with for the remainder of the season. But it does not mean that the front office should start dealing future assets to try to make the playoffs this season.
Morgan needs to continue focusing on building a more talented defense for the Panthers and building around Bryce Young rather than trying to find quick solutions.
By the end of the season, the Panthers should have a better understanding of which players on the current roster need a bigger role on the team and which positions need to be addressed in the offseason.
While there is nothing wrong with trying to make the team better before the deadline, it would be wise for the Panthers to avoid overpaying for a player who does not fit into the organization's long-term plans.
The Panthers have enough talent to take another step forward this season. However, they are not ready to mortgage the future of the organization to make the playoffs this year.
Sunday's loss to Denver was another reminder of that.
General manager Dan Morgan should be willing to listen to offers and make a move if the right opportunity presents itself. But if nothing happens by Tuesday's deadline, that wouldn't be a bad thing either.
Sometimes the best move a general manager can make is knowing when not to make one.

title: Panthers' Cornerback Injuries Expose a Problem Dan Morgan Can't Ignore
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have had many cornerbacks go down with injuries this season, and Panthers general manager Dan Morgan is currently searching for some healthy bodies to put out on the field. The Panthers also had a lack of depth at the position even before all of these injuries occurred.
Now, with Tuesday afternoon's NFL trade deadline approaching, Morgan is going to have to make a decision as to whether or not to trade for a cornerback or wait until the offseason.
The Panthers lost both Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson i n the Browns game in Week 3. Both players were placed on injured reserve.
To make matters worse, Akayleb Evans was placed on IR on October 29. Additionally, rookie Will Lee III suffered a hamstring injury against the Packers. The Panthers were down to their last healthy cornerbacks on the roster for the Broncos game.
Chau Smith-Wade is listed as a starting cornerback for the Panthers, with Malcolm DeWalt IV listed as a backup on the depth chart.
Of course, the coaching staff is trying to get the best out of what's left of the roster, but there's only so much they can do with so many players injured.
The number of injuries the Panthers have experienced at cornerback this season was unforeseen by many. However, the injuries have exposed the need for the Panthers to have a better plan behind their starters at cornerback.
Carolina does not have to make a trade before today's 4 p.m. ET trade deadline. Morgan could look to add a veteran cornerback to help the team out for the rest of the year. He could also look to use an early pick in the draft on another cornerback or make it a priority in free agency.
Horn and Jackson will return at some point, but that doesn't mean the Panthers will be in good shape at the position if either player goes down again for an extended period of time.
Morgan can't just go out and find another cornerback to put on the field. He has to find a player who can do what the coaching staff wants him to do without forcing the rest of the defense to make so many adjustments when a starter is out of action.
The Panthers have tried to put together a roster to contend in the NFC South over the last few years, but cornerback is still a position of concern.
Morgan doesn't have to make a desperate move before the deadline, but he does need to make sure the Panthers have better options behind their starters moving forward.

title: 2 Trades the Panthers Have to Make After 3rd Straight Loss
full_text:
The NFL's trade deadline is here, and there's potential for an active day filled with surprising moves and big names dealt to new franchises. The Carolina Panthers are in a precarious spot entering Tuesday's deadline.
Coming off a third straight loss , this time at home to the Denver Broncos. The Panthers have taken a nosedive from their 3-2 start. However, they still remain alive for the division title because the NFC South is so bad this season.
The NFC South went 1-3 in Week 9, with the New Orleans Saints as the lone winner. Due to tiebreakers, the Panthers are still sitting atop the division despite a 3-5 record. With the division title still being a real possibility and a pivotal Week 10 matchup against the Saints ahead, Carolina needs to make moves.
Here are two trades that make perfect sense for the Panthers.
Part of the loss to the Broncos that was so frustrating for the Panthers was the issues in the secondary. It was clear that Denver head coach Sean Payton wanted to test the back end of Carolina's defense, and it worked.
Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton received seven penalty flags. Wilson was especially undisciplined, drawing multiple flags for pass interference and even for a taunting call.
If there weren't penalties, then it was either missing assignments or just losing one-on-one matchups against Denver's receivers.
There's still time before Jaycee Horn or Mike Jackson returns to the field, so Carolina needs to trade for a bridge starting corner, enter Riq Woolen.
Woolen is coming off a Super Bowl season with the Seahawks, being a contributor to that elite defense. Now he's with the Philadelphia Eagles, who could be in fire-sale mode based on their recent deal involving DT Jordan Davis.
Carolina wouldn't have to give up more than a fourth-round pick for Woolen. The Panthers own two fourth-round picks this year, including their own and the Vikings'.
Carolina's pass rush was supposed to be the team's most improved unit on this team. However, injuries have plagued it thus far. Carolina began the season without budding star Nic Scourton, who tore his ACL, and has been without Jaelan Phillips for weeks due to a hamstring injury.
If there's one way to help the secondary without directly addressing it, it's adding to the pass rush. Will McDonald IV is a key name to watch at the deadline. McDonald requested a trade from the New York Jets because he hasn't seen much usage.
There's clearly talent there, as McDonald has had a double-digit sack season before, with 10.5 in 2024. This could be a situation where a change of scenery unlocks his potential once again.
Carolina would have to give up a valuable asset, likely a second-round pick or a package of a third and a sixth. That said, one of those picks could very well be worth it for a 27-year-old pass rusher who's in the prime of his career.

title: Panthers Stock Up, Stock Down: Two Bright Spots Can't Hide Bigger Problems
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers lost their third consecutive game on Sunday to the Denver Broncos by a score of 26-21. The Panthers are still trying to put together four quarters of quality football this year.
Several Panthers played well in the game, but there are still some major issues that the Panthers have yet to fix this season. Here's a look at whose stock rose and whose stock fell in the game against the Broncos.
Darren Walle r had a phenomenal game for the Panthers, recording eight receptions for 90 yards and a touchdown against the Broncos. This was easily Waller's best game of the season, as he recorded his highest number of receptions and receiving yards in a game this year.
His eight receptions on Sunday were also the most by a Panthers tight end in a single game since Greg Olsen had eight receptions in 2019. The Panthers have been searching for a reliable target in the middle of the field all season, and Waller showed on Sunday that he can be that guy.
Young connected with Waller for a 15-yard touchdown in the third quarter to give the Panthers their first lead of the game. He now has four touchdowns on the year.
The Panthers need to find more ways to get Waller the ball. Young has found another target to trust, especially when the receivers aren't getting open.
Corey Thornton had to step up in a big way against the Broncos. With numerous injuries at cornerback, the Panthers were forced to put Thornton into the starting lineup. Thornton had three tackles, three passes defended and an interception in his first career start.
There were some rough spots for Thornton, including two pass interference penalties, but overall, Thornton showed that he belongs on the field. His interception was one of the better defensive plays of the day for the Panthers.
The Panthers will need even more from Thornton in the coming weeks if the injuries at cornerback continue to mount. While he will make mistakes, Thornton's first career interception and three passes defended in his first career start are something that the coaching staff can build upon.
Young threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns in the game, some of his better numbers of the season. However, the Panthers' offensive line could not keep the pressure off Young when the Panthers needed another drive to win the game.
With 1:24 remaining in the fourth quarter and the Panthers trailing by five, Broncos linebacker Nik Bonitto stripped the ball from Young and recovered the fumble, ending the Panthers' hopes of scoring late to win the game.
Young was sacked three times against the Broncos after being sacked six times against the Packers the previous week. That is nine sacks in the last two games for Young.
The Panthers' offense had some great moments in the game, but when they needed to score late to win, the protection broke down, and the Panthers never got another opportunity.
There are some good players on the Panthers' roster, but there are some holes as well. The depth at cornerback is definitely one of them. The Panthers have suffered numerous injuries at cornerback, but that does not mean they should be relying on practice-squad players against some of the best teams in the NFL.
The Broncos attacked the Panthers' cornerbacks early in the game. Corey Thornton and Marco Wilson were called for four enforced defensive pass interference penalties, and the P anthers finished with 13 penalties for 119 yards.
The Panthers were already short-handed at cornerback before the game, and Denver took advantage of that weakness.
There are many good things that Morgan has done as general manager of the Panthers, but cornerback depth is still a problem that needs to be addressed. It is hard to expect the defense to play well when players who were not expected to start are suddenly expected to play at a high level.
There is still time before Tuesday's trade deadline for Morgan to make a move to acquire more depth at cornerback. He does not have to give up valuable draft picks to get help, but whether he makes a move now or in the offseason, the Panthers need more dependable players to back up their starting cornerbacks.
The Panthers can hang with the best teams in the NFL, but they need to find a way to finish those games. Until the Panthers solve some of their roster problems, great individual performances like those of Waller and Thornton will not always be enough to win games.

title: Slumping Panthers Still Atop an NFC South in Total Disarray
full_text:
A season ago, the NFC South was won by a team that lost more games than it won. That would be the Carolina Panthers, who captured its first division title since 2015 with an 8-9 win-loss record. Of course, that was also the case back in 2022, when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers finished 2022 also managed an 8-9 mark and walked away with the top spot in the division.
Speaking of the Panthers, they are currently tied for the best record in the NFC South with the 3-5 New Orleans Saints. Dave Canales's team currently has the tie-breaking edge due to the fact that they have split a pair of divisional games. On the other hand, Kellen Moore’s club was blasted at home by the Atlanta Falcons, 45-24, on a Monday night in Week 4 in the club’s lone clash with an NFC South rival this season.
That changes this week when the Saints host the Panthers on Sunday afternoon for the first of their two meetings. A year ago, Moore’s team finished 6-11 and in the division basement (the 3 other clubs all posted 8-9 records), but they managed to sweep Carolina. And given the way things have gone for each of the four clubs at home this season, it’s anyone’s guess what will happen at the Superdome.
Not only is every team in this division at least two games under .500, the four clubs all own sub-.500 marks at home. Now keep in mind that the Saints and Falcons have “home” losses to the Steelers and Bengals in Paris and Madrid, respectively. Take those setbacks out and Carolina (1-3), New Orleans (1-3), Tampa Bay (1-4), and Atlanta (1-3) are a combined 4-13 in their own buildings this season.
As for Canales’s club, it is currently in the midst of a three-game skid, the latest loss a 26-21 home setback to the Denver Broncos on Sunday. The slide began back in Week 7 at Bank of America Stadium, when the Bucs opened up a 33-6 halftime advantage on the way to a 43-13 victory. That was followed by a Thursday night loss at Lambeau Field and yesterday’s loss to Sean Payton’s surging club.
The Panthers OL finally gave Bryce Young time to breathe and he rewarded them with a strong performance against the Broncos defense pic.twitter.com/GCGbIlw1cw
Ultimately, it may be the Saints who decide who wins this division due to the fact that they will face NFC South rivals in four of their final five games.
Here are the latest NFL Power Rankings via Vinny Iyer of The Sporting News , and it certainly speaks volumes when it comes to this quartet. He has the Buccaneers as the division’s top team, but at No. 21. They are followed by the Falcons at No. 22, the Saints at No. 23 and the slumping Panthers at No. 25.
Is it a foregone conclusion that the NFC South will have a champion with a losing record for the third time in five years? And is it possible we could see this division by a team with 10 losses?
Russell S. Baxter has been writing and researching the game of football for more than 40 years, and on numerous platforms. That includes television, as he spent more than two decades at ESPN, and was part of shows that garnered five Emmy Awards. He also spent the 2015 NFL season with Thursday Night Football on CBS/NFLN.

title: Reports of Bryce Young's Demise Were Greatly Exaggerated
full_text:
Bryce Young, quarterback for the Carolina Panthers, did have a good game against the Denver Broncos, but the Panthers lost the game. This season, Bryce Young has received a lot of criticism, some of it justified, but some of it not. There have been several games where the Panthers' offense has struggled to get anything going, and many fans are questioning whether or not Bryce Young is the Panthers' long-term answer at quarterback.
While the offense struggled in some of the Panthers' games this season, there were also games where the offense was clicking and Young looked like a good quarterback in the NFL.
It's easy to blame the quarterback for a loss when the offense isn't scoring enough points. For much of the season, fans and media have been wondering if the Panthers should be looking for a new quarterback.
The game against the Broncos was not enough to clear up all the questions that people have about Young, but it sure did give people something else to talk about.
While one game cannot be proof of anything, it can be the starting point to show that Young is capable of being a good quarterback in the NFL.
Young did his part to keep Carolina in the game. The Panthers didn't come away with a win, but the offense gave them a chance, and Young deserves some credit for that.
Carolina's offense has had some struggles this season, with Young holding onto the football too long and missing out on some opportunities to get the ball out quicker. These are certainly things that need to be addressed, but they shouldn't be the only things that people remember from his season.
Some of the talk about Bryce Young has made it seem like the Panthers are ready to move on from the young quarterback. After watching him against the Broncos, that doesn't appear to be the case.
While Bryce Young can receive much of the criticism for the Carolina Panthers' losses, t here are many other problems with the team that the Panthers must address.
The Panthers are going to have to get better at several things, and that includes Bryce Young. While he has some things that he can work on, the Panthers' offense needs to get better around him as well.
Even though Carolina lost to Denver on Sunday, Bryce Young gave the Panthers a chance to win the game.
Carolina may have another loss on its record, but Young gave his critics a reason to reconsider how quickly they've written him off. He still has plenty to prove, and Sunday's performance showed why that opportunity shouldn't be taken away just yet.

title: 3 Major Takeaways From Panthers' Frustrating Loss to Broncos
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers had opportunities to take down the Denver Broncos on Sunday, but the team fell short and lost to the Broncos, 26-21. After taking a 14-13 lead in the third quarter, the Panthers were unable to hold on and lost for the third straight game.
While the Panthers had several good moments, particularly on offense, errors in the game cost the team the victory. Once again, Carolina found itself in a position to win but couldn't finish the job.
Three things we learned from the Panthers' loss to Denver on Sunday.
Carolina had 13 penalties for 119 yards on Sunday. The Panthers gave up a lot of yards to the Broncos in the game, many of which came on penalties that allowed Denver to keep drives going.
There will always be some penalties in a game, but the Panthers had too many on Sunday. A number of the penalties were for pass interference, and some of those resulted in Denver gaining extra yardage on drives that otherwise would have ended.
The frustrating thing is that the Panthers were competitive for the majority of the game, and they didn't have to play a perfect game to win. But giving the Broncos free yards is not the way to win.
Dave Canales and his coaching staff have to get these penalties under control before they cost Carolina another game.
The Carolina Panthers quarterback, Bryce Young, had some really good plays on Sunday. He had three touchdown passes on the day, gave Carolina the lead in the third quarter and kept the Panthers in the game until the final minutes.
The Panthers have also had problems protecting Young throughout the season , making his performance against Denver an encouraging sign.
One of Carolina's scoring opportunities ended with a strange interception. Young threw to Tommy Tremble in the end zone, and the ball was deflected before ending up in the hands of Devon Key of the Denver Broncos.
Officials initially ruled the pass incomplete, but Denver challenged the call. After reviewing the play, officials determined that the ball had hit Tremble's foot rather than the ground before Key secured it, giving Denver the interception.
This took away another opportunity for the Carolina Panthers to extend their lead in the game. The ball wasn't caught by the receiver, and that was out of Young's hands.
Young had a solid game for the Panthers, throwing three touchdown passes. He gave the team opportunities to win, but the rest of the players on the field must take advantage of those opportunities.
The secondary was once again giving up too much space to opposing receivers, especially in the first half of the game. Bo Nix was able to find many of his receivers on short completions and drive the Broncos down the field.
As Panthers On SI discussed in its halftime breakdown, Carolina's defensive backs were giving Denver's receivers too much room to operate.
While the defense held Denver to a field goal prior to halftime, the secondary allowed too much space for the opposing team's receivers and gave up too many opportunities.
The Panthers also had a number of pass interference penalties on the defensive backs. Those penalties made it even harder for the defense to get off the field.
To be a competitive team in the NFL, the defensive backs of the Carolina Panthers need to challenge receivers and not give up easy completions to the opposing quarterback.
Even with the problems, the Panthers showed that they can compete with the Broncos. But too many mistakes are keeping Carolina from winning games.

He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Carolina Panthers Falter in NFL Power Rankings After Tough Loss to Broncos
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers looked for a moment like they were going to inexplicably right the ship. They had the Denver Broncos on the ropes, first-and-goal from the one with a seemingly inevitable eight-point lead coming in mere seconds.
A missed defensive pass interference on the first attempt is one thing , but letting the Panthers run a whole play before going back to grant a challenge is another. After it was overturned to an interception, the Panthers fell behind by 12 points, and their comeback attempt was thwarted by a sack-fumble.
For a moment, it felt like the Panthers might actually surge up the NFL Power Rankings this week, as they did after a shocking home win over the Detroit Lions. That is their second-most recent win, and it also feels like it was six months ago.
Now, the Panthers are 3-5 and in a freefall, no longer in first in the NFC South and tumbling down the power rankings.
The Panthers have been slipping and sliding in the Power Rankings for a few weeks now. After they beat the Philadelphia Eagles, they breached the top 10 on some lists. And at the time, it didn't feel ridiculous.
Since then, the entire season has turned on its head. A shocking and embarrassing home loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers started things in the wrong direction. That led to a frustrating one-score loss to the Green Bay Packers, which led to (checks notes) a frustrating one-score loss to the Denver Broncos.
Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer had the Panthers ranked 22nd last week , and now they're 25th. We firmly believe this team is better than that and better than 3-5, but the record is what it is. Injuries have played a role, but there's no caveat in the rankings.
"The Panthers' big defensive issue, with or without now-fired former defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero, has been staying on the field too much after third down. Opponents have converted around 54 percent against them. The Broncos were 6-for-10, even when held to 82 rushing yards by a horrible run defense," Iyer wrote.
Next up is the New Orleans Saints. They've been a thorn in Carolina's side, but this is a winnable game. The Saints are, however, riding high after a clutch overtime win over the Cleveland Browns, a team that beat the Panthers this year.
Regardless, that's their next chance to right the ship and get moving in the right direction on the power rankings.

title: The NFL’s Explanation of Broncos’ Challenge vs. Panthers Holds No Water
full_text:
We've all seen the play and the ridiculous circus that took place after, which turned into a Carolina Panthers turnover in the end zone. To summarize, Tommy Tremble appeared to be interfered with, and the ball bounced up off his hand and into the hands of Denver Broncos' DB Devon Key.
The Panthers then ran a whole play and got stuffed at the goal-line before referees appeared to retroactively grant a Sean Payton challenge. The tipped ball was correctly ruled an interception on the replay, so it was a touchback for the Broncos.
The Broncos went down and took a lead they wouldn't relinquish after that play. On a pretty dismal day by the referees, that mistake loomed large. Surely, the explanation after the game will help us all make sense of the unprecedented turn of events?
Pool reporter @alexzietlow05 spoke with referee Alan Eck and VP of Instant Replay Mark Butterworth after the game: pic.twitter.com/M2oETnPMXf
Not so. Charlotte Observer reporter Alex Zietlow asked the referees about the replay gaffe, and their explanation doesn't make any sense.
Head referee Alan Eck said, "Replay can get involved to make sure that the head coach throws his challenge flag prior to the next snap. We were actually able to use angles to show that the flag was out before the snap, and so we permitted the challenge."
That doesn't hold water, though. In the past, if the referees did not see the challenge flag come out and the play commenced, it's dead in the water. It's an unfortunate and rather silly aspect of the challenge process, but it's been this way forever.
If you don't get the ref to see what you want to do before the ball is snapped, then you're just out of luck. Unless you're Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos, it seems.
And it's not as if the referees blew the play dead because of the challenge. The play was blown dead because it had ended. The play had entirely taken place, and the referees decided to retroactively grant the challenge.
We won't pretend to have seen every challenge in NFL history, but that feels like something no one has seen before or will ever see again. And the nonsense explanation from Eck doesn't help the matter.
That's not the only mistake the refs made that hurt the Panthers, and it's not the only reason the Panthers fell short on Sunday in Charlotte. But it was essentially a 13-point swing in a five-point loss, and the NFL's attempt to justify one of the biggest mistakes this season just doesn't hold up.

title: Chargers Trade Rumor Gives Bears Shred of Hope for Khalil Mack Deal
full_text:
It seemed all hope was lost for the Chicago Bears when it came to a possible Khalil Mack trade, but the latest Los Angeles Chargers trade rumor has cracked the door open slightly.
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the Chargers have now changed their tune on trading players in contract years and are possibly willing to deal.
Schultz adds that Mack, who is in a contract year, is still a long shot to be traded, but that presents more of a chance than the Bears had going into today.
"Sources: The Chargers have been more receptive to trading players over the last 24 hours," Schultz wrote. "Khalil Mack is still considered a long shot, but other expiring contract players are available if the offer makes sense."
A few weeks ago, it was reported that the Bears had called Los Angeles about Mack , which was the first sign they had interest in him.
However, reports have suggested for weeks now that the Chargers weren't interested in selling, even amid a horrific campaign that now has Los Angeles sitting at 0-8.
Los Angeles had also stated publicly that they didn't want to trade Mack, and the future Hall of Famer also noted that he wanted to remain with the Chargers .
"Yeah, they know how I feel, man," Mack said when asked if he told the Chargers he wants to stay. "It's just tough with all the outside noise. And so, ultimately I want to be here and I want to help them win. Even though it's tough right now, you always see the light at the end of the tunnel."
“I want Khalil Mack here. Khalil Mack wants to be here. He’s one of the pillars of our team," head coach Jim Harbaugh said .
But clearly something has changed, at least when it comes to the Chargers' willingness to make a trade, and perhaps Mack will be changing his stance in the waning hours, also.
It isn't clear if the Bears ever had a legit offer on the table for Mack, but if they did, perhaps sweetening it a bit will be enough to entice the Chargers to let him go, assuming Mack is down to be traded.
That said, if Mack doesn't want to be moved, the Chargers are almost certainly going to oblige because of the immense amount of respect they have for him.
The Bears are reportedly in the market for a cornerback and the Chargers have a veteran cornerback who is on an expiring deal.
That is Donte Jackson, who is set to be a free agent in 2027.
Jackson isn't having a good season by any stretch, but he could offer some depth for Chicago during a season in which Jaylon Johnson has seen massive struggles .
For the cheap price it would cost to acquire Jackson (probably a late Day 3 pick), it might be worth it to take a swing on him for insurance behind Johnson.

title: Ben Johnson Shares Thoughts on Chicago Bears NFL Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
To trade or not to trade? That is the question the Chicago Bears and their fans are asking on Tuesday.
As of 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 10, trades will no longer be possible, so the clock is ticking on the Bears' ability to make another move.
The Bears have already made their all-in addition with the trade for Jeffery Simmons, but reports suggest they are still in the market for a cornerback .
Edge rusher has been another position Chicago has been linked to possibly adding at .
When asked about what the team could do on Tuesday, head coach Ben Johnson wasn't ruling out another deal or two happening.
However, he also noted that he believes the team has enough as is to be just fine the rest of the season.
"I think Ryan (Poles) is doing a phenomenal job every day. He’s going through and seeing how we can improve this roster, what we need the most of," Johnson said, per ESPN's Courtney Cronin .
"The coordinators are certainly talking every day right now, just with where their concerns lie within the roster. So we’ll see. We’ll see if there is another move or two to be made or if we stand put. I feel really confident about the guys we have in this locker room right now. And I think we’ve proven at this point that we can find a way to win each and every week with this group," he added.
While a lot of times you can't take what a coach says at face value when it comes to how he views his roster, we can do so here with Johnson.
That's because the Bears already looked like a true contender before the Simmons trade, and they are in even better shape following that blockbuster deal.
That said, general manager Ryan Poles' actions show us that this team is no doubt all-in, so it certainly wouldn't be at all surprising for the Bears to make another deal or even two before 4 p.m.
We already mentioned cornerback and edge rusher.
The Bears could use more depth at both spots, and especially at cornerback, where the team needs an insurance policy for the struggling Jaylon Johnson .
Chicago is in pretty good shape along the edge as long as Dayo Odeyingbo can get back from injured reserve in due time.
Another position to keep an eye on is tight end after Chicago lost its No. 2 tight end, Cole Kmet, to a season-ending knee injury.
The Bears deploy multiple tight ends sets more than the vast majority of teams in the NFL, so having a deep room is key.
Right now, it's hard to say the Bears have that behind Colston Loveland, as rookie Sam Roush has had issues and Stephen Carlson doesn't offer much outside of blocking.
After all of the rumors and speculation, we'll finally have answers by 4 p.m. ET today.

title: Trades Chicago Bears Might Make Today and Chances the Deals Will Happen
full_text:
The Bears were linked to interest in Mack by FOX Sports' Jay Glazer a few weeks back, which makes sense because Chicago could use more depth at edge rusher.
Unfortunately for the Bears and their fans, it doesn't look like a reunion is likely.
The Chargers have said publicly they don't want to trade Mack, and Mack has said he doesn't want to be traded. Adding to that, reports suggest the Chargers and Mack aren't lying .
"Despite their 0-7 record, the Los Angeles Chargers continue to tell teams that they have no interest in trading away Khalil Mack, and the veteran pass rusher will not be going anywhere before Tuesday's deadline, according to sources," ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported.
There's a few reasons why we're holding out hope. One of them has to do with the fact that this could simply be posturing on the Chargers' part in order to try and get more for Mack.
It also makes no sense for both sides to stay together. Mack may very well be in the final year of his career after mulling retirement in the past and it's hard to fathom him staying with an 0-8 team going nowhere. The Chargers would be better served moving on and picking up a draft pick.
The Bears could use another starting-caliber player at cornerback given the struggles of Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson this season. At the very least, more depth is needed.
Woolen is a great fit because he thrives in man coverage, which the Bears play at the second-highest rate in the NFL this season, and Woolen has plenty of starting and even playoff experience, and has been better than Johnson in 2026.
The Philadelphia Eagles showed they are ready to sell after trading Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars, and it makes sense to deal Woolen, also, as he'll be a free agent in 2027.
Cost will be important here, but with Woolen's price likely being a fourth-round pick, at most, we could see the Bears making this trade.
Wright left for the New York Jets in free agency and that proved to be a colossal mistake for the veteran cornerback.
Wright has not played a single snap on defense this season and has routinely been a healthy scratch. Safe to say, Wright likely wouldn't mind getting out of there and Gang Green probably wouldn't be opposed to trading him, either.
Wright started in 16 games for the Bears last season and was pretty solid. He also proved to be a turnover matchine after notching five picks.
There wouldn't be much of an acclimation period, either, thanks to Wright's experience in Dennis Allen's defense. He will also be dirt cheap, which only adds to the likelihood the Bears will at least have interest in him.
After losing Cole Kmet to a season-ending injury , the Bears, who use a lot of 12 and 13 personnel, are relying heavily on rookie Sam Roush, who has struggled this season, and uninspiring veteran Stephen Carlson behind Colston Loveland.
The Bears could use a well-rounded tight end like Goedert, who has proven to be a solid blocker and very good pass-catcher during his career.
The rules for why the Eagles would trade Woolen apply for Goedert, although the latter obviously has a deeper connection with the Eagles because he has spent his entire career there.
At a reasonable price of a fourth- or fifth-round pick, it wouldn't shock us to see the Bears trade for Goedert, although we don't believe it's likely, either, since the Bears have bigger fish to fry.
Here's a more realistic option for the Bears at tight end.
Alie-Cox doesn't offer as much in the pass-catching department as Goedert, but he's serviceable in that area and is as good, if not better, as a blocker. Alie-Cox will come cheaper than Goedert, also, with it likely costing a sixth-round pick, at most.
The Indianapolis Colts are in the midst of a fire sale after trading off Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, so everyone is on the table right now, and especially when it comes to players who are slated to be free agents like Alie-Cox is.
If the Bears do come away with a tight end on Tuesday, look for it to be Alie-Cox, or someone like him.

title: Bears Trade Deadline Tracker: Every Rumor and Reported Move for Chicago
full_text:
One of the biggest days of the NFL calendar is here for the Chicago Bears, as it's officially trade deadline day.
The NFL trade deadline will hit at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, and after that there will be one less avenue for teams to improve their rosters for the rest of the season.
Of course, the Bears have already made one of the biggest trades in the NFL in recent years when they acquired superstar defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons on Oct. 29. Since then, Simmons has proven to be a massive difference-maker for the Bears.
Now, the Bears will turn their focus to seeing if they can improve in any other areas of the team before the deadline passes.
Follow our tracker below for all of the latest reported rumors and acquisitions the Bears make on Tuesday. We've also included the Bears' biggest needs beneath that.
Chargers more receptive to trade, Mack still a long shot
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the Chargers have changed their stance when it comes to being open to selling players.
However, Schultz adds that a Khalil Mack trade remains a long shot.
"Sources: The Chargers  have been more receptive to trading players over the last 24 hours," Schultz said. "Khalil Mack is still considered a long shot, but other expiring contract players are available if the offer makes sense."
Hey, the Bears at least have a better chance to land Mack than they did 24 hours ago, so there's that.
Bears looking for a cornerback
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the Bears are in the market for a cornerback before the deadline.
"Chicago would love to add to their secondary with a corner," Schultz reported on Monday.
Chargers won't trade Khalil Mack
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , the Chargers are not going to trade Khalil Mack.
"Despite their 0-7 record, the Los Angeles Chargers continue to tell teams that they have no interest in trading Khalil Mack, and the veteran pass rusher will not be going anywhere before Tuesday's deadline, according to sources," Schefter and Rapoport said.
The Bears had been linked to interest in Mack , but it appears the dream reunion is not going to happen.
Bears trade for Jeffery Simmons: The Bears sent two first-round picks and a fourth-rounder to the Tennessee Titans for Simmons and a fifth-round pick. The trade was historic , as he's the first defensive tackle since 1967 to be acquired for multiple first-rounders.
Cornerback: While rookie Malik Muhammad has been excellent, Jaylon Johnson has struggled on the other side and the Bears can't depend on Tyrique Stevenson to replace him. At the very least, the Bears need another depth option for the boundary.
Edge Rusher: The Bears don't have a dire need here as long as Dayo Odeyingbo gets back from injury soon. Even if he isn't out much longer (Odeyingbo is eligible to return in Week 11), more depth certainly wouldn't hurt.
Tight end: The season-ending injury to Cole Kmet has left the Bears depending on rookie Sam Roush as their TE2 and veteran Stephen Carlson as the TE3 behind Colston Loveland. Roush has struggled this season and Carlson doesn't offer much as a pass-catcher. The Bears use a lot of 12 and 13 personnel, so they could use a well-rounded tight end.
Safety: With Dillon Thieneman, Cam Lewis and Elijah Hicks, the Bears are in pretty good shape here, and that will be especially true if Coby Bryant gets back late in the season. If anything, Chicago could use another depth piece.

title: Jonah Jackson Defends Jeffery Simmons Against Bucs OL's Accusations After Bears' Win
full_text:
Following the Chicago Bears' Week 9 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, offensive lineman Luke Goedeke lobbed a few accusations at defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons.
Goedeke accused Simmons of holding offensive linemen to help his defensive end, and then the Bucs veteran accused Simmons of launching himself at Bucs players and even taking a cheap shot at his head, according to ESPN's Kalyn Kahler .
"I mean, you're holding me on one, you came right at my head," he said. "I mean, that's always fun. He's known for it in pass pro, just holding the tackle so that the DE can run free, so I got that twice."
"There's no reason to come out on a TE and just drill a tackle on the side of the head," he added.
Simmons has not yet publicly responded to Goedeke's claims, but one of his teammates have.
When asked about Goedeke's accusations, at least when it comes to Simmons launching himself and holding offensive linemen, Bears guard Jonah Jackson said none of that is unusual.
In fact, he said Bucs defenders were launching themselves at Bears offensive linemen during the same game.
"The guys on his team tried to launch themselves at us I think every play," he said on 104.3 The Score on Monday. "I don't know any different. That's on him how he feels. It is what it is. This is football. Especially in the trenches, it gets rough and rowdy."
"They all do it," Jackson said when it comes to holding. "It is what it is. You've gotta find ways to combat it."
Goedeke had told Kahler that he "occasionally" sees guys doing what Simmons does in terms of the holding and launching, but clearly Jackson would beg to differ, especially as it pertains to Buccaneers defenders who are apparently doing the same.
Is Goedeke going to go to his teammates and tell them to stop doing that? Not likely.
And let's not pretend that Goedeke is some angel, either.
Here's a two-play sequence that first saw Simmons toss the Bucs lineman like a ragdoll before Goedeke retaliated with a cheap block in the back on the next snap.
1) Jeffery Simmons sent Luke Goedeke flying. 2) Next play, Goedeke tosses Simmons to the turf. It's getting chippy at Soldier Field! pic.twitter.com/yoZvqtqqg4
What this all adds up to is Goedeke is frustrated that his team lost and Simmons got the better of him.
There is no other explanation for Goedeke acting like what Simmons was doing is unusual because clearly it isn't.

title: Bears' Trade For Jeffery Simmons Looks Like a Landslide Win After Jordan Davis Trade
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' decision to trade for Jeffery Simmons set a high bar for other teams looking to bolster their defensive interior ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.
The Bears are going all in, and they paid a premium to do so. They shipped two first-round picks and a fourth-round selection for the defensive game-wrecker and a fifth-round pick on October 29.
The Jacksonville Jaguars took a similar all-in approach on Monday. They made three trades to fortify their defense ahead of a hopeful playoff run, with the headliner (and blockbuster) being their decision to package a first- and second-round pick to Philadelphia for DT Jordan Davis.
With that trade, the defensive tackle trade market is officially set. It's also clear which team got more bang for their buck with their respective all-in move .
Chicago's decision to put their chips on Jeffery Simmons has already proven to be a shrewd move. He unlocked their defense as soon as he took the field , and he has 10 tackles, 2 sacks, and 2 pass deflections over his first two games donning the blue and orange.
Those 2 sacks are .5 more than Davis has this season. Those 2 sacks are more than a fifth of Davis' career sack production (9.5 career sacks in 73 career games). Now, we know they have different skill sets, and Davis is one of the league's premier space eaters. It's really not fair to compare their sack production in a funnel.
They're both defensive tackles who got dealt in the past ten days, though. It is fair to compare each trade in a funnel. Simmons is a do-it-all defensive game wrecker with 46.5 career sacks. He's a three-time All-Pro and four-time Pro Bowler. Simmons is the league's third-highest-paid defensive tackle ($35.276 million per year) and is widely considered to be the league's premier DT .
Jeffery Simmons is as advertised The Bears are the team to beat in the NFC pic.twitter.com/s0PZbj8LNQ
Meanwhile, Davis is a 336 lb. behemoth and sheer force against the run. He's coming off a career-best 2025 campaign, when he put up 4.5 sacks and 9 TFLs (the same number Simmons has right now, and a mark he's beaten in each of the past three seasons). The Eagles re-signed Davis to a three-year, $78 million deal this offseason, and his $26 million per year is tied for eighth at the position.
Davis is a great player, but he's not nearly as dominant as Chicago's new star defensive tackle. Nor is he as versatile. Even with Simmons being three years older (29 vs. 26), Davis just doesn't bring as much to the table.
The age difference will only become a factor if Simmons experiences a fall-off in his age-32 campaign in 2029 (he's technically signed through 2030, but the Bears wouldn't owe him any dead money at that point). They also play a position featuring countless players who thrive into their mid-to-late 30s.
If Simmons is worth two first-round selections and a mid-round pick swap, then Davis should've been dealt for a first- and fourth-round selection. A first- and fifth-round pick also would've made more sense than Jacksonville giving up a first- and second-round pick. A two-round difference might not seem like much, but it is when teams value first- and second-round picks like gold. It's a substantial overpay.
Now, to the Jaguars' credit, the move will make perfect sense if they win a Super Bowl this season. It's also not like they were a threat to poach Simmons from their AFC South rivals.
They cemented themselves as serious contenders in the AFC amid the flurry of defensive trades they made on Monday. You also can't fault them for going all-in with a wide-open playoff picture.
Still, when comparing the two deals side by side, it's hard not to favor the Bears for taking a slightly bigger bite of the apple to land a true game-wrecker.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Baker Mayfield Calls Out Bears for Mimicking His Cadence, and Refs May Be Watching Next
full_text:
The Chicago Bears came away with a 27-24 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday night thanks in part to an incredible defensive performance.
An NFL team would need an incredible defensive performance to win when their offense turns the ball over five times. Needless to say, Caleb Williams' unit didn't hold up their end of the bargain after a fast start (they were up 14-0 after the first nine minutes).
Sure, the Buccaneers ran for 126 yards on the ground, but that was more than 40 fewer yards than they've averaged this season. It was also 106 fewer yards than they've averaged over the past month, as they've been downright unstoppable on the ground over the past few weeks.
Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield thinks the Bears used some cheap tactics along the way, though.
The Buccaneers committed eight penalties for 45 yards on Sunday night. Five of them were false starts by their usually composed (and recently dominant) offensive line. Still, that's common with teams playing on the road, especially in a stadium rocking as much as Soldier Field was last night.
Mayfield had a different take as to why those penalties occurred, though. He says Chicago's defense mimicking his cadence played a role.
"The last one [false start], I know they were barking out the cadence, which you can’t do that," Mayfield said. "It’s tough for the refs to call that because they’re not right there at the line of scrimmage. They called that on Tristan [Wirfs], but you can’t do that.”
That's a fair grievance. On the flip side, it's also a bit hilarious, especially since it worked. However, Mayfield calling it out could make the refs more mindful, so they'll have to be careful to avoid an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty going forward.
Mayfield wasn't the only Buccaneer who was eating sour grapes after the contest, either.
The Bears enjoyed a four-sack performance of Mayfield. They were awfully close to getting him down a few more times, and the defensive line deserves a world of credit for helping Chicago come out on top.
Jeffery Simmons had another strong showing, finishing the game with four tackles, a sack, and a pass deflection. Nevertheless, Buccaneers right tackle Luke Goedeke took issue with how he played the game when speaking to ESPN writer Kalyn Kahler.
"I mean, you're holding me one on one, you came right at my head," Goedeke said. "He's known for it on pass pro, just holding the tackle so that the DE can run free, so I got that twice. I mean, respect the guy, but some of the stuff he can really take out of his game. It's just kind of old, to be honest.
"There's no reason to come out on a TE and just drill a [offensive] tackle on the side of the head. It's really not a place in the game for that, to be honest with you... Most [defensive linemen] will at least play with their hands and no try to launch themselves at you."
Honestly, this is a bad look for Goedeke. I'm all for player safety, but he plays the most violent position in the world's most violent sport. Offensive and defensive linemen bang their heads into each other for 60 minutes every week.
Yet he's calling out Simmons for playing the same way every game-wrecking defensive lineman in the league does ? This is a situation where it feels fair to call it like it is. He got beat a few times by one of the league's best defensive linemen, and he's upset about it.
Yeah that was nasty. https://t.co/Nt5Po4QP6K pic.twitter.com/voW0IKaAKu
I don't know if the play above is the one Goedeke is referencing when speaking to Kahler (Simmons wasn't lined up over a TE), but it seems similar to his grievance. It sounds like he's upset Simmons took him with a stunt (which is designed to get a free rusher at the quarterback by having DEs and DTs rotate their assignment at the snap).
Notably, stunts are a common practice across the league. I've never heard an offensive lineman complain about them before, because that's a silly thing to do. While Mayfield's criticism was fair, it's much harder to defend Goedeke's comments about Simmons.

Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Chicago Bears Report Card for Week 9 Win: A Successful Salvage
full_text:
Ben Johnson wanted to point to one real positive Sunday night after the Bears nearly squandered a game they should have put away in the second quarter.
"Despite the displeasure I might be presenting right now, there's a lot of good in terms of building this team that comes from a win like this," Johnson said. 'Like I said, one, it's hard to win under those circumstances. But to your point, we really haven't been in that situation in the fourth quarter with little time left, needing a field goal, touchdown, whatever it is.
"It just hasn't happened a whole lot this year. And yet I feel like our guys, we are prepped for that and we're ready for it."
It's a good thing they showed they still had this in their back pockets.
If the Bears continue playing the way they did Sunday night, they're going to be facing a lot of future deficits and will need those late-game Caleb Williams comebacks.
Bust: #Bears WR Rome Odunze can’t catch this. pic.twitter.com/3YSepVRW68
Finishing before the break with a 7-2 record was essential in an NFC North where every team must win every week to keep from losing ground.
At least the Bears managed to do this, even if their performance inspired little confidence about the remaining eight games.
Here are the grades from possibly the ugliest victory of Johnson's time as head coach.
CAIRO SANTOS WINS IT FOR THE BEARS ‼️ pic.twitter.com/k526FOfdkj
Giving a failed grade would be easy but they did enough in the first quarter with a perfectly executed 56-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden III and the 9-yard TD to Rome Odunze, and later with the 38-yard pass to Colston Loveland to salvage something. In between, QB decision making and passing were poor, there were jailbreaks from the line and Odunze bobbled away a chance to secure a wide-open TD at the back of the end zone. The optimal grade for any offense with four interceptions should be a C. The Bears only got that because of the late drive for the winning points.
Game on the line, I TRUST THE ICEMAN #Bears pic.twitter.com/dhOXmWNQhp
A season-low 72 yards and only 3.3 yards per carry would have been even worse if not for Williams scrambling for 16 yards. Salvon Ahmed's 5.0 yards per carry on five rushes kept this from descending into "F" territory. D'Andre Swift obviously needs a rest because of some type of unreported injury situation because he averaged 2.6 yards again for the second straight game. He failed to reach 100 yards for the eighth straight game and to average more than 3.5 yards for the fourth straight game. The running game needs balance from Kyle Monangai's power back badly, but their anemic rushing totals by backs says there could be something more needed from the blocking as well.
A familiar theme for the defense has been to allow a few longer runs that bolstered opponents' numbers but failed to really dent the game. Bucky Irving came up 3 yards short of 100 but no one could say he had a huge impact. The Bears can't get outrushed 126-72 in games and stay competitive, though. The overall goal is to force opponents into passing situations on third down and their front succeeded at this. Linebacker Devin Bush again recorded a strong game with nine tackles, including one of their four for loss.
JAYLON JOHNSON HOUSE CALL ☎️ 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/FVkfIjPwvQ
Jaylon Johnson saved the day with his 67-yard interception return, aided by Montez Sweat's block on Baker Mayfield. They had their share of failures, like the 58-yard completion allowed to Tez Johnson and the 44-yarder after a Mayfield scramble to Kenneth Gainwell. The pass rush and coverage failed on that broken play. However, the rush consistently got after Mayfield with four sacks and the two interceptions not only prevented points but added to the team total. A 2-for-12 game on third down by Tampa Bay let the Bears come away with the chance to win at the end.
Reports confirm that Bears Luther Burden III suffered a concussion on this hit. Never should've been in doubt. Textbook sign "no protective action when falling" A conscious man tries to fall palms down. The backs of his hands hit first, which breaks wrists pic.twitter.com/NjVVoB3mmh
Zavion Thomas' 92-yard touchdown return got wiped out by a terrible phantom holding call or the Bears might have been so far ahead in the first half that the Bucs never could have been close, even with five takeaways. Cairo Santos' seventh game-winning field goal as a Bear wasn't long at 38 yards, but once again he delivered when it mattered and there have been plenty of NFL instances of kickers missing in the clutch this season. In between successes were a poor knuckle kickoff by Santos to give Tampa Bay the ball at the 40; a deflected Tory Taylor punt; Kalif Raymond's muffed attempt to field a punt, with disaster averted by his recovery. Raymond did make a 26-yard punt return and Thomas averaged 29.3 on three kick returns, while the coverage units had another outstanding night with four kicks covered at a 23.0-yard average and no punt return yards for Taylor punts.
Zavion Thomas ran the kick return 90 yards for a touchdown, but it was wiped off the board due to a holding penalty 🤔 Did the refs get the call right? pic.twitter.com/yoAAB021ik
Johnson can't actually come onto the field and throw the ball out of bounds for Williams. He can only tell him what to do. The Bears are obviously facing issues running the ball or blocking the run and Johnson's play calling reflected this with only 17 run calls for backs. Dennis Allen's ability to scheme up the right call with rather exotic coverage or rush looks was huge over the first three quarters. Not many teams can hold it together when the offense is turning it over five times, and the Bears won a game for the first time since 2006 when they did this -- they also won one that year when they turned it over six times. That was the "they are who we thought they were" game.
Winning ugly sure beats losing ugly. Their defense and Santos prevented something totally unsightly. Johnson tends to use bye weeks to make lineup changes he deems necessary. He did this last year. Will any be coming?
Caleb Williams with the hat trick against the Bucs. 1….2…3 interceptions in the first half. pic.twitter.com/4Rse5ovRjv
