title: Winners and Losers: Jordan Love Makes Case for MVP as Packers Rout Patriots
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers could not have drawn up a better start as they were on the road against the New England Patriots. Drake Maye threw an interception to Xavier McKinney on the second play from scrimmage. Two plays later, Jordan Love ran for a touchdown that made the score 7-0. That score would go as high as 17-0 in the first half.
The second half started with Love hitting a couple big plays to Christian Watson leading to a touchdown to Savion Williams.
Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns. His top two receivers both went for over 160. The safety duo picked off Drake Maye three times.
The story of the game is the passing game on both sides.
That leads off our weekly list of winners and losers.
Jordan Love has been asked to carry Green Bay’s entire offense all season long. They can’t run the ball. They can’t protect him. His receivers lead the league in drops.
None of it has mattered as Love came into Sunday’s game leading the league in passing yards. Playing in the same stadium as the best quarterback to ever play, Love was the best quarterback on the field.
He diced up New England’s defense essentially regardless of what the Patriots threw at him. He was under pressure a bunch. Didn’t matter.
JORDAN LOVE WAS BORN TO BALL 362 PASS YARDS 3 PASS TD 154.5 PASS RATING pic.twitter.com/bp55moIQUl
His run game still showed no life until late in the game. Didn’t matter.
The Patriots’ defense is really good at taking away explosive plays. That didn’t matter either. Love threw for 372 yards. He may have gone over 400 if he did not take a seat for the last nine minutes of play.
He threw a touchdown pass to Golden and Savion Williams, and ran for another. There’s no such thing as an MVP candidate until the calendar turns to December. If such a list were to exist, however, Love would be on it. He’s been that good.
Jordan Love against the blitz vs Patriots 10/11 146 Pass Yards Pass TD 149.1 Pass Rating pic.twitter.com/VFboo8DsNA
How good is Evan Williams? The Packers’ safety is starting to get some national recognition. Tom Brady was gushing about Williams during the game, and Williams put on a show.
He had an acrobatic interception early in the game with some fancy footwork off a tipped pass by his teammate Brandon Cisse.
He was deployed all over the formation and in the face of Drake Maye early and often when Jonathan Gannon would send him on pressures.
As well as his teammate Xavier McKinney has played, Williams has been better.
One cool tidbit: Williams’ mother used to babysit Brady when Brady was a child.
Christian Watson and Matthew Golden carry Green Bay’s passing game. The thought coming into the week was that Christian Gonzalez could be a formidable challenge to help eliminate at least one of those players from the equation to some degree.
That was a foolish thought. Both receivers torched Gonzalez and defensive backs not named Gonzalez. Watson and Golden both went well over 150 yards. They both scored a touchdown, with Golden getting the honors of catching the 100th touchdown pass of Love’s career.
JORDAN LOVE CHRISTIAN WATSON PACKERS ARE DOMINATING GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hxEPzs2KdC
It’s not as if the rest of the league doesn’t know what Green Bay’s plan is on offense. Watson is going to surpass 1,000 yards for the first time of his career if he stays on the field. Golden might join him as well. That would make Watson and Golden the first duo of receivers to top 1,000 yards in Green Bay since Randall Cobb and Jordy Nelson.
They are on pace to finish with 3,139 receiving yards.
Christian Watson and Matthew Golden vs Patriots 17 receptions 335 rec yards 2 TD Best WR duo in NFL? pic.twitter.com/VQtqRDep5e
Xavier McKinney’s first season in Green Bay felt like he caught an interception every week. Last season, the interceptions dried up, but the Packers insisted that McKinney was still playing as well as he did in 2024 when he was a First-Team All Pro.
Sunday, McKinney picked off Drake Maye twice, including one on Maye’s first pass of the game. Those were McKinney’s fourth and fifth interceptions of the season, which more than doubled his total from a season ago.
Xavier McKinney jumps the route for his 2nd INT of the half! GBvsNE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3YxfSAtIvC
The Packers’ secondary is excellent, specifically at safety. McKinney is the leader, and keeps this group lined up correctly. Now, he’s making the big plays too.
Do the Packers have a running back? That’s probably a stretch at this point, but Kaleb Johnson emerged from Matt LaFleur’s doghouse and into the lineup out of necessity. Marshawn Lloyd was inactive. Josh Jacobs left the game early with a hand injury.
Johnson has looked good in his limited sample size during the season, he just had a fumbling problem that kept him on the bench.
Johnson’s first eight carries went for 56 yards. That made him the first individual rusher to go over 50 yards in a game this season.
Johnson may not be special, but he hits the hole with authority and runs downhill. Maybe that’s what the Packers need?
Even if Jacobs is ready to play next week, Johnson needs to get some run as his primary backup.
Josh Jacobs has been out of the lineup for reasons outside of an injury. Sunday was his third game back in the lineup, and it did not last long. Jacobs took a pitch in the red zone on the Packers’ second scoring drive and stuck his hand in the facemask of a Patriot defender. The result was a hand injury that knocked him out for the rest of the first half.
Josh Jacobs got his right hand caught in the defenders face mask. I’m curious if it’s his hand or his fingers. It almost looks like one of his fingers snaps. pic.twitter.com/hngCa0PdG6
Jacobs also fumbled on the play, but the ball went out of bounds which helped the Packers avert disaster. With the trade deadline looming, running back is at the top of Green Bay’s potential shopping list. If Jacobs has to miss time or is limited, would Brian Gutekunst be more apt to find his replacement?
Meanwhile, with Jacobs on the bench, Kaleb Johnson found some traction in the run game. It’s a small sample and obviously Jacobs is a more accomplished player than Johnson, but Johnson looked better today than anyone has all season.
Aaron Banks bounced in and out of the lineup again with a knee injury that has bothered him all season long. When he was in the game, he struggled mightily. He was credited with giving up three pressures, one sack, a quarterback hit, and a hurry in the first half from PFF.
He was beaten badly on a Josh Jacobs run that lost yardage as well.
Despite his struggles, he continues to start when he is healthy enough to play, and that included the second half of Sunday’s game. The play didn’t get any better. Banks is slow out of his stance. When he’s beaten, he’s beaten easily.
He was either injured or benched in the second half when Kevin Zeitler replaced him late in the third quarter at right guard with Laken Tomlinson sliding into Banks’ spot.
Maybe the Packers liked the idea of Aaron Banks when they signed him, but it’s pretty clear he’s not the player they envisioned. With his injury history, it’s fair to wonder if he ever will be.
New England’s first scoring drive came when Nick Niemann was pressed into a spot he had not been at for most of his career in Green Bay. Niemann is Green Bay’s fifth preferred linebacker, but had to see action due to a chest injury for Ty’Ron Hopper.
Niemann was caught flat-footed on a pass that was intended for Rhamondre Stevenson. Stevenson ran by Niemann with relative ease and was hauled in the pass from Maye to give the Patriots their first touchdown of the day.
Valentine was in competition to start this offseason at cornerback, and there was some thought he might get the nod because of his ability in coverage.

title: Every RB Texans Can Potentially Land at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Houston Texans are just hours out from the NFL trade deadline–– and nobody knows which direction this team is going to go .
One area on the roster that has been circled as a potential position of interest for the Texans has been running back.
According to Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer, Houston has been among the teams checking in on "available" running backs around the league before the deadline, along with safeties.
As to who the Texans might have their eyes on is a bit of an unknown. However, when surveying around the league, there are several running backs that could stick out as guys that are potentially available, fill a need on the roster, and within reason for Houston to go out and add for the right price.
So let's do some digging. Which running backs around the league could the Texans truly go out and make a move for?
Let's look at 10 different names at the position around the league to keep an eye on––tiering them as either veteran depth pieces, high-value starters, and longshots that probably aren't on their way to Houston anytime soon:
This would be the range of outcomes to expect for the Texans: not an upgrade that really shakes up the top of the depth chart, but one that could provide some much-needed depth behind the current running back room that's been both shallow and dealing with injuries over the past few weeks.
Each of these guys feels unlikely to claim more than a day three pick in exchange for their services on the trade market. And for the Texans, that's a price tag they could be willing to pay in order to add some much-needed security at running back for a run game that's been stuck in the bottom half of the NFL all season.
The one name I'd keep the closest watch on here is Devin Singletary of the Giants; a veteran runner who would cost minimal assets to acquire, has been in Houston before, and could be the right caliber of back to slot behind Woody Marks and David Montgomery as a reliable RB3 who can produce on the ground and through the air in a pinch.
These two feel like they could be grouped within the next category: they haven't been included in many trade rumors leading up to the deadline, and in all likelihood, probably won't be on the move to the Texans anytime soon.
However, the idea of the Texans pursuing either is at least fun to consider.
Breece Hall was briefly rumored as a Houston target this past offseason as a potential addition to an expansive roster of Iowa State alums, while Ashton Jeanty presents a similar situation to Marvin Harrison Jr., where the front office takes a chance on a young talent who hasn't performed up to expectations in the spot he was drafted.
When stacking up the price tag of each (likely to cost at least a day or two to pick), along with the lack of clear desire or aggressiveness from either team to make a move on these backs, don't hold your breath on the Texans striking on a trade here.
But maybe once the offseason arrives, and the situation continues to look as it does for both running backs, then perhaps the Texans' interest could shift in a different direction––if their backfield dilemma is still in a similar spot.
Here are the big names at running back that everyone's talking about at the deadline: Jonathan Taylor, Saquon Barkley, and Derrick Henry.
Each would be due to command some serious interest in the market if their respective teams decided to aggressively shop them. And for a running-back-needy team like the Texans, they make sense as a suitor that should keep all three at least on the radar leading up to the deadline.
But the realism behind a move for any of these three–– at least from Houston's perspective–– feels pretty out there with just a few hours to go until the buzzer sounds.
For one, there's the cost that each would be due to land from any team interested in acquiring them: a first-round pick appears to be the going rate.
Maybe the Texans would be interested in paying that given their Super Bowl aspirations, but that's still a pretty steep price for an older running back with many miles on the odometer.
But Barkley and Henry have also both been informed by their teams that they won't be traded ahead of the deadline. That creates an even stronger hurdle for Houston to overcome. Taylor might be a different story, but it'd be really hard to expect the Colts to ship out their franchise running back to a division rival like the Texans, even if the package in return was an ideal one.
So if the Texans were to make an addition at running back at the deadline, expect the scale to be a bit smaller than these guys. These top-tier stars might just be out of reach, and if they weren't, their price tag might be a little too steep for Houston's desires.

title: Texans Must Consider a Last-Minute Splash for This Trade Candidate
full_text:
The Houston Texans are right around the corner from the NFL trade deadline–– and there hasn't been a whole lot of chatter surrounding how this team could approach the coming hours .
Some argue the Texans should stand pat with their current group. They're coming off a win building momentum for the second half of the season with an already-talented roster, and investing in another addition to the roster might not be exactly necessary.
Or, there's the argument that the Texans could hit the market as buyers.
After all, this roster isn't perfect, and following their AFC South rival, the Jacksonville Jaguars, peppering the market with multiple moves on Monday , that might add even more incentive for Houston to get aggressive and make a push to make a tweak before the next nine games on the schedule.
But what might the Texans' most splashy move on the trade market be, within reason?
It's hard to really expect the Texans to go out and trade away multiple first-round picks for a superstar talent at this point. And especially for a big move surrounding someone like Jonathan Taylor, who sits right across from them in the AFC South, Houston making a move for his services might be a bit wishful thinking .
But there is one starting-level, acquireable trade candidate that the Texans should have their eyes on leading up to the deadline: someone that could provide an immediate impact for the offense, fills a position of need, and has Super Bowl pedigree that Houston would be sure to love adding as well.
That's none other than Philadelphia Eagles offensive lineman Landon Dickerson, who makes too much sense as a Texans trade target to at least consider in the time before the deadline buzzer sounds.
Now, when looking at the Eagles' perspective of why a Dickerson deal makes sense, it's not too tough to sort through.
Philadelphia is taking a step back by making multiple selling moves by already sending away guys like Jordan Davis and Cam Jurgens. Dickerson fits the mold as a valuable, starting offensive guard who can also net future value for their upcoming retool. That part adds up.
And when surveying around the market, the Texans might just be an ideal trade partner for the Eagles to look towards.
Their offensive line has been steadily improving throughout the season, but could still use further stability with a talented guard like Dickerson; someone who's strong and physically gifted at the position with experience and versatility to play multiple positions.
This season, Dickerson hasn't performed quite as well as he has in years past. PFF places him with the 55th-best overall grade among 77 eligible guards (55.5), along with ranking bottom 10 in pass-blocking grade.
However, perhaps in a new situation out of the Eagles, like in Houston–– a team that seems to be trending up rather than down for the next several weeks–– maybe that could rejuvenate Dickerson to be the high-end guard that he had been during Philadelphia's Super Bowl runs.
The Texans, or any other team that were interested in acquiring him, would be due to only pay him $607,500 in the remaining 2026 salary, but would then be forced to pay upwards of $20 million in each of 2027 and 2028.
Short-term, the costs wouldn't be hard to stomach whatsoever, but could become a bit more challenging after the season. And if anything, that could be what holds the Texans back from pulling the trigger on such a move.
In terms of draft compensation, it's hard to imagine the Eagles being able to net more than a day-two pick in exchange for Dickerson when combining his recent play, injury concerns, and contract implications. And for a Texans team that just gave up a second-round pick for Marvin Harrison Jr. , any more than a third to give up for Dickerson might feel too rich.
But that type of investment might need to be one that the Texans consider in an effort to take their roster another step forward for the second half of the season.
The Jaguars just went out to add a stout defensive tackle from the Eagles that could be due to give the Texans trouble down the line, and maybe adding Dickerson on the line upfront is the best way to counter that.
He can fill in at left guard, allows rookie Keylan Rutledge to shift to the center spot, and gives the Texans a really respectable three-man interior to move forward with for the rest of the season.
The ball is in the Texans' court. Time will tell if they wind up pulling the trigger on a big move like this or similar, or if they instead decide to play it safe without a move at the buzzer.

title: How Jalen Pitre Helped Texans Defense Find Its Identity vs. Chargers
full_text:
After an up-and-down first seven games on the season, the Houston Texans' defense finally looked closer to their elite form in Week 9 against the LA Chargers en route to their dominating 44-22 victory in SoFi Stadium .
Everything was clicking for the Texans' defense compared to some of their recent performances. They got to Justin Herbert for a season-high eight sacks , which led to him completing just 50% of his passes, forced two turnovers, and held the Chargers' offense to less than 325 total yards on the day.
So what changed for the Texans this week? Why was their defense finally able to turn a corner for a solid day of production when stacked up against some of their latest disappointments?
In DeMeco Ryans' mind, a lot of the credit falls on the shoulders of Jalen Pitre.
Pitre, who had been out of the Texans' lineup since suffering an AC joint sprain in Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans, had finally made a return to the defensive side of the ball as Houston's versatile nickelback against the Chargers.
And Pitre really wasted no time making his regular impact. He ranked second on the team for combined tackles on the day with six, with two of those coming as tackles for loss.
DeMeco Ryans spoke the day after the win over the Chargers about the defense's overall performance from the weekend, and unpromptedly spoke about why Pitre's return to the Texans' defense was so valuable on Sunday.
"The defense definitely executed much better when it came down to, specifically, the tackling piece of it," Ryans said. "I thought our guys really tackled well. I thought having Pitre back was really the highlight for me."
"The plays that he's able to make; it really energizes our entire team. Like, the physicality he plays with. Him blitzing off of the edge, making plays in the backfield, really making it hard on opponents, because of his playstyle and where he's aligning all over the field."
It's hard to argue with Ryans. A lot of what the Texans had been missing on their defense over the past several weeks are traits that Pitre himself brings to the table: tackling, consistency, and versatility in the secondary, and hard-hitting bravado.
And that's exactly what he was able to chip in for on Sunday, turning out to be one of the bigger stars on the Texans' defense entirely, and helping Houston's stock on that side of the ball take a much-needed turn in the right direction.
When Pitre is on the field with this Texans' secondary, while the likes of Derek Stingley and Kamari Lassiter are also playing up to their All-Pro and Pro Bowl standards, paired with a commanding pass rush, it quickly becomes tough to attack this defense altogether.
That was exactly the case for the Texans this Sunday, and helped them get back on track with their third victory on the season. And if Pitre is able to lead the way for similar success from this talented Houston defense moving forward, there are due to be a few more wins to follow.

title: Where the Texans Stand 24 Hours Before the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Houston Texans are now less than 24 hours away from reaching the NFL trade deadline.
And to this point, how the Texans might approach their plans in the coming hours is still largely undetermined.
Coming off a Week 9 win at 3-5 and looking to continue building momentum for the second half of their season, there's a chance that Houston goes searching around the trade market in hopes that they can improve this roster from its current state.
There's also a world that the Texans decide to stand pat and play things conservatively at the deadline if there isn't a deal on the table that the front office truly covets. Houston has already made a couple of trades over the past few months as is, so maybe this time of year winds up being a bit quieter than expected for the front office.
The ball is in the Texans' court right now. They've got until 3 p.m. CT on Tuesday afternoon to make any and all trades they may be interested in, and potentially put a finishing touch on this roster moving into the next portion of the regular season.
Let's sort through everything that matters surrounding the Texans' trade deadline situation, and what to look out for in the coming hours as teams begin to scramble looking for any final moves.
While the Texans have been watching from the sidelines on the trade market since their move to acquire Marvin Harrison Jr. , the surrounding AFC South has made no shortage of moves to either double down on their hopes of making a deep postseason run, or in the case of a couple of teams, take a step back and look towards the future.
The Jacksonville Jaguars just added a couple of defensive pieces as of Monday in Jessie Bates III and Davon Godchaux. The Tennessee Titans just shipped out All-Pro Jeffery Simmons as of last week. And the Indianapolis Colts could still be on track for a bit of a fire sale, having already sent out Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, and maybe Jonathan Taylor in due time.
So will that extra activity around the division influence the Texans to go out and make a move of their own? It's certainly possible knowing how much general manager Nick Caserio likes to make a trade every now and then. And it might not be the worst idea to hit the market for a deal either.
If they were persuaded to pull the trigger on something, it feels far more likely that Houston would hit the market as buyers rather than sellers, having just come off a Week 9 win to sit just two games back from .500.
The last we heard on the Texans' interests at the deadline, SI insider Albert Breer linked Houston to potentially target two positions : running back and safety.
Now, as to how significant in terms of scale the Texans are willing to upgrade each position remains to be seen. Maybe Houston goes out to add a star safety like their division rival Jaguars just did less than 48 hours out from the deadline, but having both positions on the radar does make sense.
The Texans' run game has started to look better over the past few weeks since David Montgomery has been out with a groin injury , but could still use another layer of depth and playmaking for the second half of the season.
Houston's safety unit has also dealt with underperformance and injury issues, with their latest concern centering around Reed Blankenship and his concussion/hand injury. So if the Texans felt they needed to find an upgrade at either spot on their roster, now might be the perfect time to address it.
The one name on the Texans' roster who had probably seen themselves in the most trade rumors over the past week was veteran edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney, who ESPN's Adam Schefter reported had been generating interest from teams leading up to the deadline during Houston's bye week.
But while the interest in Clowney might be there, it doesn't make much sense internally for the Texans to consider moving him.
Clowney fits a need on the Texans' defense, is on a flexible and affordable one-year contract, and comes fresh off potentially his best game of the season against the LA Chargers, where he was one of three players to end the day with two sacks. Simply put, Clowney is here to stay .

title: What Stood Out From Texans' Week 9 Snap Counts vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Houston Texans claimed a much-needed win over the LA Chargers in Week 9, commanding their way to a 44-22 blowout, that now puts this team back on track for a potential run in the second half of their schedule with the same record they had at this time last season.
And in the fallout from the Texans' Week 9 victory , we now have a glimpse of how the snap counts panned out for Houston within all three phases, giving us a picture of who played a bunch, and who didn't over the course of their West Coast road trip.
Let's take a look at how things shook out for the Texans and Chargers' snap counts for Week 9, and point out a few aspects that might be a bit notable from Houston's perspective:
For yet another week, the Texans showed that they weren't shy when it came to getting wide receiver Xavier Hutchinson on the field, as he saw a resounding 81% of Houston's total offensive snaps, which was even higher than Nico Collins’s snap share of 73%.
Hutchinson isn't the most dangerous downfield weapon for the Texans to keep on the field, but he is a positive blocker who contributes in the run game, while also providing a reliable set of hands who chipped in for three receptions, 29 yards, and a touchdown as of this weekend.
Another development that sticks out in the Texans' wide receiver room: both Tank Dell and Marvin Harrison Jr. were able to see the field noticeably more than before the bye. Neither eclipsed a 25% snap share in their latest showing against the New York Giants, to now seeing those opportunities doubled in Week 9.
Dell definitely turned in those added snaps for the better day, as he was one of two Texans pass-catchers to reach above 100 receiving yards. But to see both Dell and Harrison Jr. on the field and more involved in Houston's offensive game plan is a positive sign for what's ahead.
It only took four weeks of being a healthy scratch on the Texans' gameday roster, but second-round rookie tight end Marlin Klein finally got back on the field for Houston in Week 9 , where he got a chance to get some reps in a first-year campaign he's been largely limited in.
And it was in this game where Klein saw a season-high 19 offensive snaps with nine on special teams–– which is a significant step forward from how the Texans' usage panned out for him through the first seven weeks.
The only problem arises when factoring in Klein's zero recorded stats in those opportunities. Maybe he can show more in Week 10 against the Cleveland Browns.
The Texans made an underrated addition to their defensive line at the bye when they added recently-cut San Francisco 49ers defensive tackle Naquan Jones; a previous member of Houston's 90-man roster before the season started, and would be one of their toughest cuts heading into Week 1.
But the Texans got their hands back on Jones for the second half of the season. And against the Chargers, they wasted no time getting Jones involved as a rotational piece of their defensive line.
Jones landed just under 40% of Houston's defensive snaps, and was one of five defensive tackles to get at least 33% of the snap share. It was a heavy rotation for DeMeco Ryans' interior this weekend, but a strategy that proved to be effective.

title: Texans' Trade Deadline Plans Must Change After Jessie Bates Deal
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline right around the corner, the Houston Texans haven't found themselves at the center of many rumors linking them to a big splash acquisition.
After all, the Texans did just spend a second round pick to bring in wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. only a few weeks ago. Imagining Houston to pull the trigger on another major deal at the trade deadline to give up significant assets could be tough to imagine.
However, after the events of the latest NFL blockbuster to shake up the league––and perhaps more importantly, the AFC South––the Texans might be forced to have a different approach to this year's deadline.
That's because Houston's top threat within their own division, the Jacksonville Jaguars, just took a big swing to go out and land Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III in exchange for a second and a fifth-round pick.
Trade: Falcons are sending former Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick, sources tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/zsvYXRXj0P
Now, the Jaguars undoubtedly make a big investment here to upgrade a position of need in Bates. Especially knowing that Bates is in the final year of his contract and will be a free agent in 2027, that makes this move even more significant for Jacksonville.
But from Jacksonville's perspective, they're a team that feels well within reach of making a run to the Super Bowl out of the AFC.
Many teams around the league in a similar position have already made their big moves to push the chips in on a championship-level group––such as the Chicago Bears with Jeffery Simmons or the Seattle Seahawks with Quenton Nelson––and this seems to be the Jaguars' own version of just that.
Bates is an All-Pro level safety who can add an immediate upgrade to the Jaguars' secondary that's already performed relatively well through the first half of the season. If the investment pays off, Bates could be the one piece needed to take this current defense over the hump for that Super Bowl appearance.
For the Texans, however, such a move from the Jaguars should sound some alarms within the building: their top threat in the division just added an All-Pro defender, and they're one of many teams that Houston will have to go through in the AFC for a hopeful deep postseason run themselves. They even have to play them once more in the regular season come Week 15.
So with the trade deadline less than 48 hours away, might the Texans' front office consider a similar big move for their roster to try and keep up with their immediate competition? The idea certainly makes sense––especially if a star talent emerges on the market at the right price.
So now comes the Texans' time to evaluate opportunities on the market, see where starting-level talent might be available, and find a roster upgrade to acquire and keep up in an arms race of sorts with the Jaguars.
Where on the roster might the Texans target, and who could be available? Houston was rumored to add another running back or safety at the deadline last week, so perhaps those two positions could be ones to keep an eye on––even if one of the top safeties on the market has now made his way to a division rival.
Maybe Houston sends in some aggressive calls for Derrick Henry or Saquon Barkley , or even sends out similar offers to Jacksonville for a high-end safety that's available. Perhaps the front office goes with a surprising route of bolstering up their defensive interior.
But if no deadline move comes to form for the Texans, it'll be hard to have a ton of optimism that this group can not only make their resilient climb up the AFC as one of seven playoff teams, but also have the talent necessary to win multiple games on the road in the postseason.
For the Texans to truly move into the second half of the season with a confident, championship-caliber roster, taking a big deadline swing for another star might just do that. They'll have until 3 p.m. CT on Tuesday afternoon to make it happen.

title: Key Quotes From Texans' C.J. Stroud After Week 9 Win vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Houston Texans managed to find a much-needed win in their Week 9 road trip facing the LA Chargers on Sunday, as they'll be coming home with a commanding 44-22 victory that takes their record to a bit of a better-looking 3-5 through eight games.
The win was one that was made a whole lot easier thanks to the high-level play of Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud , who put together an impressive 384 passing yards with five passing touchdowns and an interception.
Stroud was poised in the pocket throughout the day, making excellent decisions and getting several pass-catchers involved, and thus helped lead the way for a big-time road win in the process .
Let's sort through a batch of notable quotes from Stroud following the game after he put together one of his best performances in recent memory back in his home state of California.
Q: One of your best friends, not only on this team but in life, is Tank Dell. What was it like for you to be able to connect with him like that, just like the old days?
"Yeah, it was great, man. I'm just super proud of him. He's been through a lot these last couple of years. Just the perseverance, the faith that he has in God and where God has him in life, and where God has put him through."
"I always tell him that God is never going to leave you or forsake you. He has you right where he needs you. He's working things out that you don't even know. For him to have that knowing, I think it's taken him very far."
"Just to see him get 100 yards in his second game back from a crazy injury, that's crazy. But for him, that's the type of confidence we have in Tank. He's a heck of a football player and showed it today."
Q: We're going to look at the stat sheet, and we're going to see the amount of yards that you threw for today and the amount of touchdowns. But can you just talk about your poise and perseverance in the pocket?
"They're a good defense. They've held a lot of teams out, especially in the first half. They were able to hold the Chiefs to a few points in the first half. The Rams, same thing. We knew that coming into the game."
"It really started with their front. I thought their D-line was really good. I thought our O-line, all the way from Tay to Keylan to Evan to Ed, all the way to Trent, did a great job all game."
"Even when it got a little rocky, they settled in and did a great job because it's hard to pass protect that many times and be 100 percent. I just appreciate them keeping the fight."
Q: You finally able to connect with Kayshon [Boutte]. How did that feel for you? Coach said that he finally got a pass where he could stand up and keep running.
"I know, I know. But no, he's a great football player. I try to tell him, 'Man, I know I miss you sometimes, but just trust me, I got your back. I want the best for you. I want to see you succeed in life and football.'
"Just to see him ball today was great. He's a football player, and I'm really glad he's on our team."
Q: Did you feel in the zone? What were you feeling throughout your game?
"To be honest with you, I was very sick this whole week. I don't know what I had, but I was not feeling good all week. I barely practiced on Thursday. My teammates really helped me. [Offensive assistant] Cole Weeks came and encouraged me during the week because I was really feeling bad and just wasn't feeling great."
"Even today, I woke up feeling not great. I don't know what I had. I had chills and all the things. To have that type of performance, even under the weather a little bit, was a testament to our team and our resilience."
"I'm grateful that God has allowed me to play this game even when I'm sick. I'm just really happy with what we were able to do coming off a bye week. We knocked off a little rust in that second drive, and from there we started to roll. It's a good start. We have a lot more work to do."
Q: A lot of quarterbacks, even the great ones, go a whole career without throwing five touchdowns. What's it like to have that kind of day?
"It's amazing. It's pretty cool, man. I beat myself up a lot when I don't do great. So, I'm going to enjoy this and celebrate with my friends, my family and my teammates. I know what it feels like to throw a couple of interceptions. So, you have to also be very positive toward yourself."
"I think that's something the quarterback position has taught me about life. Everybody can think one way, but it's about how you view yourself and how God views you. I'm grateful that God has allowed me to have some tough skin and push through tough times."
"Days like this come from being on the other side and not playing so great. I'm grateful that God has allowed me to have this opportunity to play today."
Q: This offense is starting to become like muscle memory for you. Can you talk about the game that Nick Caley called today?
"Again, great job by Cales. He got the game ball, and he's very deserving of it. He gets a lot of slack as well. Everybody has an opinion nowadays, but he and I have the opportunity to go do something about it.
"I have the utmost trust in him. The fact that he's been so aggressive, throwing the ball down the field, shows how much faith and trust he has in our O-line, tight ends, receivers, running backs and myself."
"Kudos to him for keeping the faith because it can go like the Giants game, where it doesn't go so great. For him to have faith coming off a bye week, I thought was really great."

title: Texans' Biggest Winners & Losers From Blowout Win vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Houston Texans came out of the bye looking strong on both sides of the ball in Week 9, as they took down the LA Chargers on the road in SoFi Stadium , 44-22, to mark down their third win of the season.
And in the midst of the Texans' Week 9 win, there were a handful of big winners around the roster to take note of that stood out with a big performance. There were also a couple of losers on Houston's end that stood out for one reason or another, even if they came out on top with a much-needed victory.
With that in mind, let's sort through a batch of four Texans winners and two losers from their dominant win over the Chargers:
It's hard to argue that anyone was a bigger winner in this game than C.J. Stroud, as he found his way to a season-high 384 yards and five touchdowns, leading the Texans' offense to their highest point total of the season in the process.
Stroud was sharing the ball around to multiple playmakers and showed some elite-level decision-making. If he can continue playing like this while the Texans keep up the winning, it'll be hard not to put him into some MVP conversations.
What a memorable day it was for Tank Dell, who was active for his second game since returning from his 2024 knee injury, and had a true breakout performance looking like his pre-injury self : four catches, 105 yards, one touchdown, and tied for the Texans' biggest offensive play of the day at 63 yards.
Many wondered just how the Texans' passing attack would pivot without Jaylin Noel in the lineup. It turns out, Tank Dell might be more than ready to take on those extra opportunities.
In a week where the Texans felt due to give Marvin Harrison Jr. a larger share of the workload in the passing game, that leap in usage didn't exactly happen for Houston's newest wideout. He saw just two receptions for 20 yards in a game that looked largely similar to his prior two showings.
It's still early in Harrison Jr.'s tenure with the Texans, and it's far too soon to press the panic button for what's ahead. But three games in, Houston's big investment at the wide receiver position hasn't panned out quite as well as expected , while others around the room (Dell, Kayshon Boutte) are shining in their opportunities.
After two quiet weeks from Will Anderson, where the Texans' star edge rusher failed to come away with a single sack to add onto his league-leading total, the verdict was a whole lot different this weekend.
Anderson came away with two sacks as a part of the Texans' wrecking performance upfront in their pass rush. Anderson now has a bit more of a comfortable lead as the NFL sack leader through nine weeks, and might have the inside track to winning Defensive Player of the Year midway through the season.
After being the center of trade rumors over the past week , Jadeveon Clowney proved exactly why the Texans need to keep him around for the second half of the season.
Clowney was one of Houston's three pass-rushers to finish with two sacks on the day, as one of the many disrupters to cause havoc on Justin Herbert. If it wasn't clear as to why the Texans brought in Clowney before the season, games like these are perfect representations as to why his presence down the depth chart can be valuable.
Heading into this game, it felt like Marlin Klein's stock was trending up . The Texans' second-round rookie tight end had been a healthy scratch on the gameday roster every week dating back to Week 4 against the Dallas Cowboys, but was officially activated for the day against the Chargers.
However, even while Klein was finally able to get on the active roster, he pretty much remained a non-factor on the offensive end and on special teams, which makes you wonder what the purpose was for the Texans to activate him in the first place.
At the very least, avoiding that healthy scratch is a step in the right direction for Klein to eventually become an impact player in the Texans' offense. But time is slowly dwindling for that to happen in his rookie season.

title: 3 Texans Takeaways From Resounding 44-22 Win vs. Chargers
full_text:
The Houston Texans came out of their bye week looking better than ever in their Week 9 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, as they were able to come away with a commanding 44-22 victory to lift their record to 3-5 at the official midway point of the regular season.
Let's do some instant analysis of the Texans' Week 9 win by sorting through three instant takeaways just minutes after time expired in Los Angeles:
You can't talk about the Texans' success in this game without first addressing C.J. Stroud–– who had quite possibly one of his best games since entering the NFL from start to finish.
Stroud did record his second interception of the season, but that only came because of a tipped ball that got in the hands of Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley.
Outside of that blip on the radar, though, the Texans quarterback played lights out. He completed 21 of his 35 passes for a season-high 384 yards and five touchdowns.
Stroud got his top targets involved consistently throughout the day: Xavier Hutchinson claimed the first touchdown of the year, Stroud made sure to feature Nico Collins a bit more than last week with four receptions, 55 yards and a touchdown, but the two biggest standouts were Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell.
C.J. Stroud to Tank Dell for the TD 🗣️ HOUvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/r0q9mBmr5d
Boutte and Dell combined for eight receptions, 130 yards and three touchdowns, which was made possible by a well-called game by offensive coordinator Nick Caley after the bye , and a strong day commanding the Texans' offense under center by Stroud.
More days like this from the Texans' offense could be just what the team needs to rattle off a few late-season wins. In this game against LA, that production from Stroud was the engine behind a much-needed victory following the week off.
The Chargers' offense looked uncoordinated all day as they have throughout the seven games they played before this one. But one area that the Texans' defense really managed to expose was their holes in pass protection.
It was a statement day for the Texans when it came to bringing pressure on Justin Herbert. After the defense had combined for just three sacks over the past two weeks, Houston came alive for a whopping eight takedowns on the Chargers' signal-caller for 40 yards.
And it wasn't simply a one-man wrecking crew upfront for the Texans either. Everybody was eating.
Will Anderson Jr. got back on track with two sacks. Jadeveon Clowney made his presence felt with a pair of sacks. Sheldon Rankins got a couple of his own. Even safety M.J. Stewart got one. That led to Justin Herbert completing 13-23 passes for less than 200 yards, with a touchdown and an interception.
Watch for the sack. Stay for the celly. HOUvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yR3ue1gJWu
If the Texans can continue causing that type of disruption within the trenches moving forward, combined with the improved play this secondary also showed against Los Angeles, this Houston defense could finally be able to get back to business as one of the best collective units in the NFL.
This is an overall positive showing for the Texans, no doubt. This was their highest point total in a game this year, as well as their second-biggest margin of victory. Coming on a West Coast road trip makes those results even more impressive for Houston.
However, the result is one the Texans should take with a grain of salt.
On one hand, the Texans really stepped up in all three phases. C.J. Stroud took care of business with his best performance of the year, the defense wrecked havoc throughout the day en route to two turnovers, eight tackles, and less than 4.5 yards allowed per play from Los Angeles.
On another note, it's fair to keep in consideration that this Chargers roster has not won a game this season. Los Angeles entered this week with the worst scoring offense in the NFL and the highest turnover count. This was a game the Texans should've dominated .
So, while the Texans and fans alike should certainly celebrate this win, what's more important is how the team takes this win and creates some momentum with it.
Houston has three winnable games up ahead against the Cleveland Browns, Indianapolis Colts, and Baltimore Ravens, and this game against the Chargers does provide some confidence that the Texans could have another late-season run in store like they did around this time last year.

title: Texans' Week 9 Inactives vs. Chargers Feature One Key Surprise
full_text:
The Houston Texans and LA Chargers sit right around the corner from their Week 9 matchup at SoFi Stadium .
And in the leadup to Sunday's action, we now have a clear picture of which players will be out on each side, as both teams have officially released their inactives list ahead of kickoff.
Let's break down what we learned from each side:
S Reed Blankenship TE Cade Stover RB David Montgomery OG Febechi Nwaiwu OT Braden Smith OT Nate Thomas
The Texans will be down a couple of key starters due to injury, while also sitting out a couple of key names on the offensive side of the ball for one reason or another.
As for those dealing with injury, running back David Montgomery (groin) and Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand) had been ruled out for Week 9 earlier in the week after each being unable to practice throughout the entire week.
Both have been out with their respective injuries dating back to before the bye week, but even after an extra few days of rest, those two will have to wait before getting back on the field for a game. Their next opportunity to return to the lineup comes in Week 10 against the Cleveland Browns.
Outside of the Texans' injuries, a couple of other inactives stuck out as a bit more noteworthy: veteran offensive tackle Braden Smith was deemed a healthy scratch, as Blake Fisher is expected to take the duties as Houston's backup swing tackle to Aireontae Ersery and Trent Brown .
That means Fisher will be deemed the Texans' primary jumbo tackle to enter the game for those six-offensive-linemen sets. However, it remains to be seen just how much Houston implements that personnel into their game plan coming out of the bye.
The biggest surprise of the Texans' inactives list, though? Second-round rookie tight end Marlin Klein is not seen as a healthy scratch this week, meaning that he'll get his first chance to hit the field for the first time since Week 3.
Klein has only played three games on the Texans' season so far, recording one reception for 16 yards. This Sunday, Houston's third pick of their most recent draft will finally get a chance to add to those numbers .
Cade Stover will be the fifth tight end on the roster to be deemed inactive for the week, leaving Klein to join next to Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau, and Brevin Jordan at the position on the depth chart.
To round out the Texans' inactives, fourth-round rookie Febechi Nwaiwu still awaits his NFL debut and will be inactive for another week, while Nate Thomas has still yet to make his debut as a part of the Texans' roster and will also be deemed a healthy scratch for Week 9.

The Chargers won't be facing any surprise absences on their inactives list. All of their top starters will be healthy and ready to play, hoping to claim their first victory on the season after a brutal 0-7 start.

title: Indianapolis Colts Fire Sale Tracker: Analysis, Trades, Rumors, and More
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts will be the center of the NFL world for the foreseeable future.
This is the second consecutive season that Indianapolis will be featured in trade talks at the midway point, but unlike last year, it's not because they're the number one seed in the AFC.
Instead of buying at the deadline, the Colts will be selling.
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline (November 10th, 4 PM EST) is quickly approaching, and the Colts are amidst a complete teardown of their franchise.
The Colts fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard after they fell to 2-4 in a humiliating loss, and have been active in the trade market ever since as they look to recoup any valuable draft capital they can after Ballard traded away their 2027 first-round pick, as well as their 2026 first-rounder and WR Adonai Mitchell.
It was the beginning of a poetic end, as the last Ballard-led Colts game was a loss to the 0-5 Tennessee Titans, a team that many still consider the worst team in the NFL. Even then, this version of the Colts may very well be the league's worst.
On top of only one playoff win in three appearances, the Colts failed to win the lowly AFC South across 9.5 seasons (2017-2026) under Chris Ballard.
Despite ample evidence to suggest otherwise, Indianapolis Colts' Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon decided to bring back both Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen for the 2026 season, referencing their hot start to the previous year as a reason to give them another chance.
The former had been given far too many chances to that point, but to be fair to Irsay-Gordon and her sisters, Co-Owners Kalen Jackson and Casey Foyt, this was the organization's first full offseason under new ownership.
Following the decision to give Ballard and Steichen one last shot in her postseason press conference, Irsay-Gordon said that the "sense of urgency has never been higher" for the GM/HC tandem.
Many didn't believe her, given that she was entering her first full offseason as an NFL Owner/CEO and appeared to be betting on an inevitable collapse, but Irsay-Gordon did what needed to be done, even if it came a bit too late.
In the past 14 days, the Indianapolis Colts have fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard, fallen to 2-6 on the season, and traded away two of their franchise cornerstones.
This article is meant to serve as a one-stop shop for all things Indianapolis Colts-related ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline. I will be updating this story as new information presents itself, so be sure to regularly check back in.
Navigate our trade central (finalized trades, rumors, etc.), future outlook, and more below.
Outside of players still on their rookie contract, as well as some exceptions such as cornerback Sauce Gardner, wide receiver Alec Pierce, left tackle Bernhard Raimann, and a few others, nobody on the Colts roster is safe.
Although the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline is on November 10th at 4 PM EST, the Colts have already gotten a head start on their fire sale.
In order, our trade central will featured finalized trades, a rumor mill, and will conclude with analysis on the team's overall outlook.
A current third-round pick and a future fifth-rounder may seem scoff-worthy at first glance, but when you break down the history of traded compensation for other guards across the league, Nelson's haul starts to make more sense.
Indianapolis' return of a 3rd and a 5th for Quenton Nelson is the most pure draft capital for a guard since at least 2011, per Spotrac. only 4 have netted a 4th: 2013: G. Carimi, 4th 2014: L. Mankins, 4th + player 2021: B. Bredeson + 5th + 7th, 4th 2025: J. Thuney, 4th
I think this is both the best example of why the return for Quenton Nelson isn’t as irresponsible as some are suggesting, and also why the Chris Ballard era needed to end: non-premium positions.
It stings to see any team trade their homegrown future Hall of Famer, but this is the bed the Colts made, and now they must sleep in it.
The Colts' 2026 fourth-round rookie guard Jalen Farmer is Nelson's immediate replacement.
Buckner's departure creates a similar challenge on the defensive line. More responsibility will fall on the remaining interior defenders, including Stewart and Adetomiwa Adebawore.
Not only is the opportunity there, but Adebawore has earned the increased role in question.
After seven weeks, Adebawore is undeniably the Colts' best pass rusher. He is currently tied for second with the most sacks among interior defensive linemen league-wide and leads the team in most major pass-rush statistics.
We've known that Adebawore has some nasty pass-rushing chops, but the biggest development has been his improvement in run defense.
Adebawore has blossomed into a legitimate starting defensive tackle, and it comes at no better time as the Colts have parted ways with their longtime pillar across the defensive line.
However, the Colts' newfound star is on an expiring deal. Adebawore is playing in the final year of his rookie contract, so a big payday is set to come his way.
Update (11/3) : The Indianapolis Colts have signed Adetomiwa Adebawore to a two-year, $35 million contract extension that includes a $13 million signing bonus and $22.5 in new money through 2027.
Update (11/5) : NFL Insider Jordan Schultz : "The belief around the league is that, barring an offer that blows them away, Indianapolis plans to wait until after Sunday’s game vs the Cowboys before revisiting the offers on the table and making the trades that make sense on Monday and Tuesday ahead of the deadline.
ESPN's NFL Insider Adam Schefter confirmed on Halloween that the Indianapolis Colts are officially open to trading Jonathan Taylor and have been active in talks.
Schefter added that the Colts have already received an offer of a 2027 second-round pick along with additional compensation for Taylor's services.
Colts Owner/CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon views Taylor as "a key part of the organization and a likely mainstay in their rebuild," according to Schefter and fellow ESPN Insider Ian Rapoport , the latter of whom added that Indianapolis could change its stance if the right offer comes along, leaving the door open without signaling that a deal is imminent.
Taylor's most comparable trade package is that of Christian McCaffrey's blockbuster haul from 2022.
In exchange for McCaffrey, the Panthers received a 2023 NFL Draft second-round pick, a 2023 third-rounder, a 2023 fourth-rounder, and a 2024 fifth-round pick.
The Colts are understandably trying to pry a first-round pick from an interested suitor's hands, but it doesn't feel like they'll be able to achieve that.
However, if teams get desperate enough, the Colts may end up pulling off a much-needed heist to kickoff their rebuild.
Of course, the highly unlikely yet somewhat feasible hypothetical first-round compensation would come via a contender, thus the projected draft pick would not be able to relieve the hurt that is the Colts' projected Top 5 pick that is sitting in New York, though it would help tremendously.
The good news for this pipe dream is that Taylor is garnering heavy interest across the league. According to Schefter, multiple teams have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing.
"The list of teams that have expressed at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor is thought to include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, and New York Giants," Schefter wrote.
NFL Insider Jordan Schultz added on Monday that the Cincinnati Bengals and Seattle Seahawks have entered the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
"My understanding is that 5-6 teams have been aggressively pursuing him: Giants, Packers, Broncos, Seahawks, Bengals, Vikings," Schultz said on The Pivot .
"I think it'll take at least a second-round plus additional compensation to get it done, and I actually do expect that to happen."
The aforementioned Christian McCaffrey blockbuster haul remains the ideal return for the Indianapolis Colts.
