title: The Morning-After Thunder: Chargers Defense Breaks as Offense Watches Helplessly
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel tried a new approach against the Texans. McDaniel moved from on the field to the booth to call the game, the results were the same. The Chargers lost, again.
The Chargers' trainwreck of season continued in week nine against the Houston Texans. The final score of the game was 44-22; a final score that makes the game feel more competitive than it actually was. Los Angeles has now fallen to 0-8 on the season.
The Chargers offense continues to be unable to score and remains frustratingly inefficient. Despite being winless on the season, head coach Jim Harbaugh is not adjusting his coaching style, he maintains a conversative approach, opting for field goals instead of going for fourth-down attempts.
Los Angeles' defense has been the lone bright spot for the team this season. The defense has consistently put their best foot forward and gone to battle week in and week out despite the offense not holding up their end of the bargain. The defense was bound to have a bad day at the office and that day came this week against the Texans. Houston quarterback CJ Stroud appeared dialed in and carved up the Chargers defense. Even when the coverage was perfect, passes were still caught.
NICO COLLINS, ARE YOU KIDDING ME?!? 🤯 (via @HoustonTexans ) pic.twitter.com/zv7Zrgbuf0
There were several developments that happened before, during and after this beat down that are worth discussing for the Chargers. Let's dive into the biggest takeaways.
Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has dealt with every injury imaginable this season and his role in Mike McDaniel's offense has left him downrange for massive hits across the middle. He played only his second full game of 2026 in week eight afte coming off a bye. McConkey experienced back spasms in pregame warm ups in Week 9 and did not play a single snap against the Texans.
Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz brought in Cole Strange and gave him a low-level starters contract to be the Chargers new right guard after spending most of the season with Mike McDaniel and the Miami Dolphins in 2025. Everyone outside of the Chargers building suspected this may not go well.
It is not breaking news that the Cole Strange experiment has been awful. He has been the worst offensive lineman the Chargers have had on the field this season and the grades make that clear. Still, the Chargers rolled him out there every week but finally Texans defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins took him behind the woodshed today, to the point where the broadcast was nearly laughing about how bad he was being beaten on a down to down basis.
The Chargers finally pulled him and rotated Branson Taylor and rookie Alex Harkey. Head coach Jim Harbaugh did say that Strange may have lost his starting job and they will look at it this week.
After 37 consecutive drives, the Chargers finally scored a touchdown as Quentin Johnston broke a tackle and broke free for a 57 yard catch and run. When asked about the streak ending, tight end Charlie Kolar had no idea it had been that many drives without a touchdown.
#Chargers TE Charlie Kolar had no idea the offensive did not score in 37 straight drives. 💀😅 “37!?” Kolar said. “I wish you never told me that.” @SportingTrib | #BoltUp pic.twitter.com/nlcpzub7TS
It appears breaking a bone now appears to be an annual tradition for Justin Herbert. Late in the third quarter Herbert stiffed armed away a would be sack and immediately looked down at his finger. In true Justin Herbert fashion, he did not come out of the game and actually finished the drive with the touchdown to Quentin Johnston.
Herbert went to the sideline and the blue medical tent and emerged with a glove with a massive temporary cast on his finger. The specific injury has not been announced but the broadcast did capture his finger pointing in an unnatural direction. Backup quarterback DJ Uiagalelei finished the game and threw his first career touchdown pass.
The Chargers are driving the NFL world mad with their apparent stance that they will not trade anyone. There is an argument that because the Chargers do not have high-value trade assets, the late Day 3 picks that they could get in return are not worth moving on from as they try to right the ship heading into 2027.
oh but remember, they don't want to make anyone feel discouraged!
It is worth noting that edge rusher Caleb Murphy who has mainly logged special teams snaps since he returned to the Chargers, did function as the fourth edge against the Texans despite Bud Dupree being active. Either Dupree has been demoted or Murphy may be getting a look in the event that Khalil Mack is moved before the trade deadline despite all the public statements that he will not be moved. Dupree has not logged snaps on defense since week five.
All eyes now shift to the Chargers front office ahead of the deadline. Will they still stand pat and move no one? Or will they move a player or two at the deadline?

title: Justin Herbert Injury: How Does Chargers QB’s Setback Impact NFL Trade Deadline?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have fallen to 0-8, already finding themselves in what we all thought was the worst possible situation for the franchise after their semi-successful 2024 and 2025 seasons. Unfortunately, in classic Chargers fashion, it got worse .
Justin Herbert suffered a finger injury , playing through the injury for a few plays, eventually moving to the blue medical tent once the offense was off the field. Once it was time for the offense to go back on the field, Herbert stayed back and found himself on the bench watching backup QB DJ Uiagalelei finish out the blowout loss at the hands of the Houston Texans.
While information has yet to be finalized on the exact injury Herbert has suffered, it seems that the consensus is a broken middle finger on his non-throwing hand. Herbert has played through broken fingers before, but it seems that the team may need time to consider if he should continue to play and risk more injury.
Now, with this hesitancy, this could very well change the Bolts' outlook on the NFL trade deadline, which is right around the corner, being marked as Nov. 10, 2026.
With the Bolts being 0-8, NFL teams were rightfully calling Los Angeles to ask about some of the team's players in hopes of hoping their own roster. The Chargers should be answering those calls and looking to build for their future, not for the 0-8 2026 Chargers.
Unfortunately, Joe Hortiz has seemingly been unwilling to move away from players, with reporters saying the Chargers "still have belief" prior to this Texans loss. Now, with another loss and their star QB injured, can they finally turn the other way and sell off assets?
Of course, only time will tell, but it was only logical when the team was 0-5; it is even more logical with the team being 0-8 and with an injured QB. To go full fire-sale mode, some names to look out for on the trade market:
Khalil Mack: The most spoken-about trade asset . He has mentioned he does not want to be traded, but it is worth mentioning that the veteran EDGE has plenty of value to other teams...if Mack were to change his mind.
Donte Jackson: Another veteran who could have some value for a team in need of a starting-caliber DB. Even with the Chargers having injuries piling up at the position, it could be smart to let young practice squad players play rather than letting Jackson play for no team-related upside.
Dalvin Tomlinson: One of the team's better run defenders could find his way on the market, as he is playing well, is healthy and is 32 years old. The Chargers have other options in Jamaree Caldwell and Nick Barrett who could take some snaps as the position.
Daiyan Henley: A young LB who had a 2024 season filled with promise. He had an interception against the Houston Texans, but he is obviously in need of a fresh start. He could possibly be valued highly around the league considering his age and history of strong play.

title: Where the Chargers Stand 48 Hours Before the  NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are officially at a crossroads. What was supposed to be a season of competing and building momentum has turned into something entirely different. At 0-8, the Chargers have reached a point where simply looking ahead to the next game isn’t enough.
Sunday’s game was another reminder of how much work remains for this team. Eight games into the season, the Bolts still cannot get into rhythm.
Now, general manager Joe Hortiz has to determine what makes the most sense for the organization moving forward. They don’t necessarily need to abandon everything they have been building, but continuing to approach the season as if a turnaround is right around the corner could be a mistake.
One of the biggest questions heading into Tuesday is whether they will seriously consider moving veteran players. I know they are firm on not dealing any of their guys whatsoever.
However, When a team is sitting at 0-8, the conversation surrounding potential trades naturally changes. Players who might have been considered untouchable earlier in the season could suddenly become part of a much larger discussion. With every loss more becomes possible.
Khalil Mack is an interesting name in that conversation. His experience and production make him valuable, especially to teams that believe they have a legitimate opportunity to compete this season.
There is also the question of what the Bolts could realistically receive in return. A trade only makes sense if the compensation matches the value of what the organization is giving up. Accumulating draft picks is important, but those selections eventually have to translate into players who can help change the direction of the franchise.
The same approach should apply to any other veteran who could generate interest around the league. Hortiz needs to evaluate the roster honestly rather than make decisions based solely on the disappointment of the current record.
Perhaps the most important part of this situation is what happens once Tuesday passes. The Chargers still have the remainder of the season to evaluate their roster, develop younger players and determine which areas require the most attention heading into the offseason.
There is no reason to make unnecessary moves simply because the season has gone poorly. However, there is also little reason to ignore opportunities that could improve the team beyond this year. The Chargers have reached a point where the remainder of the season should be about finding answers. Tuesday’s deadline gives the organization its first major opportunity to act on that reality.
Honestly, there's no salvaging the season. The question is whether the decisions made over the next 48 hours can help prevent another season like this one.
The Chargers are reportedly not trading players ahead of the deadline. Per ESPN, they do not want to send the message that they are quitting on the season. I'd argue keeping McDaniel without any adjustments sends a louder message of quitting than flipping expirings for picks. pic.twitter.com/1XxdAW8S7k

title: Chargers' Justin Herbert Suffers Injury During Blowout Loss
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers took an absolute beating at the hands of the Houston Texans during Week 9. The Chargers had hoped to find some success on offense with a few changes including Mike McDaniel leaving the field level.
The Chargers offense has not been good this year. They have been downright awful and dead last on most statistical categories. It did not get better on Sunday. The Chargers offense watched hopelessly as their defense failed to contain CJ Stroud and the Texans' wide receivers.
Jim Harbaugh left Justin Herbert in the game despite the score being 41-9 late in the third quarter. Herbert, under pressure all afternoon, tried to evade a sack and stiff armed a defensive lineman. He immediately looked down at his left hand and started shaking it.
It appeared from closeup views on the broadcast that Herbert either broke or dislocated his middle finger on his left non-throwing hand. He went on to finish the drive and score the Chargers first touchdown in nearly 40 offensive possessions. He would not return and was replaced by backup DJ Uiagalelei while Hebert was seen with a massively taped glove and covering on his left hand.
Look At The Glove Justin Herbert Has On His Hand. Holy Crap, That Thing Is Huge. You Don’t See A Quarterback Wearing Something Like That Every Week. pic.twitter.com/OZs2AHuEuw
DJ Uiagalelei threw his first career touchdown pass on the following drive.
This story will be updated with more information when it becomes available.
Thomas Martinez has covered the Chargers and the NFL draft since 2022. Born and raised as a Chargers fan, experienced the improbable Super Bowl run in the 94’ season as a child, survived Ryan Leaf, the Marlon McCree fumble and Nate Kaeding in the playoffs. He graduated from UC Riverside with a degree in Political Science and The University of Redlands with an MBA.

title: Chargers' Ladd McConkey suffers injury vs. Texans
full_text:
While attempting to avoid 0-8 ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Los Angeles Chargers suffered another injury setback with wide receiver Ladd McConkey.
McConkey was absent from the Chargers’ stat sheet halfway through the first quarter while his team was down 7-3 when it was revealed that he was questionable to return due to a back injury.
According to Noah Furtado of The Athletic, McConkey suffered from back spasms during pregame warmups.
McConkey has battled nagging injury woes all season while also struggling in Mike McDaniel's offense. Entering Sunday, he had appeared in six games, catching just 17 passes for 286 yards and one score. In a testament to just how off the rails things have gone for the Chargers, that still led the entire offense.
When McConkey misses time, Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris are the primary one-two punch. Rookie Brenen Thompson, a hand-picked McDaniel target, is out.
UPDATE: McConkey didn't enter the game, nor did coaches such as Jim Harbaugh have anything to add on the topic after the 44-22 loss.
As we noted later, the Chargers now have some serious Ladd McConkey questions to consider for the long-term future. Harbaugh and Co. don't figure to be buyers or sellers at the trade deadline this week, but McConkey's repeated injury woes creates more questions than answers for next offseason and beyond.

title: NFL Trade Deadline Speculation Wonders About Justin Herbert to Vikings
full_text:
Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has suddenly been connected to speculation involving the Minnesota Vikings, creating an interesting conversation about what a potential blockbuster trade between the two organizations could look like.
NFL reporter Albert Breer wrote that the Vikings should at least inquire about Herbert, as it wouldn't hurt anything at all. Breer noted that “I wouldn't mind the Vikings taking a swing on this.” With the Bolts being winless halfway through the season and Kyler Murray not living up to expectations, this wouldn't be a stretch by either side.
However, Joe Horitz and Jim Harbaugh have made it crystal clear that Herbert is not available and they are sticking with their franchise quarterback.
Obviously moving on from a quarterback like Herbert would be an enormous decision for the organization. His arm strength, ability to make difficult throws, and overall physical tools have made him a major part of the Chargers future. Players with that kind of ability simply do not become available very often.
That is exactly why this situation is so interesting.
For the Vikings, the idea of bringing in Herbert would be a massive opportunity. The Vikings have been looking for long-term stability at the quarterback position, and acquiring someone with Herbert’s experience and ability would immediately change the conversation surrounding the franchise.
A quarterback of Herbert’s caliber would not come cheap. Any team attempting to acquire him would likely have to put together a significant package involving valuable draft capital and potentially additional pieces. We're talking about multiple first-round picks.
Meanwhile, the Chargers would have an equally difficult decision. Moving a player like Herbert would signal a major change in direction, especially considering how important he has been to the organization. It would also raise questions about what the Bolts believe their future should look like and whether the team would be willing to start over at the most important position in football.
At this point, there is a difference between discussing a possible trade and suggesting that something is actually close to happening. Herbert remains a Charger, and speculation involving the Vikings should be treated accordingly. Still, the fact that his name is being connected to a potential move like this is enough to get people talking. If a deal of this magnitude ever became realistic, it would easily become one of the biggest quarterback stories in the NFL. The Vikings would potentially get their franchise quarterback, while the Chargers could find themselves entering an entirely different era.
It is a fascinating possibility, even if it remains just that for now.
Brennan is sports writer focused on delivering sharp analysis, real-time reactions, and engaging storytelling focused on NFL analysis.  He is passionate about football and breaking down what matters to bring fans closer to the action.  Brennan comes from a family of Chargers fans.

title: LIVE: Rams NFL Trade Deadline Tracker — Trades, Rumors and Latest News
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline has officially arrived, and the Los Angeles Rams could be a team to watch. After placing several key starters on injured reserve over the last few weeks, including wide receiver Puka Nacua on Monday, the Rams could look to add at the position on deadline day.
Throughout the Les Snead and Sean McVay era, the Rams have been one of the more aggressive teams when it comes to making trades. On Tuesday, the question will be whether the Rams feel like they can still compete at 5-4 despite all of the injuries.
The Jacksonville Jaguars are not planning to trade wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. With Thomas falling out of favor with the Jaguars over the last several weeks, there had been some speculation that the Jaguars would listen to offers for Thomas. With that said, the Jaguars seem to feel that Thomas provides more value on their roster at 6-2 than a potential future draft pick.
The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources. They have relayed that to interested teams. Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise. pic.twitter.com/0QxdybXqaN
Prior to Monday, the Rams seemed content with their roster. The idea in the building seemed to be that players coming back from injury could be treated as in-season trade acquisitions. “What you look at is hopefully some of those trades will be guys getting back from injury that haven't played for us. That's the way that we look at it,” said head coach Sean McVay.
However, that has changed since Nacua went on injured reserve. McVay said on Tuesday that the team will look at all avenues and see what the team can come up with. With Jordan Whittington also injured, the Rams currently only have Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, and CJ Daniels available at wide receiver.
“I think you have to look at all avenues to try to be able to solve some of the issues or situations or scenarios that have come up,” McVay said. “A lot of new things occur on a daily basis, so I would never rule it out.”
As much as the Rams may want to make a trade, there are some limiting factors with the cap space and draft capital that they have available. There are ways to make a deal work, but the Rams would have to get creative.
According to the NFLPA Public Salary Cap report, the Rams have around $248,600 in salary cap to work with. That makes a trade very difficult unless the other team is willing to take on a large portion of the salary or the Rams restructure a contract.
With that said, another significant obstacle to the Rams making a move will be their limited draft capital. The Rams don’t have a first- or third-round pick next year. Moving their second-round pick would mean not picking until the fourth round. They do have available picks in 2028, but the Rams may not be as willing to move those.
The Rams are in dire need of a wide receiver after Puka Nacua's injury. Here are a few names that have been rumored targets .
The Rams typically haven’t been active on trade deadline day, but that could change this year. At the 2018 NFL trade deadline, the Rams acquired edge rusher Dante Fowler. Fowler helped propel the Rams to the Super Bowl that year. Just ahead of the trade deadline in 2021, Snead traded for edge rusher Von Miller from the Denver Broncos.
In 2019, the Rams traded away cornerback Aqib Talib. The Rams made a similar move in 2024, trading away Tre White.

title: Rams Should Swing for the Fences With Garrett Wilson at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams approach the NFL trade deadline , they will be exploring their options at wide receiver. With Puka Nacua likely set to go on injured reserve and Davante Adams out as well, Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and CJ Daniels make Brandon Gibson, Tavon Austin, and Austin Pettis look good.
Heading into Tuesday’s deadline, there had been some speculation that the Rams could make a move for Jacksonville Jaguars’ wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. However, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler has reported that the team isn’t looking to move Thomas.
With Thomas unavailable, the options for the Rams at wide receiver are very limited . While Josh Downs could be available, he may no longer be a fit. Downs would have been a good WR2 or WR3 alongside Nacua and Adams, but he’s not a true WR1. He’s certainly an upgrade over what the Rams have, but the Rams would still be in a similar situation to the one they're in now.
The issue with the Rams’ wide receiver situation is that they don’t just need another complementary wide receiver. Players like Jauan Jennings or Jerry Jeudy make sense as complementary pieces. However, without Nacua and Adams , the Rams need a player who can be a featured piece of the offense.
Under Les Snead, the Rams have been no stranger to taking big swings. They are a team that has consistently swung for the fences with trades. Just this offseason, the Rams acquired All-Pro players in Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett. The Rams have made moves for players like Brandin Cooks, Marcus Peters, and Jalen Ramsey.
It’s very possible that the Rams simply stand pat and don’t chase their losses. In the end, that might be the smart thing to do. Still, at 5-4 and on a three-game winning streak, it wouldn’t be crazy for the Rams to believe that they can compete for a championship if they can keep their head above water until December.
Their options are certainly limited with Thomas no longer available. The Dallas Cowboys have also said that they have no plans to trade away George Pickens. If the Rams make a move on a wide receiver, it feels like it needs to be a big one. With that said, that type of trade may not be available.
Since McVay took over in 2017, the Rams have been able to take advantage of good players on bad teams with poor roster management. They traded for Dante Fowler and Ramsey from the Jaguars, both of whom were former first-round picks. The Rams did the same in a sense when they traded for Garrett this offseason.
If the Rams make a trade, that's the type of opportunity they should be targeting. One player who fits into that is wide receiver Garrett Wilson from the New York Jets. It seems unlikely that the Jets would trade Wilson. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reported a few weeks ago that the Jets have told teams no on Wilson. Wilson has also said that he wants to be a Jet.
“New York has gotten calls on Wilson, whose frustration with a struggling offense was evident during last week’s loss to the Dolphins,” wrote Pelissero ahead of Week 8. “But the Jets’ answer to interested teams has been emphatic: Wilson is not, and will not be, available for trade.”
Since then, the Jets have lost two more games, extending their losing streak to four as they sit at 2-7. They may be a team with three first-round picks in April, but they are likely headed into a new regime at the end of the year. Aaron Glenn could be on the way out, leaving the Jets with another new head coach.
As much as the Jets may not want to trade Wilson, every player has a price. If the Rams gave the Jets their second-round pick in 2027 along with a first-round pick in 2028, would that get the conversation started? Wilson would give the Rams a young wide receiver option alongside Nacua to replace Adams and only cost $1.5 million against the salary cap for this season.
It’s certainly possible that any mention of a Wilson trade is simply internet fodder. Wilson is a special player and the Jets just extended him last July. He’s a player they should want to build around. At the same time, does it make sense for the Jets to commit $100 million to Wilson given their current situation? They don’t have a quarterback and their head coach looks to be on his way out.
The Rams have made it clear that they're all-in on winning a Super Bowl this season with the acquisitions of Garrett and McDuffie during the summer. At 5-4 and on a three-game winning streak, that could still happen even if injuries have put that in jeopardy.
Trading for Wilson would be expensive, but it would also give the Rams a legitimate chance to compete this season while setting themselves up for the future at wide receiver. It may take another aggressive move from Snead to convince the Jets to bite, but that's exactly the type of move he's built his reputation on making

title: Rams Week 9 Player Grades: Myles Garrett Shines, Matthew Stafford Struggles in Win
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams won their third consecutive game on Sunday, defeating the Washington Commanders 20-13 to improve to 5-4. Myles Garrett's return provided a much-needed boost to the defense, which delivered one of its best performances of the season. However, Matthew Stafford and the offense remain inconsistent. Let's get into the Week 9 Player Grades.
The Rams have gotten average quarterback play from Matthew Stafford for most of the season, and Sunday was no different. Stafford missed throws that he typically makes and had another really bad interception. He finished with a -0.06 EPA per pass and 36.0 QBR. If the Rams are going to make a run in the second half of the season, they need Stafford to be better.
Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 103 yards on the ground. Corum scored a touchdown and Williams had an important conversion on fourth down on the opening drive. Williams added three receptions in the passing game as well, while Corum didn’t catch either of his two targets and got run through in pass protection.. Overall, the Rams’ running back duo played well.
We simply need to start grading the Rams’ wide receivers separately from Puka Nacua. Nacua played well, but this is a group project with one person doing all the work. Tutu Atwell dropped a pass on third down. Konata Mumpfield had two targets throughout the game and Jordan Whittington offers very little as a wide receiver. The Rams need to trade for a wide receiver.
The Rams were able to operate out of 13 personnel with Colby Parkinson healthy. However, until Terrance Ferguson returns from injury, the Rams’ tight ends don’t offer a lot in the passing game. Tyler Higbee had a drop and his route running left a lot to be desired. Given how Max Klare played last week, it’s fair to say he should get more opportunities.
For most of the season, the Rams have remained healthy on the offensive line. However, Steve Avila left Sunday’s game and Beaux Limmer was asked to step in. Limmer was fine, but the Rams will hope Avila is back in the lineup as soon as possible.
Myles Garrett returned for the Rams this week, and the entire defensive line benefited. Aaron Donald had his best game of the season. Ty Hamilton continues to play well in place of the injured Kobie Turner. As the Rams get healthy, the defensive line could be one of the biggest beneficiaries.
Over the last month, Omar Speights has played very good football. Because the Rams are perceived as being weaker at linebacker, Speights has flown under the radar despite playing like one of the better linebackers in the league. Nate Landman nearly created a turnover as well with the peanut punch.
Without Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, this group performed very well. Emmanuel Forbes was the best of the group on Sunday and has taken a step forward this season. He was targeted 10 times by the Commanders and had three pass breakups. Additionally, Kam Curl led the team in tackles.
Sunday was undoubtedly the best performance from the Rams’ special teams unit. Joshua Karty was effective on kickoffs, and Ethan Evans punted well. The bar was pretty low, but special teams played well against the Commanders.

title: 3 Wide Receivers the Rams Must Target at NFL Trade Deadline After Puka Nacua Injury
full_text:
If the Los Angeles Rams were in need of a wide receiver last week, they will be desperate for one heading into Tuesday’s trade deadline. The Rams will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua for at least the next four weeks with a sprained PCL and MCL in his knee. Over the next four weeks, The Rams now enter another grueling stretch of their schedule. If they are going to remain competitive, trading for a wide receiver is a must. Here are three wide receivers the Rams should consider trading for ahead of Tuesday's deadline.
Prior to the Rams losing Puka Nacua, Brian Thomas Jr. may not have made the most sense . It was hard to see where he fit once Davante Adams returned from injury. However, with both Nacua and Adams out, the Rams need a player that has the ability to be a WR1. While Thomas hasn’t found success in Liam Coen’s offense, he has already shown that he can be a WR1. He had 1,200 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie and fits the wide receiver profile that has been successful with Stafford.
The question remains whether the Jaguars would trade Thomas. While they are set to listen to offers, they are still 6-2 and he has a role in their offense. He may have more value on their roster than a second or third-round pick. With Nacua out, the Rams also won’t have a ton of leverage in trade negotiations.
George Pickens is currently playing the 2026 season on the franchise tag. He hasn’t been happy with the Cowboys this season and was inactive last week with a nagging hamstring injury. Still, he has 39 receptions for 533 yards and two touchdowns. He’s at least a player the Rams would have to make a call on before the trade deadline on Tuesday.
Pickens would fit in well alongside Nacua and Adams when they return, but he would likely cost the most to acquire. It’s also hard to see the Cowboys moving on from him as they remain in the thick of the NFC East race.They have said they aren’t willing to move on from Pickens, but everybody has a price.
Bad franchises stay bad for a reason. They typically trade away good players and the Rams have taken advantage of that in the past. Like Pickens, Wilson may not be available, but he’s someone the Rams should at least call on ahead of the trade deadline. He’s the caliber of wide receiver that the Rams need while Nacua and Adams are sidelined with injuries. Wilson has 43 receptions for 527 yards this season.
Again, the biggest hurdle here is getting the Jets to bite. Wilson just signed a contract extension last offseason and is someone the Jets want to build around. The Jets already have three first-round picks, but only have one pick in the second round and are 2-7. The worst the Jets can do is say no, and Wilson is a player worth calling on.
With the Rams in need of an “X” receiver, a player like Ridley could make sense . He’s a veteran who could help the Rams get by over the next four weeks. While Downs was initially one of my favorite options on the trade market, he’s not a WR1. He would have fit perfectly alongside Adams and Nacua, but he’s not a standalone guy. If the Rams want a cheaper option, Dontayvion Wicks from the Eagles could be someone to watch.

title: Rams Lose Puka Nacua to Injured Reserve as Injury Nightmare Continues
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams just can’t catch a break when it comes to injuries this season. On Monday, the Rams announced that they will be without wide receiver Puka Nacua as he heads to injured reserve. According to Ian Rapoport, Nacua sprained his MCL and PCL late in the game against the Washington Commanders and will now be out for at least four weeks.
The #Rams are expected to place WR Puka Nacua on Injured Reserve with MCL and PCL sprains, plus turf toe, coach Sean McVay told reporters. pic.twitter.com/LLWLyGwVMy
With Nacua headed to injured reserve, the soonest he would be able to come back is for the Rams’ Week 14 game against the Dallas Cowboys. It’s unfortunate timing for the Rams as Nacua is now set to miss arguably the most important part of their schedule. He’ll at least miss the team’s games against the Arizona Cardinals, Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and San Francisco 49ers.
Nacua got hurt on the second-to-last drive of the game against the Commanders. The Rams called a jet sweep to Nacua, who took a helmet to the knee. While the Rams were confident that Nacua didn’t tear his ACL, missing time always felt like a possibility.
All-Pro WR Puka Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap today, and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury, per @MikeGarafolo and me. The team does not believe he suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more. pic.twitter.com/S264w2Fe0A
Without Nacua, the Rams will now be down their top two wide receivers for the immediate future. Davante Adams was placed on injured reserve following the loss to the Arizona Cardinals. His timeline was 6-10 weeks, and the Rams hope to have him back closer to the 6-8 week range. Still, Adams will likely miss the next three to four games as well.
That leaves the Rams with Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and Jordan Whittington as their top three wide receivers . While the Rams were set to get Terrance Ferguson back last week, a last-minute hamstring injury during Friday’s practice likely sidelined him through the bye.
The Rams' decision not to add a wide receiver in the offseason remains a huge oversight. Adams was coming off of a hamstring injury and Nacua hasn’t played all 17 games since his rookie year. The chances of both staying healthy were low, especially with Nacua averaging 13 targets per game given his physical playstyle. Nacua had already missed time with a groin/hip injury early in the season.
Now, to be clear, that doesn’t necessarily mean that the Rams should have drafted a wide receiver with the 13th overall pick. If Ty Simpson works out, that was the right call. However, the Rams had opportunities to draft Antonio Williams over Max Klare in the second round. They also could have added veterans such as Keenan Allen or Stefon Diggs before training camp.
Nacua’s injury is the latest setback in what has been an injury-riddled season for the Rams. Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Myles Garrett, Jaylen Watson, Kobie Turner, and Aaron Donald are among players for the Rams who have missed multiple games due to injury. Adams, Nacua, Garrett, Turner, and Watson are players who have now been on injured reserve. The Rams simply can’t seem to catch a break.
With the trade deadline on Tuesday, the Rams still have time to find a solution at wide receiver to help navigate the next four weeks. At 5-4 and entering a critical part of the season, the Rams need to continue winning games if they’re going to make the playoffs in a very difficult NFC.

title: 10 Takeaways From Rams’ Win Over Commanders: Myles Garrett Dominates, But Concerns at Wide Receiver Remain
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams won their third straight game on Sunday, beating the Washington Commanders 20-13. While it wasn’t pretty, the Rams are above .500 for the first time this season, with Myles Garrett impressing in his return . Let’s get into this week’s 10 takeaways.
Over the last two weeks, the Rams have gotten off to a slow start, but it’s been an issue for much of the season. They have yet to score a touchdown on the opening drive of a game. The Rams rank 24th in first quarter points per game and 17th in first quarter offensive EPA per play. Following the Rams’ opening drive that ended in a field goal, they had back-to-back three-and-outs. Sunday’s game was a 10 a.m. PT start on the road, but the Rams need to find a way to start quicker.
Over the last two months, the Rams have been awaiting Myles Garrett’s return to the field. After he returned to practice last week, Garrett made his return on Sunday in a limited role and made his presence felt. Garrett finished with three sacks, which was more than Josaiah Stewart and Wesley Bailey had all season. He also created a turnover with a forced fumble in the first half that resulted in points for the offense. Late in the fourth quarter, Garrett had a sack that helped stop a late surge by the Commanders. If Sunday was only a glimpse of what is to come, it’s hard not to be excited.
Nacua is carrying way too much of the Rams’ passing game. He finished with 14 catches on 19 targets. It was the fifth time in six games that Nacua had 10 or more targets. It’s also the second time he’s had 15 or more targets in a game. On drives in which Nacua had two or more catches on Sunday, the Rams scored all 20 of their points. When he didn’t, they punted four times and had an interception. It’s simply not sustainable and increases the risk of Nacua getting hurt.
The Rams did not convert a third down until the fourth quarter against the Commanders. Heading into the week, the Commanders ranked 26th in third down defense. The Rams are 6-for-25 on third downs over the last two weeks. Had the Rams not gone 3-for-3 on fourth down, it could have been a long day on offense. The third down operation hasn’t been good enough in recent weeks.
Throughout Aaron Donald’s career, players have experienced an “Aaron Donald effect”. Essentially, Donald was so good and garnered so much attention that other players benefitted. Donald got to experience the other side of that on Sunday. He had his best game of the season, recording nine impact plays according to Sumer Sports. His four pressures were also a season high. Donald came out of retirement to play alongside Garrett, and after the game, it was obvious how much he enjoyed it.
When the offense has struggled over the last two weeks, the defense has stepped up and done its part. After the Rams went 3-and-out on back-to-back drives following the Commanders’ touchdown, the defense forced two quick punts as well. Following the Rams’ two turnovers, the defense responded by forcing a turnover on the next play after one and holding the Commanders to a field goal after the other. The Rams asked their defense to win the game for them late in the fourth quarter and got two crucial stops.
Over the last three weeks, the Rams have found a good balance with their running back rotation. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum have had 10 or more carries in each of the last three games. Williams led the way with 15 carries, while Corum had 11 against the Commanders. Corum had 58 yards on his 11 carries with a long of 15 and also scored a touchdown. Matthew Stafford did throw the ball 43 times, but the Rams were able to lean on the run game when they needed to and the offense had balance.
After Trent McDuffie injured his back at the end of the game against the Chargers, he entered Sunday’s matchup listed as questionable. The Rams were also without Jaylen Watson, who was ruled out for the season with a shoulder injury. With McDuffie and Watson out, the Rams were relying on their depth corners in Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace. Both played well with Forbes having a tackle for loss and two key pass breakups. Wallace remained as steady as he’s been all season. The Rams have asked a lot of their depth cornerbacks this season with injuries and they stepped up again on Sunday.
Dare I say that the Rams’ special teams unit was actually good against the Commanders? Three of Joshua Karty’s four kickoffs hit the landing zone before going through the end zone for a touchback, putting the Commanders at the 20-yard line. Jordan Whittington had a nice kickoff return and Ethan Evans averaged over 50 yards per punt. It was by far the best performance from the special teams unit this season and it will be interesting to see if they can build on it.
When it comes to other teams in the NFC, the Rams likely aren’t in that top tier right now. They are likely a step below teams like the Chicago Bears and San Francisco 49ers. The Rams remain an imperfect team with clear flaws, but they seem to be finding their stride. After losing to the Cardinals, the Rams have won three straight games. Early in the season, the Rams found ways to lose. Now, they are finding ways to win. Getting to the bye week at 6-4 would be huge, but for the first time, the Rams are above .500, and that’s a step in the right direction.

title: Monday Morning Rambling: Rams Finally Get the Myles Garrett They've Been Waiting For
full_text:
Sitting in the press box at the Melbourne Cricket Ground back in September, it was almost depressing watching the Los Angeles Rams trot a limited version of Myles Garrett onto the field . Garrett was very clearly not 100 percent in that game and voiced that afterwards. After not recording a single pressure, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year and NFL sack leader walked into the media room and said, “This was the worst version of myself.”
Days later, the Rams placed Garrett on injured reserve, where he remained until Sunday.
The Rams traded away Jared Verse for Garrett in what was their biggest move of the offseason. In a similar thought process to when they traded Jared Goff for Matthew Stafford, the Rams hoped that trading for Garrett would match their current timeline better than Verse. Essentially, they could accelerate that development process.
Garrett was supposed to be the missing piece of the defense and the player who helped them close out games in the fourth quarter. What if the Rams had Garrett available in their losses to the Denver Broncos and Arizona Cardinals? Those were two games the Rams led late in the fourth quarter and the defense was unable to get a stop.
Instead, Garrett watched from the sideline in those games as he managed a knee injury that he’d dealt with since training camp. There was a lot of angst heading into Garrett’s return. Some weren’t even sure if he’d be back before the bye week. Garrett was originally given a six-week timeline before eventually missing seven games. Would he be the same dominant player the Rams had traded for in June?
The answer to that question was yes.
On Sunday, Garrett finished with three sacks, two of which were in the fourth quarter. His first came with him chasing Jayden Daniels from the backside before halftime, forcing a fumble and creating a turnover. That was one play after Puka Nacua and the offense had fumbled and the Commanders were looking to take control of the game.
Garrett’s second sack came on a 2nd-and-9 on Washington’s first drive of the fourth quarter to set up a 3rd-and-14. While the Commanders ended up converting, Garrett’s final sack may have been his most impactful and showed why the Rams traded for him. The Commanders faced 3rd-and-5 from the Rams’ 38-yard line after Garrett jumped offside. He immediately made up for it.
On the very next play, Daniels dropped back and Garrett cleanly beat the center to burst through the middle of the offensive line. Garrett wrapped up Daniels and sacked him to set up a 4th-and-17. When Emmanuel Forbes broke up the pass from Daniels to force a turnover on downs, the game was basically over in large part due to Garrett’s sack that resulted in a 12-yard loss.
Back in September, Garrett called that the worst version of himself. If Sunday was just a glimpse of what he can provide, it’s hard not to be excited for what’s to come. On Sunday, Garrett showed exactly why the Rams made the investment they did. It was only one game, but if this is the version that the Rams are getting for the second half of the season, the outlook for this team changes significantly.
It should be considered malpractice if the Rams don’t trade for a wide receiver this week . Puka Nacua has 41 targets in the last three weeks. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and Jordan Whittington have combined for 16 targets in that same span. Nacua had 19 targets against the Commanders alone and finished with 150 receiving yards. The next closest Rams wide receiver had 20. It’s just not sustainable.
Without trying to jinx anything, the Rams’ special teams unit played well yesterday. Josh Karty had three kickoffs bounce through the end zone to set up the Commanders at the 20-yard line. It seems crazy to keep two kickers, but it has worked. Ethan Evans averaged 52.8 yards per punt and had two land inside the 20. Jordan Whittington had a nice return as well. The bar is very low, but that was a promising performance.
The Rams were without their two starting cornerbacks on Sunday, yet they held Jayden Daniels to -0.19 EPA per pass, which ranked 19th for the week.. Emmanuel Forbes finished with two crucial pass breakups and had a tackle for loss. Josh Wallace remained solid as well. Defensive backs coach Jimmy Lake deserves a lot of credit for how well he’s coached up the cornerback depth.
How do you not give the game ball to Myles Garrett in this one ? Garrett had three sacks and a forced fumble. He was dominant in his return to the field in limited snaps. The Rams and Garrett had been waiting for that type of game, and with a lot of patience, they finally got it.
While the Rams may have been an abysmal 3-for-14 on third down, they were 3-for-3 on fourth down. The Rams converted a 4th-and-1 on their opening drive to set up a shorter field goal. They went for it again on 4th-and-3 during their final drive of the first half, which eventually resulted in another field goal. Those are six points the Rams added by going for it, and those points proved to matter in what was a seven-point win.
Since losing to the Cardinals, the Rams have gone on to win three straight. They’ll play the Cardinals again on Sunday and hope to take a four-game winning streak into the bye. Sunday could prove to be difficult if the Rams are without Puka Nacua after he got injured late against the Commanders. The Rams are still searching for their first division win of the year, and the Cardinals will be a good opportunity to get that.

title: Rams Winners & Losers: Myles Garrett Dominates in Return as Rams Win Third Straight
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams defeated the Washington Commanders 20-13 in Week 9 to win their third straight game and improve to 5-4 on the season. Sunday also marked Myles Garrett’s return to the field after spending the last two months on injured reserve. Garrett was one of the biggest winners of the day, recording three sacks and a forced fumble. Let’s get into this week’s winners and losers.
For the last two months, the Rams have been awaiting Myles Garrett’s return . Garrett showed up in a big way on Sunday. He had three sacks, the first of which forced a fumble and the last one helped put a stop to a late surge by the Commanders. Garrett opened up opportunities for Aaron Donald and others while making a significant impact despite a limited snap count. If Sunday was only Garrett scratching the surface, the Rams can be very excited for what’s to come.
Back in 2023, the Commanders took Forbes in the first round of the draft. Forbes was cut in the middle of the 2024 season and has been with the Rams ever since. While he’s been a rotational player this year and still hasn’t lived up to his first-round draft status, Forbes filled in for Jaylen Watson on Sunday and had a bit of a revenge game. Forbes played physical and had two crucial pass breakups in the second half, including one on 4th-and-17.
Every week, it seems we’re talking about the Rams’ lack of wide receiver depth , and this week is no different. The Rams did get Atwell more involved as he had a season-high five targets. However, he had a crucial drop on a 3rd-and-2 in which he was wide open over the middle and Matthew Stafford hit him in the hands. A big narrative over the last month is how the Rams need to get Atwell involved. That might be true, but Atwell needs to take advantage of his chances when he gets them.
One of the biggest winners of Myles Garrett being back in the lineup against the Commanders was Aaron Donald. A big reason why Donald came out of retirement was to play alongside Garrett. While he didn’t end up with a sack on Sunday, he was credited with nine impact plays via Sumer Sports. Garrett opened up 1-on-1 opportunities for Donald and it seems like only a matter of time before he gets his first sack.
Since falling to 2-4, the Rams have won three straight. According to The Athletic, the Rams have a 40 percent chance to make the playoffs. A win against another NFC team will help with tiebreakers. The Rams still need to focus on getting their first division win of the season and should have a good chance to do that this week against the Arizona Cardinals.
It’s clear that the Rams need Terrance Ferguson back in the lineup. Tyler Higbee simply can’t be consistently relied on in the passing game. He had some moments, but couldn’t come down with a perfectly placed ball from Stafford in the second half. Later in the game, he completely stopped on a route, leading to an incompletion. Higbee has his role in the offense, but it’s unrealistic to ask him to be the second receiving option.
Like Emmanuel Forbes, Kam Curl had an opportunity for revenge against his former team on Sunday. While Curl showed up as questionable on the injury report going into the game, there was no question he was going to do his best to play this one. Curl led the Rams’ defense with eight tackles and played a big role in the secondary with McDuffie and Watson out. He’s been one of the most important players on the Rams’ defense over the last two seasons and showed why against his former team.
Sunday’s game against the Commanders might be the first time all season that we haven’t had to talk negatively about the Rams’ special teams. Kyren Williams didn’t offer much as a returner, but the special teams unit played well. Joshua Karty had multiple dirty kickoffs go through the end zone, resulting in the Commanders starting at their own 20. Brandon McManus made both of his field goals and extra points. Ethan Evans averaged 52.8 yards per punt and had two punts land inside the 20. Dare I say, the Rams’ special teams unit played well?

title: Myles Garrett Was Worth the Wait as Rams Beat Commanders For Third Straight Win
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams overcame another slow start on Sunday against the Washington Commanders, winning 20-13. For two months, the Rams w aited for Myles Garrett to make his return , and Sunday showed that the wait was worth it. Garrett made his presence felt, finishing with three sacks and a forced fumble as the offense went through Puka Nacua in the win.
After trading for Garrett this offseason, the Rams had been without the 2025 sack leader and NFL Defensive Player of the Year since Week 1. Garrett had been on injured reserve for much of the last two months with a knee injury, but finally returned on Sunday.
It was Garrett’s forced fumble at the end of the first half that gave the offense momentum going into halftime and then his third sack of the day late in the fourth quarter that propelled the Rams to victory.
Without Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson at cornerback, the Rams relied on their cornerback depth. Facing his former team, Emmanuel Forbes had a pair of pass breakups in the second half.
Still, it took the Rams’ defense some time to find its rhythm. The Commanders scored on their first two drives as Jayden Daniels hit former Rams wide receiver Van Jefferson in the end zone to put the Commanders up 10-3.
For a second straight week, the offense had a slow start. Outside of Puka Nacua, they couldn’t find answers in the passing game. However, even Nacua took time to get going. With the Rams trailing, Nacua fumbled and the Commanders recovered at midfield.
That’s when Garrett and the defense took over. On the first play of the next drive, Daniels scrambled to his right and Garrett came in behind him and knocked the ball loose. Omar Speights recovered, giving the offense another chance to get points before the half. While the offense didn’t get in the end zone, Brandon McManus’ second field goal of the day made it 10-6.
Following the Commanders' opening touchdown, the Rams' defense went six straight drives without allowing a first down. That gave the offense the time it needed to get going. On the opening drive of the second half, Stafford hit Nacua on back-to-back plays and then it was Blake Corum who finished off the drive in the end zone to give the Rams their first lead of the day.
After Stafford threw an interception that led to the Commanders tying the game at 13, the Rams went right back to Nacua on the next drive. Stafford hit Nacua on 3rd-and-11 to convert one of their only third downs of the afternoon. Nacua’s 14th catch of the day made it 20-13 for the Rams as Stafford threw a perfect ball to the corner of the end zone.
Sunday’s game once again confirmed that the Rams have a need at wide receiver . Nacua finished with 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown. Outside of Nacua, the Rams got little production from their other receivers. Tutu Atwell had a drop, while he and Konata Mumpfield combined for four catches for 36 yards.
The defense remained stout for the Rams, closing out the game in the fourth quarter. Garrett sacked Daniels as the Commanders looked to answer the Rams. After Garrett jumped offside on 3rd-and-10, he sacked Daniels on the next play to make it 4th-and-17. Forbes then knocked away a pass intended for Jefferson to force a turnover on downs.
With the game on the line, the Commanders made it interesting, progressing to the Rams’ 31-yard line. On the final play, Byron Young recovered a loose ball as the Commanders attempted a series of laterals in a last-ditch effort to tie the game.
It was another imperfect win for the Rams. However, it’s their third straight as they improve to above .500 for the first time this season. The Rams leaned on their stars to win the game, and both Nacua and Garrett stepped up when needed.
This is a Rams team that has yet to truly reach its ceiling, but with Garrett back, it appears to be getting closer.. With a win against the Arizona Cardinals next week, the Rams would be 6-4 at their bye week and in a good spot heading into the second half of the season.

title: How Raiders Sticking To Plan in More Ways Than One
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders' 2026 season has been interesting, to say the least. After winning three games all of last season, the Raiders started this season 3-0. As much as the Raiders improved, few could have guessed they'd get off to the start they did.
Las Vegas' hot start to the season put them in a position early to potentially contend for a Wild Card spot in the playoffs. Most things seemed to be going the Raiders' way during their three-game winning streak, but four losses in the past five weeks have quickly changed things.
The Raiders sit at 4-5 this season, with games against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos up next on the schedule. They have struggled against teams with winning records this season, making another multi-game losing streak a legitimate possibility.
Las Vegas' struggles, combined with one of the league's toughest schedules, have highlighted the remaining holes on their roster. Yet those holes remain after an offseason in which the Raiders added significant talent and invested heavily on both sides of the ball.
The roster holes Las Vegas still needs to fill have been debilitating, but not unexpected. Given that the Raiders are still technically in the hunt for a Wild Card spot, and that it is early in Klint Kubiak's tenure, the Raiders appear to be staying the course in several regards.
Over nine games, the Raiders have clearly aimed to stick as close to their plan as possible. During the Raiders' losing streak, Kubiak made it clear that Las Vegas would stick with Kirk Cousins as the team's starting quarterback.
Las Vegas' defense has struggled mightily this season, especially against the league's top competition. After weeks of subpar defensive play, Kubiak also vouched for defensive coordinator Rob Leonard.
Kubiak noted that instead of firing one of his coordinators after a mad dash to put together a new coaching staff and sweeping roster changes, he plans to look for ways to improve upon what the coaching staff has already begun building.
“No, I don’t. In fact, I see us doing the things we said we were going to do better. Stand behind Rob [Leonard]. Stand behind our defensive staff. Stand behind our players,” Kubiak said on Monday.
"And I think the world wants someone’s head on a platter every time things don’t go right. But the way that I see it is that we brought people here for a reason, to get a job done and develop players for the long haul, and that’s where we’re going.”
Kubiak elaborated on why he has confidence in Leonard and the defense, despite the unit's obvious struggles. Kubiak noted that the defense has played well in spurts, but has struggled to play well for an entire game against elite competition.
"Because I see it – not to interrupt you, sorry – I see it work, just not for four quarters. And I have belief. I have belief in the scheme we run. I have belief in the coaches that run it. I have belief in our play caller,” Kubiak said.
“I have belief in the players that execute. But as a group, as coaches and as players, it’s putting four quarters of football together. No matter who the opponent, you play a damn good offense in San Francisco, there’s got to be a happy medium somewhere between that first half and second half.”
Whether it is their plan at quarterback or along their coaching staff, it was apparent from the start that the Raiders had a well-thought-out plan. It is becoming more apparent weekly that, with less than half the season left, Las Vegas' front office and coaching staff will stick closely to that plan.
However, with the coaching staff and roster moves the Raiders' front office made this offseason, and the fact that the team is unquestionably better than they were last season, they have every right to take that approach. They could use more talent on the roster, but that will have to come later.
Until then, Las Vegas must trust the players and coaches they invested in heavily this offseason. The Raiders are right where they should be at this point in their rebuild.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: LIVE: Raiders NFL Trade Deadline Tracker: Trades, Rumors, Latest News
full_text:
Time is running out for the Las Vegas Raiders to pull off a trade ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Since the start of the season, Las Vegas' front office has taken a solid approach every step of the way. It will be interesting to see whether the Raiders are active ahead of the deadline.
The Raiders have no shortage of roster needs they could address via trade. Yet a trade may not be in the team's best interest right now. This will be a critical assessment and decision for Las Vegas' front office. The roster needs improvement, but not if it could derail its current trajectory.
Las Vegas must choose between making a playoff push this season or preparing for the future. What they decide to do, or not do, at the deadline could indicate which one of those options the front office ultimately ended up choosing.
The Raiders are in their first season under largely new leadership on and off the field. Las Vegas' solid offseason helped set the ship in the right direction, but the season's first nine games proved the Raiders' roster needs significantly more help.
Despite several blowout losses over the past few weeks to elite teams, Kubiak noted that the players in the locker room do not view the team as being in a rebuild. Las Vegas has approached every game more prepared to compete than it has in recent seasons.
“I think one thing that I’m proud of is that we’re not talking about rebuilding. We’re talking about being in every game and winning every game. That’s how we treat it. We’re not looking at the future as coaches or players,” Kubiak said on Monday.
“You develop the future on the way, but every game we’re talking about winning that game. We are not satisfied with a rebuilding process, so that’s the mentality I want our players and coaches to have.”
The Raiders' Week 9 loss to the San Francisco 49ers was the latest in a handful of losses that have made their impressive start to the season merely an afterthought. Las Vegas once again started slow,  heading into halftime down by double digits.
Las Vegas has been down by double digits at halftime in three of its past five games, including a nine-point deficit in its Week 8 win over the New York Jets. Although the Raiders have improved since last season, that team was the league's worst. This Raiders team has higher goals and expectations.
“Anytime you don’t accomplish the goal, you’re frustrated and you’re upset. I think the frustrating part of yesterday is just the way we started the game. Can’t start that slow. Can’t start that sluggish versus an elite team,” Kubiak said.
“In the NFL, every week things change. And right here we sit at 4-5 with half the season left, with everything in front of us. So, as a team, we’re focusing on the next game.”
Heading into the trade deadline , few rumors have surfaced about the team's plans to pull off a trade. The Raiders are not shopping Kirk Cousins. Few trade rumors surround Las Vegas because there are not many possible trade scenarios.
Although Maxx Crosby and Jackson Powers-Johnson are solid trade pieces , little has been rumored about either player ahead of the deadline. Things could change quickly, especially regarding a potential trade for Cousins or Crosby. Kubiak shared his thoughts on the situation.
“We’re talking all the time. That hasn’t changed. As the deadline approaches, things get more urgent, and we’ll continue to talk," Kubiak said.
"That’s the business that we’re in. That’s the business of football, and those guys are veterans. They’ve been around that, so you just keep working. There’s a lot of things that are out of your control."
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: After Tough Road Loss, Raiders' Kubiak Still Maintains Belief
full_text:
After losing a game like the Las Vegas Raiders did to the San Francisco 49ers, there is always a great deal of frustration with the results.
The Raiders, nor any team, rarely win football games when they turn the ball over five times, including three interceptions from quarterback Kirk Cousins; star tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer each lost a fumble, while Las Vegas looked overwhelmed against the might of the 49ers' offense and defense.
Yet in defeat, head coach Klint Kubiak understands the process ahead and the mission for long-term success in Sin City.
Kubiak isn't shy about hiding his feelings about matters of the team. Right now, the Raiders do not have enough to compete with and beat the best teams in the league. Again, turnovers and slow starts have hurt them this season against the two best teams in the NFC West, among other opponents.
The biggest catalyst so far has been the defense, which is the worst in the NFL through nine games in multiple statistical categories. The Raiders spent a massive amount of money rebuilding the unit, and in most cases, changes would come.
Kubiak suggests otherwise, standing alongside defensive coordinator Rob Leonard in the process.
"In fact, I see us doing the things we said we were going to do better," Kubiak said. "Stand behind Rob [Leonard]. Stand behind our defensive staff. Stand behind our players. And I think the world wants someone’s head on a platter every time things don’t go right. But the way that I see it is that we brought people here for a reason, to get a job done and develop players for the long haul, and that’s where we’re going."
The Raiders have continued to show no signs of making major changes at the three levels of the defense. They are in a rebuild, committed to it, and steadfast in their approach.
Kubiak continued to explain that he sees the process working, but he also says they must put four quarters of football together, something they have struggled with all season long.
"Because I see it — not to interrupt you, sorry — I see it work, just not for four quarters," Kubiak said. "And I have belief. I have belief in the scheme we run. I have belief in the coaches that run it. I have belief in our play caller. I have belief in the players that execute."
"But as a group, as coaches and as players, it’s putting four quarters of football together. No matter who the opponent, you play a damn good offense in San Francisco, there’s got to be a happy medium somewhere between that first half and second half."
As the Raiders continue to find their footing in the second half of the season, Sunday was an example that, while things may look bad often throughout the year against quality opponents, the team continues to fight and put up a good fight against them while learning how to win in the process.

title: 3 Buzzer-Beater Moves Raiders Could Make at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders are in an interesting spot with a 4-5 record heading into Week 10.
With the NFL trade deadline looming - Tuesday at 4:00 p.m. ET - the Raiders are one of the most intriguing teams to keep tabs on in the final hours before the window closes. With that in mind, here are a few moves general manager John Spytek could orchestrate.
After what transpired on Monday night, it further proved the obvious: the Vikings need to acquire a quarterback. Minnesota is 6-2 and would be a legitimate contender with a reliable signal caller. At this point, Cousins and Daniel Jones seem to be the most realistic options for the Vikings to consider.
Las Vegas is not shopping Cousins, but if the right offer comes to the table, you would have to think the front office would at least consider it. While I've been a proponent of sending Cousins elsewhere for draft capital, I don't think the Raiders should just give away the 38-year-old quarterback. If Minnesota shows its desperation and offers a second-round pick, that deal should happen.
While Las Vegas is on the precipice of the wild card, it's difficult to envision it reaching the postseason with the upcoming schedule. The Raiders face the Seahawks and Broncos in the next two weeks. It would be a tough pill to swallow and essentially punt on those aspirations, but this is the time to capitalize and sell Crosby at his highest value.
Over the last few years, we've seen Jerry Jones overpay for players at the trade deadline. The Cowboys owner has said multiple times this season that he's always looking to improve the team. It wouldn't shock me in the slightest if Dallas offers a first-round pick plus for the two-time All-Pro pass rusher. The Raiders need to look in the mirror and acknowledge that this roster is several pieces away from competing for the playoffs. Two weeks from now, the Raiders could be out of the conversation.
This hypothetical move makes sense for both scenarios: pushing for the playoffs or looking forward to 2027. While I've said the Raiders are multiple pieces away from a roster built to contend for a playoff spot, the playoffs are certainly not out of the question. On the other hand, acquiring Thomas Jr. could also provide Las Vegas with a legitimate wide receiver for the future.
Thomas just turned 24 in October and produced over 1,200 receiving yards in his rookie season. If the Raiders can land the 2024 first-round pick for a second- or third-round pick, Spytek should pull the trigger.
