title: 3 Vikings Studs & 2 Duds After Getting Hammered by Bills on MNF in Week 9
full_text:
After a perfect start to the year, the Vikings lost their second game of the season on Monday Night Football. It was a low-scoring affair and the Bills were in control of the game while the Purple and Gold struggled to do anything offensively.
The 23-6 loss was another in a long line of prime-time embarrassments for the Vikings. Under the lights at U.S. Bank Stadium, Minnesota couldn't execute offensively under quarterback Carson Wentz at all, never entering the red zone or converting on third or fourth down with him under center.
Minnesota might still be 6-2 this season, but this game highlighted the major issues this team will face as it continues to play through the challenging schedule. The fact that Minnesota was on offense for 17:28 of the 60:00 says everything that fans need to know about this game.
Yes, Justin Jefferson caught only three passes on the day, though the ball was thrown his way 11 times; however, so many of those passes were either off-target or uncatchable. Still, he finished with 58 receiving yards, the most on the team.
The Vikings are lucky to have a player like Jefferson, who could be extremely vocal about the team's offensive struggles. Instead, he has been professional and chooses his words wisely when talking about his team or speaking with the media.
The fans watching the Vikings at home in prime time didn't hold back from voicing their displeasure over Wentz's play. Watching his passes consistently sail off target was frustrating while watching the defense work so hard. He even threw a backward pass recovered by Buffalo and was credited with a fumble on that play.
Wentz was benched in the fourth quarter but finished eight-for-25, throwing the ball, completing 32% of his passes for 81 yards and two interceptions. His abysmal play resulted in an 8.9 quarterback rating
Carson Wentz had SO MANY open receivers He tried throwing an interception instead 💀 pic.twitter.com/KT77EpHbVC
This should be a wake-up call for the Vikings' front office to see whether the team can get a deal done for a quarterback before the trade deadline.
The Vikings trailed during the entire game, which led to Minnesota running the ball only 11 times with their running backs. That is a shame, since Jordan Mason gained 35 yards on six carries, an average of 5.8 yards per rushing attempt.
Mason helped out as a receiver as well. He caught two of three targets for seven yards despite frustrating quarterback play. When a passer is having as bad a night as Wentz did, having him throw the ball 25 times compared to 11 runs from running backs seems like a terrible idea.
Although he was solid as a return man, Myles Price didn't do much to help the team offensively. He had four passes thrown his way and hauled in one of them for six yards, which was, sadly. enough to be the fifth-most for Minnesota on the night.
He was called for an unnecessary false start penalty in the second quarter that pushed an offense that was already struggling to pick up a first down back five yards. He also bailed out on a fumble during a kickoff return in the first quarter. Thankfully, tight end Ben Yurosek came up with the football to prevent the turnover.
Blake Cashman got banged up during the game, but worked out his shoulder on the sidelines and returned to action. He has been an essential piece of the defense this entire season, and he continued to show his value against Buffalo.
Blake Cashman is not a happy camper as he heads to the blue medical tent. pic.twitter.com/p0y0hlsBf9
There wasn't much that Cashman didn't do in this game. He led the Vikings with 12 tackles, including one for a loss. He also defended two passes against Josh Allen and the Bills, proving he can do whatever defensive coordinator Brian Flores asks of him.

title: Vikings Offense Nonexistent in 23-6 Loss to Bills: Here Are 3 Things That Mattered Most as the Trade Deadline Looms
full_text:
MINNEAPOLIS, MN — The 6-1 Vikings officially made their 2026 prime-time debut Monday night with the chance to prove all of their doubters and skeptics wrong against the mighty Buffalo Bills. With Carson Wentz set to start for an injured Kyler Murray, concerns swirling around the offense, and the trade deadline approaching Tuesday afternoon , the stakes could not be higher.
Would the matchup be a repeat of the legendary battle of 2022? Would this game prove the Vikings can contend as constructed? Nope. Instead, fans at home and at U.S. Bank Stadium were treated to one of the worst offensive performances imaginable .
Here’s what happened and how it may impact Nolan Teasley’s trade deadline plans.
I, like many others, thought Carson Wentz might inject some life into the Vikings offense , but boy, was I wrong. Wentz put together an abysmal performance from start to finish. He ended the day 8 of 25 with 81 yards and two interceptions in a performance that looked like he had never played quarterback in the NFL before.
Justin Jefferson kept calm but looked visibly frustrated on the sidelines. Wentz had emphasized his plans to get the ball to Jefferson during the week, but failed at nearly every opportunity. Jefferson ended with only three receptions for 58 yards.
Justin Jefferson deserves better. pic.twitter.com/Yduepzi30M
The reality is simple: Kevin O’Connell promised a deep quarterback room this past offseason, and the resulting product has been one of the worst passing attacks in the NFL. There may not be a QB upgrade available at the deadline, but Teasley needs to call just about every team in the league to leave no stone unturned. If no one bites, his focus must turn to the offseason.
"I'll defer to Nolan [Vikings GM] on that." Kevin O'Connell on if he has given any thought to acquiring a QB before the trade deadline. pic.twitter.com/lJb8BOMLJj
The Vikings defense put together another stellar performance for most of the first half before the lack of help from the offense eventually caught up. Sound familiar? The game followed an almost eerily similar flow to last week’s game in Detroit, with a strong defensive effort being totally wasted. Flores’ blitz-heavy squad brought Josh Allen down four times and held one of the best offenses in the league to 23 points.
BYRON MURPHY PICKS IT OFF IN THE END ZONE BUFvsMIN on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pJikc7Dtdj
Buffalo absolutely dominated time of possession, holding the ball for a whopping 42.5 minutes.
Flores and his defense can only do so much while the offense is completely unable to sustain drives or score. Trading for any defensive player would not help the ultimate issue unless it is part of a flurry of moves that dramatically help the offense.
This game was further proof that the now 6-2 Vikings are further from contention than many had hoped when they stood as the league’s last undefeated team just a couple of weeks ago, and the offense is the reason why. Nolan Teasley’s June hiring leaves us all with significant questions about how he views this roster. The fact that Minnesota’s first-round pick Caleb Banks was listed as a healthy scratch only raises further concerns. It would make total sense if Teasley looked at this offense and decided it needs far more help than the trade deadline can provide.
Kevin O’Connell must find playoff success soon. With multiple key defenders set to be free agents and no long-term stability at QB, it’s fair to wonder just how much longer he’ll have to get it done if he’s unable to do so in year five. If this team wants to make a run, O’Connell may need to convince Teasley to mortgage the future to do so.

title: Vikings Report Card Week 9: Grading Every Position After an Ugly 23-6 Loss to the Bills
full_text:
Well, the trade deadline should be interesting.
The Vikings—in classic Vikings fashion—were dominant on defense and abysmal on offense in their 23-6 loss to Buffalo. It was more of the same Monday night after a similar game in Detroit, and the Vikings are left searching for answers after falling to 6-2. The game was both beautiful and tortuous, but ultimately the Bills came out with the win.
Let's get into some grades from the tough loss.
Carson Wentz might as well have played with his left hand after finishing 8-for-25, with 81 yards and two interceptions. The Vikings quarterback carousel continues, as it's clear that Wentz isn't taking anybody's job moving forward. Obviously, the performance warrants some attention at the trade deadline, although there aren't many needle movers available. This is just a mess on all levels.
Jordan Mason was actually averaging a solid 5.8 yards per carry, so naturally Kevin O'Connell and the Vikings completely ignored the run game for much of the contest. By the time the Vikings might have considered it, the game had slipped away. Could the Vikings still add at the deadline here?
It's hard to judge what you don't see, and the Vikings pass catchers were simply never given a chance to make an impact. Justin Jefferson finally saw double-digit targets--if you can even call them that--but was only able to haul in three of them. Odell Beckham Jr. was promoted to the 53-man roster for reasons beyond human understanding, and finished with zeros across the board.
T.J. Hockenson reeled in a few passes, but for the most part the tight end position was quiet on the night. He had been a favorite target of Kyler Murray, but it seems that connection isn't as strong with Wentz. It's been reported the Vikings have looked at adding another blocking tight end by the deadline. Time will tell.
The run game was decent and the line only allowed two sacks. There have been rumblings that the Vikings are still looking to add on the interior, but offensive line should be the least of their worries with the issues elsewhere.
First-round pick Caleb Banks was a surprise healthy scratch, but it likely had more to do with the game plan to stop the run than an indictment on his overall standing with the franchise. The plan worked for the most part for the Vikings defense as James Cook was held to just 3.5 yards per carry, but eventually the wheels fell off after getting no help from the offense.
The Vikings' linebackers and edge players are some of the best in football and it showed again against the No. 1 offense in the league. Sacks were coming from every direction as the Vikings got to Josh Allen four times. Andrew Van Ginkel almost had the play of the night on a near strip-sack at the one-yard line. You just have to wonder how the game would've played out had that play stood.
The Vikings' secondary held Allen in check for the most part, including a key interception in the first half from Byron Murphy Jr. A few busted coverages allowed the Bills some points, but it's also hard to fault a defense that has to stay on the field for 40 minutes a game.
Will Reichard was perfect again, and even Brett Thorson had an incredible punt downed at the one-yard line. Once again, this unit was the only source of scoring for a Vikings team that appears to be allergic to touchdowns.

title: Breece Hall Isn’t the Jets RB That the Vikings Need to Trade For
full_text:
Time is running out for the Vikings to make a trade . The deadline to get a deal done is Tuesday at 3 p.m CT, so if the general manager, Nolan Teasley, wants to add some talent to the roster, they need to act quickly .
Running back has been a position that has received a lot of trade buzz for the Vikings. Players like Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, Titans rusher Tony Pollard, and Breece Hall of the New York Jets were at the top of many fans' wish lists.
However, there is one player who might provide a long-term answer at running back for Minnesota who hasn't received a lot of attention, and that is Braelon Allen, a fourth-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
The 22-year-old running back would be a fantastic future investment for the Vikings. Allen would immediately become a major part of Minnesota's running back rotation and would create a dynamic duo with Jordan Mason.
When Hall suffered a quadriceps injury in Week 3 against the Detroit Lions, Allen stepped in as the Jets' starter. Hall returned in Week 9, seeing 19 opportunities (15 carries, four targets) across 27 offensive snaps, while Allen saw 10 (eight carries, two targets) despite playing 10 more snaps than his counterpart.
During the five-week stretch when Hall didn't suit up, Allen ran wild on the opposition. He carried the ball 93 times for 504 yards and two touchdowns. His 5.42 yards-per-carry average is exceptional, and his 80.4 Pro Football Focus grade ranks him ninth out of 51 qualifying halfbacks this season.
Allen has forced 27 missed tackles this season while averaging 3.7 yards after contact. His blend of speed and elusiveness, combined with his age and experience, makes him an interesting player to attempt to acquire.
Recently, the Jets have made it clear they have no intention of trading Hall. ESPN Senior NFL Insider Adam Schefter shared that information in a Sunday X post, adding that New York have received calls about his availability.
Despite interest and calls, the Jets have told teams they don’t intend to trade running back Breece Hall. pic.twitter.com/DKUmVY8CYe
If the Jets aren't willing to trade Hall, the next logical choice is for the Vikings to pursue Allen, who carries a $1.3 million cap hit in 2027 . New York will have to pay him soon, but it already handed out a $45.75 million extension to Hall back in May, so Gang Green might not want to hand out another big RB contract so soon.
Now that New York has Hall back from injury, they may be more inclined to part ways with their backup running back. He is playing like a running back who deserves a much more significant role than the Jets can offer, so why shouldn't the Vikings swoop in and save him?

title: Vikings Face More Trade Deadline Obstacles After Jaguars Add Jordan Davis
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is officially less than 24 hours away , leaving general manager Nolan Teasley with limited time to address the Vikings' biggest needs. While finding another running back or bolstering the offensive line depth would make a good chunk of fans happy , most want to see Minnesota improve its run defense by adding a reliable defensive tackle.
Although their defensive unit as a whole has been among the NFL's best this season, the Vikings are still allowing 116.7 rushing yards per game (16th-most). Recent struggles against star RBs have played a role in that lack of success, as the Purple and Gold have allowed 146.3 rushing yards in their last three contests, which is the fifth-most league-wide during that stretch.
With more opposing elite running backs on the horizon, shoring up the middle of the defense is something Teasley can't ignore. Unfortunately, that goal might be easier said than done.
The deadline isn't here, but it's starting to feel like the Vikings didn't strike while the iron was hot in the DT market.
For example, the last two weeks have seen star DTs Jeffery Simmons and DeForest Buckner traded to the Bears and 49ers, respectively. Then, on Monday, the Jaguars bolstered their D-line by acquiring Davon Godchaux from the Saints, only to acquire Jordan Davis from the Eagles just a few hours later.
Blockbuster: the Jaguars are trading a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis, sources tell ESPN. This is the Jaguars’ third trade for a defensive player today while the Eagles now are poised to have 10 picks in the… pic.twitter.com/NTGnLf2MoT
That's one less option for a market that is seemingly not as active as some DT-needy teams would like.
According to NFL on Prime 's James Palmer, trading for a new defensive tackle will be difficult for any team, not just the Vikings.
" Teams looking to acquire (DT) have had a hard time and feel options are limited ," Palmer reported on Monday morning. "The Eagles have told teams they aren't moving Moro Ojomo , and the Colts so far have been reluctant to trade Grover Stewart. Teams continue to search the market and checked in on Panthers Derrick Brown and were quickly shot down."
Obviously, nothing is guaranteed in the NFL, and general managers' minds can be changed with the right offer. That said, it looks like the Vikings might need to truly leave no stone unturned if they're going to improve their DT situation in the coming hours.
With the top available DTs getting scooped up and the rest seemingly off-limits, it's easy to see the new obstacle that the Vikings face. Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange are young with bright futures ahead of them, but they might not be good enough in the present to prevent the run from being exploited in the playoffs.
That's especially true when looking at Minnesota's upcoming stretch. They'll face star RBs James Cook, Christian McCaffrey, and Bijan Robinson in three of the next four games, each boasting enough talent to fill the holes along the Vikings' interior with regret. So, where do they look next?
The Jets are positioned to be sellers and have DTs on expiring contracts who could help, including ex-Viking Harrison Phillips and former 2024 seventh-rounder Jowon Briggs. The winless Chargers are a disaster and might be convinced to part ways with Dalvin Tomlinson. Or perhaps the Vikings should contact the Cardinals about potentially acquiring Roy Lopez.
Either way, the Vikings' time is running out to address one of their top trade deadline needs. Even if he can't successfully land a game-changer, exploring the market and exhausting every avenue is key for Teasley if he wants to avoid being run all over in the postseason, if not sooner.

title: Why I Fully Trust Vikings GM Nolan Teasley Ahead of the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is just 24 hours away, and for the Vikings, it could have a lasting impact for years to come.
Over the last few weeks, the Vikings have been rumored to be looking for a running back, tight end, offensive line, defensive line, and Bigfoot—even a quarterback. How much of that was just due diligence versus legitimate inquiries isn't clear, but at 6-1, general manager Nolan Teasley will have some big decisions to make after Monday Night Football.
Regardless of the outcome against Buffalo (barring some serious injuries), Minnesota will still be squarely in the mix for a top seed in the NFC. In most cases, 7-1 or 6-2 at the deadline would trigger some serious buying, but the Vikings aren't like most teams: their potential needs and unusual front office construction may lead to some problems.
Teasley wasn't brought on until after the NFL Draft, and hasn't been able to make much of an impact on the roster outside of some late-summer signings and around 874 practice squad moves. The deadline would provide him that opportunity, but it would mean having to part with 2027 draft picks before he's even sat in the Vikings' war room.
That situation almost guarantees that the Vikings' first-round pick, or picks valuing a first, won't be on the move. That also means no Jonathan Taylor (womp womp). Really, while the logic for not doing the top-tier trade seems potentially flawed, it's likely for the best. The 2026 defense would be a terrible thing to waste, but the number of question marks for the 2027 squad is virtually limitless.
It seems likely that next year's quarterback isn't on the roster, and the Vikings will have to find one in free agency or the draft. Almost half the starting defense needs new deals (or not), with key players like Andrew Van Ginkel, Blake Cashman, Jalen Redmond and Isaiah Rodgers all on expiring contracts. On offense, Jordan Mason, Aaron Jones Sr. and T.J. Hockenson could all be on the move, and Justin Jefferson's patience may only last so long .
Bringing back even half of those guys would take some serious cash, and the Vikings will need some rookies to come in and contribute right away. There's certainly a world where Minnesota stays competitive in 2027, but given aging, high-priced free agents and an empty silhouette at the most important position in sports, it's reasonable to expect the Vikings to face a steeper hill to climb next season.
As frustrating as it will be to see the Vikings nickel and dime their way through the trade deadline, 2027 is already shaping up to be a huge challenge, and adding more pressure on top of the current issues isn't a path Teasley will be willing to venture down.
Obviously, the counterpoint is that the defense is the best in the NFL this year; defensive coordinator Brian Flores could leave after the season, and adding Taylor, or even a deal for a quarterback, would all but ensure the Vikings did everything they could to make it happen in 2026. It's not every year you start 6-1, but it probably doesn't take long to see that the Vikings have punched above their weight.
The combined record against non-NFC North opponents is 9-25, and while the Vikings shouldn't apologize for winning, you could argue the real team will be revealed in November, with the peaking Packers and juggernaut 49ers up next.
It's rare for the head coach and GM to be on different timelines, and Teasley will be tempted to push the chips into the center of 2026 for an all-out sprint to a Lombardi. Still, he knows that finding elevators at quarterback or running at this point in the game won't come cheap, and overpaying to land them could send the Vikings down the Colts' current unfortunate path just a year after their all-in push.
Managing risk will be the name of the game for Teasley, and while I expect him to add some pieces at the deadline, the splash move won't happen. Whether that's enough to appease fans will be a different story, but improving a bit at the deadline while maintaining at least some flexibility in 2027 is the prudent decision.

title: Vikings’ Present and Future Could Be Defined in Final Stretch Before Trade Deadline
full_text:
If this Vikings season hasn’t had enough drama and intrigue for your liking, this week may finally deliver the adrenaline rush you’ve been chasing.
To say Monday night’s matchup with the Bills and the impact it may have on Tuesday’s 4 p.m. ET trade deadline carry massive implications would be putting it lightly. Are the Vikings truly contenders? Is general manager Nolan Teasley willing to bet it all on a roster he didn't build? Vikings fans and the NFL world at large will get their answers soon.
Let’s break down what’s at stake for a Vikings team looking to embrace the now while planning for the future.
The eyes of the nation will be focused on Minnesota’s battle with Buffalo on Monday Night as the Vikings are set to make their 2026 primetime debut. Leading the way? Carson Wentz, whose last primetime performance came against the Chargers in 2025 and ended in season-ending surgery. Safe to say, Wentz is looking for a much better ending .
Luckily, the Bills’ pass defense should give him plenty of chances to find his star wideouts.
Need to be more consistent in staying on the field and keeping our defense off the field. pic.twitter.com/juk6uh2ycQ
The Vikings will be desperate to prove they belong in contention conversations after an atrocious showing from their offense in Detroit last week. The defense, meanwhile, will look to secure its title as the league’s best unit against a stellar Josh Allen-led offense. But what happens if the offense puts up another dud while the defense shines, whether win or lose?
With some of the team’s best defenders set to hit free agency after this season, Teasley’s trade deadline actions, or lack thereof, may tell the team everything they need to know.
It seems clear to most outside observers that the current model of winning isn’t sustainable, especially as other contenders around the league are already loading up for postseason runs . Eventually, your offense will need to step up and win games, and Monday may be the perfect chance to prove it can. If not, the fanbase and team will be watching Teasley's decisions before Tuesday’s deadline closely.
Make no mistake, the right series of moves could set the 2026 Vikings up for a legitimate run at the Super Bowl. An elite defense, an elite receiver in his prime, talented veterans set to hit free agency, and two of the league's best playcallers. For many, this is enough to go all in on this season and ignore the future.
After all, how often does a team start 6-1?  But for Teasley, the implications go far beyond the now.
It’s important to remember that Teasley was hired more than a month after the draft, an almost unheard-of timeline for a GM hire. With almost no say on the current roster, an impending mess of contracts, salary cap issues, and the desperate need for a quarterback , does it make sense for Teasley to eliminate much-needed draft capital?
The answer to that question depends fully on another: Does the first-year GM see this Vikings team as a contender or pretender?
Teasley is fresh off a Super Bowl victory as the assistant GM in Seattle, so he certainly knows a thing or two about constructing a championship roster. If he goes all in for a splash move (or two) at the deadline, we’ll know he sees the potential for the Vikings to make a run. If he doesn’t, we’ll know his focus is on the future. But the potential fallout of another season without a playoff win could carry massive weight for two of the most important people in the building.
Kevin O’Connell is the first coach since Jay Gruden in 2018 to enter his fifth season without a postseason victory. While O’Connell is beloved by ownership, fans, and players, a potential roster reset may make it even harder for him to find playoff success anytime soon. This begs the question: how long is too long for fans and ownership?
There’s also the Justin Jefferson factor. The wideout is in year seven of his NFL career, with a 0-2 playoff record to show for it. While Jefferson remains the epitome of a selfless leader through adversity, his focus is clearly on winning a championship above all else. At what point does he see that happening elsewhere?
"I feel like we should win every game. That's just the mindset, that's the expectations that I have every time I step foot out there on the field." - @JJettas2 pic.twitter.com/EQkg3esiKu
Needless to say, the Vikings’ performance on Monday Night and the weight of trade deadline decisions could define this team for years to come. Let’s hope Teasley is, in fact, the right man to steer the ship.

title: Vikings Could Be Sneaky Winners From Eagles Benching Tanner McKee in Week 9
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings are surprising a lot of people by winning games this year. Their 6-1 start to the season is making many fans wonder if the team could be contenders for a deep playoff run this season.
One issue facing the Vikings entering Week 9 is the quarterback position. Minnesota has not gotten stellar play out of former Arizona Cardinals quarterback Kyler Murray, who is set to miss time for the second time this season due to injury .
Carson Wentz will once again step in as the starter, but his backup for the Monday Night Football contest against the Buffalo Bills will be Max Brosmer. The Purple and Gold could use more depth and future potential on the quarterback depth chart.
The Philadelphia Eagles are having a bad season. On Sunday, Philly lost their seventh game of the season. And with the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, they could be receptive to trading a player like quarterback Tanner McKee.
McKee isn't going to beat out Murray or Wentz, but he would raise the floor of the quarterback room and provide head coach Kevin O'Connell with a passer to develop while his veterans start games this season.
Standing 6-foot-6 and weighing 231 pounds, McKee was a sixth-round pick of the Eagles in 2023. The 26-year-old quarterback started three games for Philadelphia this year, completing 63.2% of his passes and throwing two touchdowns with two interceptions.
More interestingly, McKee averaged 212.7 passing yards per game in those three games. That is significantly more than Murray's 170.3 passing yards per game since joining the Vikings. The potential is there for him to grow into a quality backup.
Philadelphia head coach Nick Sirianni benched McKee after the Eagles went 0-3 with the young quarterback at the helm. The team opted to start Joe Milton on Sunday against the Giants, which resulted in another loss.
Trading for McKee likely wouldn't cost much. He is in the final year of his rookie contract and is set to become an unrestricted free agent at the end of this season. The Eagles would likely love to get an asset in return for him instead of allowing him to walk in free agency.
While the Eagles seem content to move on from McKee, the Vikings should be interested. While this wouldn't be the blockbuster trade that many fans of Minnesota are hoping for, it would be a solid move to show that the franchise is serious about this season and the future of the quarterback position .

title: Patriots Trade Deadline Tracker: Every Nugget, Rumor and Deal for New England On Final Day
full_text:
The NFL's trade deadline was pushed back a week this year, so the New England Patriots and 31 other teams will have until Nov. 10 to try and get deals done this season.
The Patriots , currently sitting at 5-3 and in second place in the AFC East, could end up being active on the market. Injuries across the board and potential depth issues at other places could led Eliot Wolf and Mike Vrabel to try and improve the team somehow, someway.
Aleady in this calendar year, the Patriots have made a few trades. Back in March, they shipped away Garrett Bradbury and Marte Mapu before acquiring A.J. Brown in a block buster deal with the Philadelphia Eagles three months later. During the summer, Kayshon Boutte was dealth to the Houston Texans and during roster cuts, the Patriots also sent draft picks for Corey Kiner and Walter Rouse.
So could they end up making a deal mid-season? Here's all the rumors, quotes and storylines that are surrounding the Patriots as the trade deadline looms.
Considering how banged up the Patriots' wide receiver room is, names like Brian Thomas Jr. were tossed around as potential options via trade. On Tuesday, that door was shut. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Jacksonville Jaguars won't be moving the 2024 first round pick.
This season, Thomas has slid down on the Jags' depth chart, recording just 10 receptions for 117 yards and one touchdown. The Patriots could have used his abilities to help replace the hole left by A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder). Instead, they'd need to pivot elsewhere.
One day before the trade deadline, Vrabel was asked about adding some pieces after injuries continue to hurt the Patriots. Against the Green Bay Packers , they lost Rhamondre Stevenson, Ben Brown, Brenden Schooler and Carlton Davis to injuries, along with some other players that got banged up.
Vrabel's tune the last few weeks hasn't changed when it comes to making a deal: If it helps the team, they'll think about it.
"I want to see us do anything that we can with the roster that we have or potentially guys that aren't here, to continue to improve," he said. "That's the focus here after nine weeks. We played some really good games, have been competitive, and then other days where it just wasn't good enough as a whole."
The Patriots signed Carlton Davis last year to a three-year deal, but his name has now been thrown around in deals two years in. The veteran cornerback, who's missed several games with a neck injury, could be on the move — according to SI's Albert Breer.
"This is about the age of the team and if you look at the roster big picture," Breer said . "They’ve gotten older at a lot of key spots and they aren’t exactly flush with draft capital over the next couple of years. ... They’re going to have to find a way over the next, three, four, five years to make the roster younger particularly after they pay Drake Maye. They’re trying to creatively look at this."
Davis has been the Patriots' most physical cornerback when he's healthy, but the 29-year-old is one of the older players on the roster. The Patriots could try and offload both his playing abilities and his expensive contract for a chance to get younger in the secondary.
The Patriots have a lot of money tied up to the interior of their defense line, with Milton Williams ($28.5 million) and Christian Barmore ($17.1 million) being paid very well for this season. But Barmore, who's played just 41.9% of the snaps this season, hasn't been someone that's been a consistent player so far.
According to Breer , the defensive tackle "could be had" on the trade market after falling behind Cory Durden on the depth chart. Barmore has two more years after this season on his four-year, $84 million extension he signed in 2024 before hitting the open market.
This season, the 27-year-old has six total tackles, three sacks and a forced fumble.
Could the Patriots — the team with Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on injured reserve — end up adding a wideout? ESPN reported that Indianapolis Colts wideout Josh Downs requested a trade after a pair of his teammates were shipped away on Tuesday.
Downs spent two seasons with Drake Maye at North Carolina, scoring a career-high 11 touchdowns during the 2022 season. The Patriots only have four healthy wide receivers on the active roster right now, but adding Downs for what could be a cheap deal might help elevate the passing attack.
Seven games in, Downs has 26 receptions for 307 yards.
A few days after the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears , Vrabel spoke with reporters about how the team is stacking up prior to their Week 8 game with the Miami Dolphins. One of the questions posed was about if the Patriots will be active on the phones.
His answer left the door open for a deal being made, but the head coach also didn't officially dig a potential move into the sand. Like most coach-speak, Vrabel discussed how the Patriots would make moves to try and improve the overall roster in totality, and not try to single out a certain spot that needs upgrading.
"We're going to try to do everything we can to help the team," Vrabel said. "I don't know if we will or we won't. I would imagine that we'll try to do everything that we can to help us, within reason, and makes sense for us. I don't know how you want to interpret that, but I'm sure we'll listen and talk, just like everybody else does."
Some positions that the Patriots could end up attacking are running back, offensive guard (with a myriad of injuries hitting that group), interior defensive line and some backup cornerbacks.

title: Patriots Should Be in RB Trade Market With Stevenson, Henderson Out
full_text:
Injuries have defined the first nine weeks of the New England Patriots season that's seen five wins and four losses. In the past few days, another position group suffered major losses, which is something New England will have to address.
Last week, TreVeyon Henderson took to social media to announce that he had been hospitalized with a neurological condition. While the team nor Henderson has shared how long he's expected to be out, the second-year running back is still on the Patriots active roster.
🙏🏽 pic.twitter.com/l52XuixPOc
Additionally, a report came out Monday night that running back Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a plantoris tendon issue in the back of his knee, meaning he'll be sidelined for several weeks — including the team's Week 10 game in Germany and their bye one week later..
That leaves New England with running backs Corey Kiner and Lan Larison, as well as Terrell Jennings on the practice squad.
Prior to the news about Henderson and Stevenson, the Patriots might have been in talks of acquiring a running back before the 4 p.m. trade deadline on Nov. 10. Now, the discussion for the Patriots to purchase a running back vamps up for a team looking to field a more competitive offense.
On Monday, Mike Vrabel spoke to repoters about the plans heading into the deadline.
"I want to see us do anything that we can with the roster that we have or potentially guys that aren't here, to continue to improve," he said.
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has brought an emergence of talented running backs not seen at a trade deadline before. The group of rushers available for teams to inquire about is much stronger than year's past, which presents a great opportunity for the Patriots to upgrade their roster ahead of the second half of the season.
The biggest name available is Jonathan Taylor of the Indianapolis Colts. Taylor is an accomplished running back, who has notched four 1,000-plus yard seasons. Whatever team acquires Taylor will see an immediate impact from the seventh-year veteran.
New England has emerged as favorites for Taylor across several sports books and internet discussions. After the Colts loss to Dallas on Sunday, Taylor seemingly gave his farewells to Indianapolis in his post-game media availability.
One downside for New England is that Taylor carries an average cap hit of $17 million during the next two seasons, which will be difficult for the Patriots to afford. Taylor is also one of the most expensive players at the deadline, meaning the Patriots will have to fork up a valuable player and at least a day two pick.
#Colts RB Jonathan Taylor gave a farewell to Indianapolis and Colts fans after today’s game, in case it was his last with the organization. Don’t see this often. (🎥 @WISHNews8 ) pic.twitter.com/n4uf3C3W7f
There are much cheaper options that provide a similar —  though less — impact as Taylor. Derrick Henry is another trade candidate that Vrabel will certainly be interested in. Henry and Vrabel have ties from their time in Tennessee together, and the long-time NFL running back brings a powerful downfield attack that the Patriots offense could use.
Henry is a part of a Baltimore Ravens team that is without its starting and backup quarterbacks. They're the last place team in the AFC North and may be looking to plan for upcoming seasons under new head coach Jesse Minter.
However, a different Titans running back could be on New England's radar, as Tony Pollard presents an opportunity for the Patriots to upgrade their running back room. Pollard is on an expiring contract and has been an efficient rusher this year, on pace for over 1,000 yards from scrimmage and 12 touchdowns.
The eighth-year running back has five seasons of 1,000-plus yards and is a shifty runner with great vision. Due to Pollard's age and his rental status, New England could acquire this Titans player for a low value.
There are other options that the Patriots and executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf could explore. If the team is looking for more depth or a temporary replacement while Stevenson and Henderson get healthy, there's a few names with less than $1 million remaining on their contract that could fill the position.
ELIOT WOLF HAS APPARENTLY PUT IN THE BEST OFFER FOR JONATHAN TAYLOR. 👀👀👀👀👀👀 pic.twitter.com/o9W7VpMFpD
The Giants, who are currently in first place in the NFC North, have an abundance of running backs dealing with a multitude of injuries. Devin Singletary is a veteran name with a minimal contract that the Patriots could pursue.
The Jaguars, who have been very active in trade talks, may want to move on from Ameer Abdullah. There's also Isaiah Davis of the Jets, who finds himself third on New York's depth chart.
Being the most injured team in the NFL, the Patriots will look to improve several position groups ahead of the trade deadline, but it remains to be seen which areas will be most prominently addressed.

title: Patriots Must Trade for WR After Embarrassing Loss to Packers (And Here's Why)
full_text:
Just about everything went wrong for the New England Patriots on Sunday, who dropped a 45-27 game against the Green Bay Packers —  in part, due to four costly turnovers.
With the NFL trade deadline approaching, the Patriots may look at other team's rosters to turn around the lack of success they've experienced the last three weeks.
On Monday, Mike Vrabel said that Sunday's performance wouldn't change how aggressive New England would be at the trade deadline, but also shared in his media availability that, "we gotta start putting ourselves in a position to start playing meaningful games in January."
Currently sitting at 5-4, the Patriots are on the brink of being a playoff team, with many challenging opponents ahead. To secure a spot playing "meaningful games in January," New England will have to find a way to revamp an injury-riddled and underperforming roster.
In Sunday's loss to Green Bay, the larger issues centered around turnovers, unsuccessful pass defense , and an inability to protect the quarterback. However, one piece of information many are forgetting to discuss is the underwhelming performances from Patriots wide receivers.
On Sunday, Drake Maye targeted his wide receivers 24 times and only completed 13 of those passes. Certain passes, like Maye's interception to Evan Williams on pass intended for Kyle Williams, were catchable balls that the receiver couldn't come down with.
Additionally, the four sacks allowed are the most the third-year quarterback has taken all season. The Packers weren't able to apply quick pressure on Maye; but rather, the pocket collapsed before any receivers could find openings.
Fox's coverage of Sunday's game pointed to multiple angles where receivers were unable to find separation from their defenders or a break in the zone defense.
Not excusing the turnovers they’re a massive issue but it’s astounding the level of difficulty Maye has on a snap to snap basis. Constant pressure, no one separating. 70% or more of the Pats explosives have gotta be Maye just making something happen
With Romeo Doubs on injured reserve for the next two weeks, and A.J. Brown struggling with a knee injury, reinforcements aren't expected to assist in creating more separation for this receiver room.
That's why one reaction from Sunday's loss could be to explore a trade for a wide receiver before the 4 p.m trade deadline on November 10.
1. Josh Downs (Indianapolis Colts)
Downs has formally requested a trade from Indianapolis , who finds itself in a position to sell as much talent as possible at the deadline.
A 2023 third round pick, Downs came out of the same North Carolina program as Maye, and has admitted that he didn't explore the transfer portal because he wanted Maye to be his quarterback.
While never a top wide receiver option in Indianapolis, Downs has been a reliable pass-catcher during his four-year NFL career. His ability to create space and be shifty downfield answers the problem the Patriots faced yesterday in having their receivers get open.
2. Quentin Johnston (Los Angeles Chargers)
The Los Angeles Chargers have reached an astonishing 0-8 record to begin the season after having a playoff bid one year ago. The Chargers are at the point of no-return with their current roster and should be looking to move on from some of their pieces.
Johnston is a striking name that many teams will have interest in at the deadline. The former first round pick is a deep-threat target that hasn't seen much production this season, scoring his first touchdown of the year in LA's most recent game.
The fourth-year player has been criticized in the past for his pass-catching ability and unreliable hands. But his separation downfield and 6-foot-2 frame creates a hopeful opportunity for Johnston to fit into New England's passing game.
3. Brian Thomas Jr. (Jacksonville Jaguars)
Another former first-round pick, Thomas' production in Jacksonville has been overshadowed by the emergence of Parker Washington as the top wide receiver option.
Jacksonville has been the biggest buyer at the deadline, making three massive trades on defense in one day. But with three newly acquired players, the Jaguars front office may look to make room for their new talent by moving on from other players.
Thomas has generated a lot of buzz across the NFL as a player that the Jaguars are looking to move. The Patriots could be in on the mix of teams calling about Thomas before the 4 p.m deadline.

title: Despite Loss, Drake Maye Passes Mac Jones in Patriots Record Books
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots spent a first round pick on a quarterback who'd don No. 10 and lead them into the playoffs early in his career. Of course, I'm talking about Mac Jones and Drake Maye.
Obviously, the careers of both those two players are vastly different in 2026, but they were linked together during the Patriots' 45-27 drubbing at the hands of the Green Bay Packers . Despite Maye's ugly showing — where he threw three interceptions — he climbed up in the franchise's all-time passing yards leaderboard.
Maye finished the game with 299 yards, pushing his total career yardage to 8,952. That put him past Jones' 8,918 and moved Maye into seventh-place in Patriots history.
Through nine games, Maye has had a season to remember (or forget, depending on the week). He's completing 65.4% of his passes and has thrown for 2,282 yards. He's scored 21 times, but turnovers continue to plague him.
The sky looked like the limit for Jones, who the Patriots selected 15th overall back in 2021. Beating out Cam Newton as a rookie, Jones led the Patriots to a winning record and a trip to the postseason after a one-year hiatus. He finished that season with 3,801 passing yards, 22 passing touchdowns and a trip to the Pro Bowl.
But his career started to unravel in the next two seasons. An ankle injury opened the door for Bailey Zappe to jump into the starting spot in 2022 and after a strong start to 2023, Jones eventually faded away into the backup job. He finished his three-year stint with New England going 864-for-1,308 for those 8,918 passing yards, 46 touchdowns, 36 interceptions. He'd be traded away to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2024 sixth round pick.
Maye can easily surge forward when it comes to his placement on that list. Jim Plunkett is one spot above him with 9,932 yards, and Tony Eason is just a little bit further out (10,732). Considering how this is just Maye's third season and he's already in the top seven, the outlook remains sunny .
It wasn't a good night for Maye, who acknowledged it postgame. After a short run on the game's opening play, Maye got impatient and hucked up a bad interception to Xavier McKinney. He'd later throw another one to McKinney in the second quarter — which came after one thrown to Evan Williams.
"They've hunted a lot of turnovers on, eyes on the quarterback, in zone coverage. And I knew that coming into it and forced the first one," Maye said. "And then like I said, they jumped some crossers ... I think the bad ones hurt more than the good ones, unfortunately."
It was Maye's second-career game with three interceptions and both have come this season against really stout defensive units. He's up to 11 on the season, the most in the league, as the Patriots teeter into an international battle with the Detroit Lions.
Considering how the first three years of Maye's career have gone, he's set to rewrite the record books on a weekly basis. He also accounted for three touchdowns for the sixth-straight game, a personal best.

title: Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson Dealing with Knee Tendon Issue
full_text:
Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee tendon issue, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. The injury could keep the New England Patriots running back sidelined for a short period of time. Stevenson exited New England's Week 9 matchup against the Green Bay Packers after being tackled following a short reception in the third quarter. Schefter added that the injury will not require surgery, with Stevenson expected to recover through rest and rehabilitation. Following their trip to Munich, Germany, for a matchup against the Detroit Lions, the Patriots will have their Week 11 bye. A much-needed reset that could give Stevenson time to recover. Through nine games in 2026, Stevenson has rushed 102 times for 399 yards and two touchdowns while adding 26 receptions for 258 yards and two more scores through the air.
A potential absence for Stevenson would be another major blow to a Patriots offense that can't seem to catch a break. New England lost top wide receiver A.J. Brown to a high ankle sprain in its season opener, forcing him to miss four games on injured reserve. He has since missed two additional games while dealing with a knee flare-up tied to a reported degenerative knee condition. Romeo Doubs also remains on injured reserve after suffering a shoulder injury in Week 6 against the New York Jets. He is expected to remain sidelined until at least Week 12.
The injuries extend to the offensive line, where starting right guard Mike Onwenu and left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker are both on injured reserve with ankle and hamstring injuries, respectively. Backup guard Ben Brown also exited the Packers game with a knee injury. Simply put, the Patriots' offense has taken hit after hit this season. With injuries continuing to pile up at running back, wide receiver, and along the offensive line, the Patriots' offense has been left with fewer reliable options to work with.
With TreVeyon Henderson missing New England's last two games due to illness and recently releasing a statement regarding his health, the Patriots will need to be prepared for a scenario without him. Their next options at running back are Corey Kiner, Lan Larison, and Terrell Jennings, who is currently on the practice squad. Kiner, acquired in an August trade with the Arizona Cardinals, has proven to be a serviceable downhill runner for New England. His 50 carries for 244 yards and one touchdown give him the team's highest yards-per-carry average at 4.9. Larison, a 2025 undrafted free agent from UC Davis, has seen limited NFL action, appearing in just three games. Jennings, a 2024 UDFA, appeared in 10 games for New England during the 2024 and 2025 seasons, rushing 36 times for 106 yards and a score. In August, he was placed on injured reserve, then reached an injury settlement and was waived by the Patriots. He re-signed with the team's practice squad on Nov. 2.

title: Patriots Roster Moves: Rookie TE, Veteran Edge Rusher Released
full_text:
One day removed from one of the worst losses in franchise history , the New England Patriots are making some minor roster moves.
The team announced Monday that they released rookie tight end Tanner Arkin from the 53-man roster and edge rusher Jose Ramirez from the practice squad. There were no other transactions announced, so the Patriots will have an open roster spot on both the 53-man roster and the practice squad.
Here's what both of those moves mean for the Patriots moving into Week 10 and beyond:
Arkin was one of three undrafted free agents to make the team's initial 53-man roster this summer after a really impressive training camp. The Illinois alum contributed as both a blocking tight end on the line of scrimmage and worked in as a fullback at times as well.
Since the season began, his role really hasn't been anything substantial. The Patriots had claimed Cameron Latu off of waivers prior to Week 1, making it four tight ends on the active roster along with Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon. They also have Tanner Conner on the practice squad.
Arkin has dressed in five games this year and has been a healthy scratch in the other four. When Reggie Gilliam went down with an injury in Week 4, the Patriots called on Arkin in more of a fullback-type role, but he struggled in that department. He's tallied 60 total snaps on offense and 41 total snaps on defense, not recording a stat in either phase of the game.
Against the Green Bay Packers , Arkin was called for an illegal motion on the game's first play from scrimmage, one of three penalties he's been called for in the last four weeks. If he clears waivers, he could return to the practice squad.
The Patriots continue to have Ramirez bounce around their roster, making yet another move with the young edge rusher. The 27-year-old has now been part of seven different moves since originally signing with the Patriots practice squad on Sept. 1.
Ramirez did play in two game this season, dressing for the team's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3 and their 29-26 win over the Buffalo Bills one week later. He did record a tackle on special teams, but would be cut and put back on the practice squad 13 days later.
After Ramirez's release, the Patriots now have rookie Xavier Holmes, Benton Whitley and Elias Neal as the edge rushers/linebackers on the practice squad.
The Patriots have several players that could potentially be activated from injured reserve to fill a spot on the roster, including offensive guard Greg Van Roten, edge rusher Quintayvious Hutchins, linebacker Khalil Jacobs and safety Dell Pettus. The team will have meetings on Tuesday before a Wednesday practice ahead of their trip to Germany that night.

title: What Went Wrong with Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez vs. Packers?
full_text:
In a 45-27 beatdown in Foxborough on Sunday, seemingly everything went wrong for the New England Patriots, who couldn't find any solution to a high-powered Green Bay Packers offense.
The blame pie for Week 9's loss has been split in many different ways, from Drake Maye's turnovers, to  Mike Vrabel's seemingly incorrect gameplan and lack of adjustements, and poor defensive scheming. Despite all that went wrong, no individual has been handed more criticism for Sunday's loss than Christian Gonzalez.
The fourth-year cornerback, who just signed a record-breaking extension in the offseason , played without a doubt the worst game of his professional career.
A former All-Pro selection defensive back, Gonzalez earned his stripes as one of the NFL's best secondary players by locking down some of the most skilled wide receivers in the world. Against the Packers, the 24-year-old put up almost no competition to receivers Matthew Golden and Christian Watson.
According to NFL's Next Gen Stats, Gonzalez allowed a combined 187 yards and 10 receptions to the Packers dual receiving threat. Prior to Sunday, Gonzalez's career-high receiving yards allowed was 90 —  less than half of what he let up to Green Bay.
Additionally, Gonzalez only allowed 196 yards in the six other games he played in this season. The 187 yards allowed on Sunday was the third-most by any NFL defensive back this season — an embarrassing statistic for the highest-paid cornerback in the league.
Christian Gonzalez allowed 7 receptions for 105 yards to Matthew Golden and 3 receptions for 82 yards to Christian Watson. Gonzalez is the only defender since at least 2018 to allow more than 80 receiving yards to two different players in the same game. Powered by @awscloud pic.twitter.com/2voC02QTd3
Quarterback Jordan Love threw for 372 yards in his three touchdown and nearly 80% completion rate performance. With more than half of those yards coming in targets attempted towards Gonzalez, it's clear that Green Bay and head coach Matt LaFleur had a game plan to come at the star corner.
LaFleur denied this intentional game plan postgame.
"I wouldn't say we went at him all game, but it was more just attacking the coverages more so than an individual," he said.
In addition to his touchdown allowed to Watson, Gonzalez also recorded a defenive pass interference, just his third penalty of that kind assessed to him in his career.
Watson and Golden, practically toying with the Patriots defense, each set career highs in yardage on Sunday, and are now both within the NFL's top-four players in receiving yards on the season.
One of the major storylines following the Packers offense all season has been their success rate with throwing the football downfield. Love attempts more passes of 20-plus yards than any other quarterback this season. He entered Sunday as the league leader in passing yards, with two top-10 weapons in receiving yards.
Knowing this information about the Packers, it begs the question to defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr, wasn't it obvious that Green Bay would throw the ball deep?
"We knew that was going to be the key to the game – eliminate the big play," said veteran safety Kevin Byard III. "We didn't do good enough today, at all."
What makes Gonzalez's performance more puzzling is how he was targeted. The Patriots have notoriusly been one of the best man coverage teams in the NFL, calling man coverage schemes more than every team, but two. On Sunday, the Patriots ran more zone than expected, and were often beat.
Gonzalez — known to be one of the best man-to-man cornerbacks in the NFL — let up a surprising 101 yards in man coverage. His catches allowed didn't come from losing a step, or not making plays at the ball (which is how most cornerbacks are beaten in man coverage), but instead he simply wasn't where the play needed to be made.
Some of his mishaps came in unfortunate circumstances, like a trip that caused Watson to break free, or a poor defensive read by Byard, who was supposed to provide safety help on the touchdown Gonzalez allowed.
Not being close enough to his receiver is what caused yesterday's putrid performance from the Patriots defensive cornerstone. He allowed far too much space between himself and his defenders, and was often taken advantage of for it.
The Patriots most heavily-targeted defensive back seemed to not have taken his career-low performance to heart.
"I had a bad game" said Gonzalez. "So, I'm not shaken up by it. I'm not too worried about it. I'll move on and be ready for next week."
Patriots HC Mike Vrabel starts off his quote on CB Christian Gonzalez with: "You can't take a nap in this league." Asked him to clarify what he meant by that in this specific instance. "You just can't take a play off or think that they're not going to challenge you or throw the…
Again, one piece of the blame pie certainly belongs to Kuhr, who may have instructed Gonzalez to give the Packers receivers an extra yard or two in coverage. But there's no doubt that if Gonzalez looked like the superstar cornerback he's always played like, New England would've found themselves competing to the very end.
"When your best players don't play good, you don't have much of a chance in this league," said Vrabel. "So, we expect a lot more. He expects a lot more. We need more from him and everybody else."

title: Patriots Get Tough News on Ben Brown's Knee Injury Heading into Week 10
full_text:
FOXBORO — Mike Vrabel said one day after the New England Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers that they were "wearing out the MRIs."
That doesn't seem like a surprise, as the Patriots got banged up beyond belief in Sunday's drubbing of a game. Several key players, including Rhamondre Stevenson, Brenden Schooler and Carlton Davis, would leave with lower body injuries. Starting left guard Ben Brown, who was only in the game after injuries have decimated the offensive line to this point, also was ruled out with a knee injury.
Asked on Monday if there was an update on Brown's status heading into this week, the outlook for the 28-year-old guard didn't appear that good.
"(He) probably won't make it this week," Vrabel said.
After Brown left the game, Walter Rouse came in to replace him. In totality, the Patriots offensive line really struggled to make things easy for Drake Maye in the pocket. He was sacked four times and was under duress for most of the evening .
It's been a tough year for Brown health-wise. After repping as one of the top backups during the summer, he got banged up during a preseason game that forced him to miss some time at the start of the year. Once he returned, he was slotted into the starting lineup before another injury against the New York Jets knocked him out again.
He missed the team's TNF loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 7, but returned to play in the next two games.
It's been a trying time for this offensive line. The Patriots have already lost Mike Onwenu, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Greg Van Roten to IR, forcing Bown, Rouse and Matt Pryor to have larger roles in the offense. Despite that, the Patriots are sitting at 5-4 (still currently in the AFC playoff picture) and could end up making things interesting as winter rolls around.
"We're five and four. I think there's going to be a lot of contending teams that are five and four," Vrabel said. "I think that's the nature of the National Football League. We got to draw a line here. Now we got to think that we're zero and zero, and we got to start putting ourselves in position to play meaningful games in January or in the middle of January."
With Brown unlikely to go against the Detroit Lions in Week 10, that could be a sign that the veteran Van Roten, who's 21-day window to be activated off of IR began last week, could make a return to the roster. It also might end up being a sign that the Patriots need some more interior depth ahead of Tuesday's NFL trade deadline .
"That's something that we'll look at," Vrabel said. "He's eligible and has been working hard to get back, so we'll take a look at that and see where he is tomorrow or Wednesday when we practice."

title: Patriots Running Game Needs to Step Up After Several Players Go Down
full_text:
FOXBORO — Nothing went well for the New England Patriots in their 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers Sunday. The running game, down TreVeyon Henderson, didn't amount to much either.
Despite having their running back trio run for 91 yards, the group of Rhamondre Stevenson, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison didn't impact the game in the way they might have been able to. Yes, Stevenson had some nice runs and found the end zone as a receiver, but this group continues to struggle.
Most of Kiner's rushing yards came deep into garbage time, well after the score had been out of hand and after Stevenson was ruled out with a knee injury. He'd score his first-career touchdown to make the score look a bit more respectable, but for all intents and purposes, it didn't work.
"He wasn't able to return," Mike Vrabel said postgame on Stevenson, who also fumbled the ball in the loss. "I'm not sure the extent of what it is. He just came off, so we'll take a look at it, and we'll see. I don't want to speculate right now."
The Patriots are going to have to get that part of their offense going at some point, and right now, there are question marks surrounding that group.
How will Stevenson respond this week after walking to the locker room injured? Will Henderson, who put out a statement about neurological issues he's dealing with, even return this year ? Will a player on the trade block a la Derrick Henry or Jonathan Taylor find their way to New England in 48 hours?
There's a lot to figure out about this team right now as a whole, but the running game — one that's struggled a bunch all season — needs to find even footing.
Playoff teams, at least good playoff teams, rely on running the ball when the weather gets cold. It can't just be up to Drake Maye and his group of oft-injured, ragtag receivers every single game. Sooner or later, with or without Stevenson in the game, the Patriots are going to need and carry the rock 25-30 times a game with efficiency.
For most of Sunday, they couldn't do that against Green Bay.
"We lost, and we got our asses kicked. There's no two ways around it," Vrabel said. "We have to find ways to be balanced offensively."
Through nine games, the Patriots are averaging 4.1 yards per carry. Far from great.
Maybe the Patriots feel like they have to make a move for someone, especially if Stevenson isn't able to suit up in Germany next weekend. For now, considering the struggles that Maye displayed against the Packers , this running attack will become super important in these must-win games down the stretch.

title: 3 Winners, 3 Losers in Patriots Smackdown Loss Against Packers
full_text:
On Sunday, the New England Patriots were outplayed in countless facets in their 45-27 loss against the Green Bay Packers.
Throughout the season, New England has dealt with numerous injuries to its squad, with those absences being highlighted against Green Bay.
With many of the Patriots' issues on Sunday stemming from the top of their roster, here are the three biggest winners and losers from their blowout loss to the Packers.
On Sunday, Gonzalez had the worst game of his NFL career by a mile. In fact, he had one of the worst games out of any cornerback this season.
Gonzalez allowed 187 yards in coverage, the third-most by any player this season, after he had allowed 196 yards in his first six games combined.
In coverage against Packers wide receivers Matthew Golden and Christian Watson, Gonzalez forced just one incompletion and allowed a whopping 10 receptions. To add more fuel to the fire, both Golden and Watson set career-highs in receiving yards on Sunday.
"When your best players don't play good, you don't have much of a chance in this league," New England head coach Mike Vrabel said. "So, we expect a lot more. He expects a lot more. We need more from him and everybody else."
Early in the season, Maye struggled with poor decision-making, forcing passes downfield in unacceptable situations. Although he had largely cleaned up his act since then, he reverted back to his old ways on Sunday.
The third-year gunslinger finished the day with three interceptions, all of which came in the first half. Those turnovers quickly put the Patriots in a hole they could not dig themselves out of.
"I'm disappointed in myself for, you can't put the team in the hole straight off the bat, first possession, first half," Maye said. "I feel like in the times we had chances to get back into the game, I messed them up, and we had chances to put us back within three points multiple times, and just frustrating...I wasn't good today."
While the Patriots wide receiver room struggled as a whole, Douglas was the lone bright spot. The 25-year-old finished the afternoon with five receptions for 102 yards, providing the lackluster New England offense with some big-play ability. Plus, he has now tallied at least 65 yards in four of his past five games.
"We got to keep going," Douglas said after the loss. "We're still in it. I feel like we just got to work. A lot of people are going to have a lot of opportunities and it's time for people to step up. When they roll call, it's time to go."
Yes, Maye made plenty of poor decisions against the Packers. However, his offensive line was not doing him any favors.
On 43 dropbacks, New England allowed 27 pressures, 13 of which were unblocked. Plus, it let up 17 hurries, four quarterback hits and four sacks. Maye was playing under durress all evening due to the poor performance up front.
Heading into the week, it was questioned whether or not Barmore would even play on Sunday. The 27-year-old did not participate in Wednesday's practice due to an illness and was the topic of trade talks from national reports.
Despite this, Barmore took the field and was one of New England's lone bright spots. His takedown of Packers quarterback Jordan Love helped extend his streak to four-consecutive games with at least half a sack. Plus, he also tallied a pair of run stops.
It may not be the best day in the office when your punter is one of your best players on the field. But, naturally, that was the case for the Patriots against the Packers.
Wishnowsky had an impressive performance Sunday, with four of his five punts pinning Green Bay inside its own 20-yard line. One of the 34-year-old's punts also landed perfectly inside the 5-yard line.

title: Saints Trading DL Godchaux to Jaguars Signals Continued Youth Movement on Defense
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints are finalizing a trade that will send veteran defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Jacksonville Jaguars , another move signaling the organization's willingness to prioritize its future over veteran experience.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that New Orleans will receive a 2028 sixth-round draft pick that could become a 2027 sixth-round pick if Jacksonville acquires one through a trade or the compensatory process.
The deal comes just one day after the Saints secured a thrilling 23-22 overtime win over the Cleveland Browns , improving to 3-5.
While the trade provides New Orleans with additional draft capital, it offers little immediate financial relief.
For salary cap reasons, the Saints had restructured Godchaux's contract by converting the bulk of his pay into a signing bonus, leaving only $650,000 of his $1.3 million base salary.
As Godchaux turns 32 this week and approaches the final year of his deal, he became an expendable veteran for a team placing greater emphasis on nurturing younger talent.
New Orleans initially acquired the Plaquemine, Louisiana native from the New England Patriots in March 2025, surrendering a 2026 seventh-round pick while assuming the remaining two years and $11 million of his contract following a restructuring.
Although Godchaux appeared in all eight games this season, his role has gotten smaller and smaller by the week. Godchaux started the first five games, but hehas  played just eight, 18 and 12 defensive snaps over the last three games.
However, Godchaux still contributed to one of the Saints' biggest defensive plays Sunday, helping stop Cleveland on a critical fourth-and-goal opportunity.
The departure of Godchaux opens up substantial playing time for the Saints' younger defensive linemen, most notably Khristian Boyd and rookie second-round selection Christen Miller .
Boyd, who recorded a sack and a tackle for loss Sunday and played a key role alongside Godchaux in the goal-line stand, is expected to see an expanded workload at center of New Orleans' defensive line.
At the same time, accelerating Miller's progress becomes more urgent, especially since the rookie was a healthy scratch for the matchup against Cleveland.
Ultimately, this deal signifies more for New Orleans than just swapping a veteran player for late-round draft compensation.
It reflects a clear strategic shift by the front office to assess its youth roster while continuing to stockpile future draft assets.
How well New Orleans fills the void left by Godchaux upfront will largely hinge on whether Boyd and Miller can take full advantage of their new opportunities.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Saints' Wild Overtime Win Over Browns
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints finally gave their home crowd something to celebrate Sunday, securing a thrilling 23-22 overtime victory over the Cleveland Browns at Caesars Superdome.
But while the Saints improved to 3-5 and snapped their home winless streak, the victory was far from pretty.
For Kellen Moore , the victory provided some much-needed relief, but it also exposed several problems that continue to plague his team and will keep him on the hot seat.
With a difficult stretch of the schedule ahead, the Saints have plenty to clean up if they want to build momentum.
Here’s a look at the good, the bad and the ugly from New Orleans' dramatic overtime victory over Cleveland.
Tyler Shough continues to show his clutch gene, even if the organization he plays for is in shambles.
Shough completed 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown while adding 51 rushing yards on 10 carries. While he didn’t do much for most of the game, it’s when his team needed him the most he stepped up. His composure in critical situations stood out.
Trailing 13-9 late in the fourth quarter, Shough orchestrated a 55-yard touchdown drive in just 50 seconds, highlighted by a 33-yard completion to Chris Olave that set up Audric Estimé 's 2-yard touchdown run.
After Cleveland forced overtime, Shough responded again, leading an 11-play, 74-yard touchdown drive capped by a perfectly placed 15-yard pass to ever-reliable tight end Juwan Johnson . That drive was his fifth game-winning drive of the season.
The performance was particularly encouraging, given that Shough was sacked five times and played late in the game without starting center Erik McCoy .
Estimé also provided an unexpected spark, rushing for 72 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries just days after being claimed off waivers.
Despite scoring 23 points, the New Orleans Saints ' offense struggled again.
The Saints didn't score a touchdown until Estimé’s run with 58 seconds remaining, settling for field goals despite moving the ball effectively at times. The Saints also only converted on two of their five red zone opportunities.
Their struggles were particularly evident in the first half, when New Orleans outgained Cleveland 176-80 but entered halftime tied 3-3.
The offensive line also had its share of problems, surrendering five sacks and repeatedly forcing Shough to escape pressure.
Even with left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. back, the Saints struggled to protect their quarterback consistently.
Sure, several individuals had encouraging performances, but New Orleans still lacks inspiration on offense and the ability to put opponents away.
Without starting quarterback Deshaun Watson , the Saints had multiple chances to take control against Cleveland but instead needed late-game heroics.
The Saints won't always be fortunate enough to overcome those shortcomings. The Carolina Panthers are up next, but the following three games: two road games back-to-back against the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals and a home matchup against the Green Bay Packers .
If there's one area that should frustrate Kellen Moore more than anything else, it's the Saints' inability to protect the football.
New Orleans committed two costly second-quarter turnovers, both involving rookies, that completely changed the complexion of the game.
First-round pick Jordyn Tyson , making his NFL debut after missing the first seven games with a hamstring injury, fumbled near Cleveland's goal line moments after making his first career reception on the same play.
The turnover wasted a promising scoring opportunity after Shough connected with Barion Brown for a 52-yard gain.
Things somehow got worse moments later.
After the defense forced a punt, Brown fumbled the return, giving Cleveland possession at the Saints' 19-yard line.
Fortunately for New Orleans, the defense bailed out the offense and special teams, stopping Quinshon Judkins on fourth-and-goal from the 1-yard line.
But the mistakes weren't limited to turnovers.
The Saints' defense also surrendered a 64-yard touchdown pass from Shedeur Sanders to KC Concepcion Jr. immediately after taking a 9-6 lead in the fourth quarter.
Then, after Estimé put New Orleans ahead with 58 seconds remaining, the defense allowed Cleveland to move into position for a game-tying 51-yard field goal.
And even after Shough delivered an overtime touchdown, the Saints surrendered a 39-yard touchdown reception to Harold Fannin Jr. , forcing the defense to make one final stand.
New Orleans escaped with a victory, but the combination of turnovers, blown coverage and late defensive breakdowns nearly turned a much-needed win into another devastating loss.

title: Saints Turn Snoozefest Into Thriller, Escape With Overtime Win Over Browns
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints secured their first home victory of the season in thrilling fashion on Sunday at Caesars Superdome, defeating the Cleveland Browns 23-22 in overtime.
Quarterback Tyler Shough connected with tight end Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown pass with 4:17 remaining in the extra period, giving New Orleans a seven-point lead. Cleveland quickly countered with a touchdown drive of its own, but the Saints’ defense shut down the Browns’ potential game-winning two-point conversion attempt to seal the dramatic win.
With the victory, the Saints improved to 3-5 while snapping a frustrating home winless streak. The loss dropped the Browns to 5-4. What began as a sluggish defensive battle turned into one of the wildest finishes of the NFL season, featuring 20 fourth-quarter points and an overtime showdown after three quarters dominated by field goals.
Shough delivered an impressive performance, completing 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards while adding 51 rushing yards on 10 carries.
On the other side, Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders was equally stellar, throwing for 297 yards and two touchdowns on 19-of-31 passing.
However, running back Audric Estime proved to be New Orleans’ secret weapon. Re-joining the team just days before kickoff after being cut following training camp, Estime provided a massive spark with 15 carries for 72 yards and a touchdown to open up the offense.
The game reached peak chaos late in the fourth quarter. Up 9-6, New Orleans watched Cleveland reclaim the lead on a dramatic 4-yard touchdown connection from Sanders to receiver Concepcion with 5:21 left. Sanders hit Concepcion on a deep route before the receiver cut left and sprinted into the corner of the end zone, stunning the home crowd.
Unfazed, the Saints executed a swift scoring drive that took just 50 seconds. Shough found wideout Chris Olave for a 33-yard completion to Cleveland’s 10-yard line, setting up Estime’s 2-yard touchdown run with 58 seconds remaining to put New Orleans ahead 16-13.
Cleveland answered immediately as Sanders orchestrated a quick drive into field goal range. Browns kicker Andre Szmyt drilled a 51-yard field goal as regulation expired to tie the game at 16-16 and send it into overtime.
In overtime, Shough led the Saints downfield and found Johnson for a touchdown to take a 23-16 lead. Sanders responded once more, connecting with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown pass to make it 23-22.
Rather than kicking the extra point to force double overtime, Cleveland aggressively went for two. However, a crucial holding penalty pushed the Browns back, and Sanders’ forced pass attempt fell incomplete to preserve the Saints’ victory.
The frantic second half stood in stark contrast to the opening two quarters, which ended in a 3-3 deadlock. Despite outgaining Cleveland 176-80 in total yards during the first half, the Saints struggled to finish drives due to costly mistakes.
Saints kicker Charlie Smyth opened the scoring with a 30-yard field goal midway through the first quarter after missing a 52-yard attempt earlier in the game. Szmyt answered for Cleveland with a 41-yard field goal with 10:30 remaining in the second quarter.
New Orleans had multiple opportunities to take control early. Following Szmyt’s field goal, Shough hit receiver Barion Brown for a 52-yard completion to Cleveland’s 11-yard line. However, rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson fumbled at the Browns’ 2-yard line, turning the ball over and squandering a prime scoring chance.
The Saints’ defense provided key plays to keep Cleveland contained. Linebacker Kaden Elliss executed a goal-line stand late in the second quarter, stopping Browns running back Judkins for no gain on fourth-and-goal from the 1-yard line to preserve the tie entering halftime. Defensive end Cameron Jordan and edge rusher Carl Granderson also recorded key sacks on Sanders during the game.
