title: Postgame LIVE Reaction: Saints Win Overtime Thriller Over Browns
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints win their first home game of the season with a 23-16 win over the Cleveland Browns .
Make sure to follow along for all of the reactions from head coach Kellen Moore, quarterback Tyler Shough and other players as well as you, the fans!
The New Orleans Saints (3-5) earned their first home win of the season, beating the Cleveland Browns (5-4) 23-22 in overtime at Caesars Superdome.
Saints win a wild one at home 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/eZ52EBujMt
After three field-goal-dominated quarters, the game erupted with 20 fourth-quarter points. Cleveland took a 13-9 lead on a 4-yard touchdown pass from Shedeur Sanders to Concepcion with 5:21 left. New Orleans answered 50 seconds later with a 2-yard touchdown run by Audric Estime —set up by a 33-yard pass from Tyler Shough to Chris Olave . Cleveland’s Andre Szmyt hit a 51-yard field goal as regulation expired to force overtime tied at 16-16.
In overtime, Shough threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Juwan Johnson with 4:17 remaining. Cleveland responded with a 39-yard touchdown pass from Sanders to Harold Fannin Jr. , but after a holding penalty on their two-point conversion attempt, Sanders’ pass fell incomplete to secure the Saints’ victory.
Shough finished with 265 passing yards, a touchdown, and 51 rushing yards. Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns. Estime, re-signed days before kickoff after being cut in training camp, added 72 rushing yards and a touchdown on 15 carries.
Moore: "We spent all week just talking about, hey, we're coming off a bye week. It's all going to be about response, eyes forward, moving forward, what's in front of us. And that's all you've got to focus on.

title: Saints vs. Browns Predictions: Will New Orleans Take Advantage of Cleveland's QB Change?
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints will take on the Cleveland Browns at noon Sunday.
The Saints are coming off a much-needed bye week after a 2-5 start to the year. Meanwhile, the Browns are off to an unexpected 5-3 start but will be without starter Deshaun Watson .
Here are our staff predictions.
This is a game I would have picked the Saints to lose, but things change.
Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson is questionable for Sunday’s game, so the organization will start Shedeur Sanders . Because of this revelation, it 100% benefits the Saints.
Watson has been one of the league's better quarterbacks all season. However, with him out for this game, the Browns’ offense is less of a threat, even with solid receiving options in wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin .
Then, add to the fact that left tackle Kelvin Banks is back after missing significant time due to an ankle injury and rookie wide receiver and first-round pick Jordyn Tyson will finally make his debut after suffering a hamstring injury during fall camp, the Saints’ odds of winning only increase.
This is a great opportunity for the Saints to get a win, especially with a three-game slate coming up.
However, if the Saints don’t get a win, there will be a lot more questions than answers in New Orleans, especially for head coach Kellen Moore and the man who hired him, general manager Mickey Loomis .
The Saints made some moves after the bye week, firing their run game coordinator and bringing in a familiar face at kicker. I asked earlier this week in my column if it was a step in the right direction or window dressing.
This week also carries with it the return of Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve after limited practice opportunities Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.
Add to that first-round pick Jordyn Tyson makes his debut in a Saints regular-season uniform this weekend.
The surprise move for me was the timing of cutting 4th year running back Kendre Miller . Though I have been on the "get rid of Miller ASAP" train for a while, I did not expect it to happen the day before a game.
These moves force me to look back at the first half of the season and wonder if this Saints team has gotten better as the year has worn on. The answer is no.
The kicking game move to Charlie Smyth is a lateral move, maybe a little better. The return of Banks will be an improvement, but the Saints weren't doing all that well running the ball with him in the lineup before the injury. Replacing a run coordinator cuts down the amount of feedback you're getting as a coach about your rushing attack. That could be good and bad. The defense cannot stop the run, while the offense can't get it going.
This is not a good team. Some want to blame Mickey Loomis, some Kellen Moore, some want to put the onus on the athletes that have been brought into the fold (or kept).
I say all that to say this: Even with Shedeur Sanders starting at quarterback Sunday for the Browns, a definite step back from the usual starter Watson, this Saints team has quite a lot to prove before I can say with confidence that they can scratch out a win.
I would love for this to be the game where the Caesars Superdome regains its reputation as a hell-hole for visiting teams. I would love to see Audric Estimé be the back who makes the difference (the way Saints fans would love him to be) instead of a guy who has bounced around from practice squad to practice squad his entire career. I would like to have Chase Young continue to hunt down opposing quarterbacks, and while he's at it to stop the run, too.
And I'd love to see the Saints win Sunday. I just don't see it.

title: Saints vs. Browns: 3 Things to Know About Cleveland's Defense
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints will look to get their offense back on track Sunday when they face a Cleveland Browns defense that has experienced its share of ups and downs this season.
Despite losing superstar defensive end Myles Garrett , Cleveland has remained a formidable defensive opponent, especially at generating pressure and creating turnovers.
However, the Browns have also struggled to stop the run, giving the New Orleans offense an opportunity to exploit that weakness.
For quarterback Tyler Shough and the Saints, exploiting Cleveland's weaknesses while limiting costly mistakes could be the difference between another frustrating offensive performance and a much-needed bounce-back win.
With New Orleans preparing for its first game following the bye week, here are three things to know about the Browns' defense heading into Sunday's matchup.
Cleveland made significant offseason changes, but none were bigger than trading superstar defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams.
Garrett was coming off a historic 2025 season in which he established an NFL record with 23 sacks and recorded 33 tackles for loss.
His departure, combined with defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz's resignation, raised questions about whether Cleveland could maintain its defensive identity.
However, the Browns have remained competitive defensively under first-year coach Todd Monken .
Cleveland has recorded 21 sacks through eight games, ranking ninth in the NFL, while collecting six interceptions.
Several young defensive players have also contributed, including defensive end Jared Vers e, who arrived from Los Angeles as part of the Garrett trade.
The Browns are allowing 126.9 rushing yards per game and 4.7 yards per carry, ranking among the league's bottom 10 in both categories.
Those struggles were especially apparent against Pittsburgh, which rushed for 200 yards in Sunday's victory.
That's an encouraging matchup for New Orleans, which has struggled to establish a consistent rushing attack throughout the season.
The Saints managed just 18 rushing yards in their 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh before entering their bye week.
If New Orleans can exploit Cleveland's defensive weaknesses on the ground, it could take considerable pressure off quarterback Tyler Shough and create more opportunities through the passing game.
Although Cleveland has struggled against the run, its secondary remains one of the defense's more dependable units.
The Browns are allowing 214.6 passing yards per game and have surrendered 11 passing touchdowns through eight games.
However, they have also intercepted six passes and held opposing quarterbacks to a relatively modest 6.6 yards per pass attempt.
Much of Cleveland's success in coverage begins with veteran cornerback Denzel Ward .
Ward has continued to establish himself as one of the NFL's premier coverage defenders, earning a 91.6 coverage grade from Pro Football Focus, the highest among qualified cornerbacks entering Week 9.

title: Giants Open as Slim Favorites vs. Commanders
full_text:
The New York Giants continue to do the unexpected by winning games in their division and building a case as a postseason contender at 5-2-1, but once again, the oddsmakers are not impressed with their start.
After earning their first victory in the City of Brotherly Love since the 2013 season by defeating the Philadelphia Eagles 19-11 in a defensive barn burner, one would think that Vegas would show some extra love as the team returns home to East Rutherford with the focus on unofficially putting to rest the idea of a multi-team race in the NFC East.
Instead, the Giants face the Washington Commanders again at MetLife Stadium on Thursday night. FanDuel Sportsbook opened its Week 10 lines with Big Blue as just a 1.5-point home favorite over the 2-5-1 Commanders.
The new spread marks a four-point swing from the first meeting between the rival franchises back in Week 5, when the Giants rallied back from a 14-point deficit in the second half and forced overtime behind the leadership of then-starting quarterback Jameis Winston and his three touchdown passes to his two top targets, Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers.
Unfortunately for New York, they couldn’t muster a winning drive in the additional 10 minutes of play and were left with a bitter taste in their mouths after a 27-27 tie.
Even with a strong lead in the NFC East there is no doubt that John Harbaugh’s team will be hungry to make up for the extra win that got away and put the Commanders’ season to rest with a convincing performance under the bright lights.
That said, it’s easy to see why betting outlets still hesitate to back the Giants fully. They are playing on a very short week, and the lack of extra recovery time can sometimes take a toll on players’ performance and possibly swing the game the other way if fatigue leads to untimely mistakes.
More importantly, the Giants left Philadelphia with some slight concern about J.J. McCarthy, who suffered a hip injury in the third quarter of Sunday’s game that forced him to miss the lone touchdown drive led by Jameis Winston before McCarthy returned on the next possession.
Harbaugh admitted after the game that his starting quarterback was in real pain but said he was confident neither ailment would keep McCarthy sidelined for Washington. The Giants are also expected to have Cam Skattebo back after the team elected to sit him against the Eagles for his hamstring issue and save the running back’s energy for the second game in less than a week.
A fully staffed Giants team still has a lot to improve from their last duel with the Commanders, including slowing down Washington’s run game, which amassed 202 yards on a 6.7-yard average carry, with 103 yards coming from quarterback Jayden Daniels, who produced two touchdowns.
The Giants dominated the run, holding Saquon Barkley to 22 yards on 13 rushing attempts and the Eagles to under 100 yards total, while Philadelphia’s passing attack struggled to pick up the slack amid an eight-sack day from the front seven that forced seven three-and-out drives.
The Commanders’ offense is ravaged by injuries in the receiver room, including the loss of Terry McLaurin to a torn patellar tendon that ended his season as Washington’s main weapon.
Four other players are also on the team’s injury report, leaving Daniels with limited options if the Giants succeed in taking away the run dimension for a second straight week.
What will be most important for the Giants is using their options to close out the game, unlike what happened in Landover, Maryland, just over a month ago. They showed it against the Texans and Eagles in two huge wins, putting them on the cusp of building an insurmountable lead in the NFC East.
No better opponent to push the cause than a Commanders team that hasn’t learned to do the same since their unforgettable mishap, which might have changed the current landscape of the division and this game at large.

title: LIVE: Giants  NFL Trade Deadline Tracker: Trades, Rumors and Latest News
full_text:
In a matter of hours, it will be known whether New York Giants general manager Joe Schoen can swing any sort of deal to help reinforce the depth on head coach John Harbaugh’s first Giants roster.
New York has been heavily linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, with speculation intensifying after the team struggled to run the ball in Sunday’s win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
That intensification comes after reports that the Giants withdrew an offer of a second-round pick in 2027 and a fifth-round pick in 2028.
There are questions about how serious the Colts are about moving Taylor, with some believing that if they really wanted to, they’d lower an asking price that is reportedly similar to what the 49ers paid the Panthers to acquire running back Christian McCaffrey in 2022.
Interestingly, though, defensive tackle is where the Giants have a greater need. New York has not worked out many defensive tackles over the last few days, according to the daily transaction reports.
And while they finally did sign defensive lineman Dean Lowry to their practice squad, that hasn’t quite quelled the belief that the Giants would still like to add to the group.
All that said, the question remains: will the Giants make a deal by 4 p.m.? They don’t have a fourth- or fifth-round pick in next year’s draft, which seems to be the asset they need to get something done with a team looking to part with players to gain assets for a rebuild.
The Giants are also not looking to overspend on a player, according to head coach John Harbaugh.
“You want to do everything you can do to make your team as strong as you can right now, because we’re in the now, and we’re told to live in the moment, be where our feet are planted, concern ourselves with today, but that’s not at the expense of tomorrow or just prudent planning,” he said on Monday.
“I think we just have to look at each situation, and just weigh it out in terms of, okay, what’s the cost? What’s the benefit? And is it worth it? Is it going to benefit us? Is it a good thing for the Giants, and for the organization, and the team? So, I would say that the now weighs more important than the future, if you’re going to put it on a scale, and kind of go from there.”

title: Giants Preview: Thursday Night Rematch With Commanders Comes With Trade Deadline Noise
full_text:
The New York Giants and Washington Commanders are set for their rematch on Thursday night, five weeks after the two teams battled to a 27-27 tie in which the Commanders squandered a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter and cost themselves a win because of clock mismanagement.
Washington is coming off a 20-13 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams, while the Giants are coming off a 19-11 road win against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Commanders are averaging 21.5 points per game with a points-per-game differential of -3.75.
The Giants have fared a little better, averaging 22.8 points per game with a 1.25-point-per-game differential. Just one of their wins (Week 4 vs. Arizona) has been by 10 points or more, which means the Giants have squeaked by so far.
The good news for the Giants is their defense has been dominant. New York has allowed just 172 points to opponents this season, the seventh-lowest mark in the league, making a valid argument that the defense has carried the team for most of the season.
What will this week bring? Let’s take a look.
The Giants erased the 13-year losing streak in Philadelphia on Sunday. This week, they have a chance to erase a five-game streak in which they haven’t defeated the Commanders, home or away.
The Giants and Commanders, of course, tied in their meeting earlier this year. Before that, the last time the Giants beat Washington was November 19, 2023. So they are long overdue.
With a win, the Giants would improve to 3-0-1 in the division and remain a couple of steps ahead of the Dallas Cowboys, who seem hot on their heels in the NFC East race.
So yes, a lot is at stake for the Giants, who are 1-6 in games played on Thursday night since 2020. The Giants are aiming for their second straight win on Thursday Night Football .
A short workweek is challenging enough, but throw in the trade deadline, and it gets even more complicated.
The Giants have been heavily linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. Still, as of Sunday, Jay Glazer of Fox Sports reported that New York withdrew its offer after the Colts said they wanted much more for their lead back.
That doesn’t mean that things can’t change, but it’s hard to see a deal happening, considering the Giants don’t have a 2027 fourth- or fifth-round pick to include in a trade, which appears to be a requisite to get a deal done.
Given that the Colts also reportedly want a second-round pick, it’s hard to envision the Giants caving, especially after head coach John Harbaugh acknowledged the team isn’t one player away.
And then there is the other side of the coin, which is defensive tackle. The Giants really haven’t been strongly linked to any defensive tackles, at least not in the way they’ve been linked to Taylor. Could a surprise move be coming?
The Giants held a walkthrough practice on Monday, so their practice participation report was just a projection. That said, it was a very positive-looking projection: not a single player among those appearing on the report would have been held out of practice.
That’s huge considering names like running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring), quarterback J.J. McCarthy (hip), receiver Malik Nabers (knee), outside linebacker Abdul Carter (knee/back), and tackles Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are all on this week’s report.
Harbaugh, in fact, expressed optimism that Skattebo and McCarthy, whose injuries appear to be the most significant, will be available for Thursday night.

title: Where the Giants Stand as NFL Trade Deadline Looms
full_text:
The clock is ticking down to the NFL trade deadline, and the New York Giants are walking a tightrope. They occupy sole possession of first place in the NFC East with a 5-2-1 record, but their wins have admittedly come against suspect competition. Burning draft capital for pricey star players could disrupt their timeline.
If Big Blue overestimates its title-contention prospects, the long-term consequences could be severe. But the NFL landscape is hard to read this season. Maybe the rules are different this year.
Giants head coach and prominent decision-maker John Harbaugh is certainly staying aggressive . The Giants reportedly had interest in former Tennessee Titans All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who was ultimately dealt to the Chicago Bears.
The organization has also reportedly expressed considerable interest in Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor. However, the Giants are unwilling to overpay amid reports that the Colts won’t budge on their price tag.
The Giants undoubtedly have needs, the biggest of which might be another defensive tackle. Other than Simmons, there hasn’t been much chatter about which other defensive tackles the Giants might be interested in, though it would be surprising if they haven’t made several calls to see who’s available.
Not that the Giants feel the need to do anything unless it’s the right move.
“Somebody’s got to come out that you really want to trade for that makes sense,” said Harbaugh.
“It’s got to make sense short term and long term. We’re not just going to go for a short-term fix at an exorbitant cost. We’re not going to do that. That’s not where we’re at.
“I never think that you’re one step away, one player away. To me, it’s always just a total momentum kind of a thing anyway. But if the right opportunity comes and there’s a deal that makes sense for us, we’ll do it.”
Harbaugh also indicated that there is no burning desire to trade away any of the players currently on the roster, such as outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux, who has been a topic of trade discussions on and off among the fan base and media.
“There’s nobody on our team that we want to trade. We like all of our guys,” Harbaugh said.
The lack of fourth- and fifth-round picks in the 2027 draft is an issue, as those assets could have helped them make a trade if there is indeed one they’re champing at the bit to make.
Their 2027 fourth-round pick belongs to Cleveland as part of the trade up in the third round of the 2026 draft to acquire receiver Malachi Fields, while their 2027 fifth-round pick belongs to Minnesota, which sent them quarterback J.J. McCarthy.
But just because they don’t have those assets doesn’t mean that they’re out of the hunt.
“I’d say we’re open for any situation, but I will say this: things do change. Things change from day-to-day,” Harbaugh said. “So it’s not like one day you may do something and the next day something happens, and it changes your position.”
In addition to staying in touch with what’s happening on the trade front, Harbaugh has the added task of getting the football team ready on a short workweek.
“Yeah, boy, I don’t know how much this has really come up. Even on the bye, we’d have to go back and look, but it’s tricky,” Harbaugh admitted.
Even if a trade were made, the likelihood of that player participating in the team’s Thursday game against Washington is slim to none, Harbaugh added.
“I would say, just honestly, we’re probably not looking at anything for this game. It would be hard to say. I don’t know. Maybe we could bring a guy in.
“He could just practice Wednesday and play, but it would be kind of hard to imagine a guy coming in and just playing with one day here, I think. So, I’d probably assume that wouldn’t be possible. So, you’d be thinking more about the next week, which would give us plenty of time to get the player ready.”
The NFL trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET today.

title: Giants Injury Report: Cam Skattebo, J.J. McCarthy Trending in Right Direction for  Commanders Game
full_text:

For the Giants, the good news is that none of the players listed were projected to miss Monday’s practice. That includes running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and quarterback J.J. McCarthy (hip), the two biggest injuries on the team’s report.

title: Giants Defensive Player Grades: Arvell Reese Is Unblockable as Pass Rush Overwhelms Eagles
full_text:
The New York Giants defense faced the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday and delivered one of their season's finest performances.
New York delivered seven sacks, 10 tackles for loss, 11 quarterback hits, four pass breakups, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery.
They held old friend Saquon Barkley to just 22 yards on 13 carries, a 1.7 yards-per-carry average. Other than a 24-yard run by newly minted starting quarterback Joe Milton III, the run defense was spectacular overall.
This week, there were many heroes, both up front and behind the scenes. Arvell Reese was a monster — anyone else sitting there wondering why five teams passed on this play-making young man like we are?
Kayvon Thibodeaux, while not delivering the numbers in the pass rush, made a bunch of little plays that helped others shine. Shelby Harris and D.J. Reader were clutch. And inside linebacker Micah McFadden once again was “super sub,” as he didn’t come off the field.
All in all, it was a stellar performance by the defense —perhaps their best of the season—and we don’t care if you want to argue it came against backups, because those guys still get paid.
Special teams? Without Dominic Zvada and Jordan Stout, this unit would be our pick for the goat horns this week. The unit was sloppy with penalties and communication, but thankfully it didn’t hurt the team.
Let’s get into this week’s individual player grades for the defense and special teams — there’s a lot to like for sure.
Continuing to give this team one of the biggest bangs for their free-agent bucks, Reader recorded his first sack of the year with a resounding clean-up of an outside rush to the spot where he was crashing.
He added another quarterback hit while providing the only inside pass rush that this team can create. We’re not here to talk about Reader’s pass rush, since his run defense shows up on every down.
He seems to relish sticking his nose into the middle and is avoided on running downs like the plague.
By the way, his other tackle this week (besides the sack) also came in the backfield. Reader is not just absorbing double-teams; he’s beating them.
One of the more interesting developments on this young team is the play of its until-now unknown rookies.
Jamison-Travis (like offensive lineman J.C. Davis, also a sixth-rounder) has taken over the rotation at nose tackle, and he’s playing the position well.
He recorded three tackles today on running downs while absorbing doubles and beating singles. He’s not only absorbing, but he’s also flashing out there.
This kid has life in his legs that gets him to places a nose tackle doesn’t normally go, but it’s his play at the point of attack that is drawing notice.
Continuing to give the defense its best defensive end play this year, Harris’ veteran eyes help him anticipate and crash spots and gaps; he’s just lacking the goods to finish off these quick attacks.
When left to play it straight up, he’s not exactly lighting things up, but he was in the backfield on a couple of passing-down snaps that contributed to the general chaos around today’s Eagles pocket and helped the defense accrue its season-high seven sacks this week.
Getting the last of today’s sacks on the game’s final play, Alexander smartly closed down on the front of the pocket and cleaned up the mess the outside pressure had created.
It was a smart veteran move by this second-year player who played one of his better games today. He knocked down a fourth-quarter pass, recorded two tackles, and showed good upfield movement on several passing downs.
We’re still waiting for the physicality to show up, but he’s got the goods to blow things up inside if he wants to. The question is, does he want it?
Playing through an illness that kept him on the injury report all week, Carter was not himself out there and finished the game with just one measly assist, this on a day where the defense recorded seven sacks.
Carter was drawing double teams whenever he lined up on the edge, which opened things up for the rest of his teammates to attack.
What a testament to Carter’s impact that when his play is quiet, the defense plays one of its best games of the year. It’s certainly a good sign that this defense has a lot of good players.
Continuing to play a solid, assignment-clean style, Thibodeaux probably played his best game of the year this week. Though he was shut out on the sack sheet, Thibodeaux’s pass rush got home, and the blitzing created chaos that freed him up to attack the pocket.
He had two quarterback hits and four total tackles on his sheet, and his edge run defense really showed its teeth again.
We’ve stopped waiting for flash plays from this player and accepted that he’s contributing to a good defense that seems to be improving by the week.
Of note, both of Thibodeaux’s quarterback hits came off inside rushes from the edge, as he continues to lack the bend and speed to get around the corner.
Continuing to provide solid outside linebacker rotation snaps, Ford got in on one tackle when he ran the quarterback out of bounds.
He’s been playing a lot of coverage during these snaps, but not so much this week.
Elevated from the practice squad for today’s game, Smoot got plenty of playing time in the edge rotation and recorded two tackles, including credit for a sack when he dove at the quarterback’s legs in pursuit of a 1-yard fourth-quarter sack.
Smoot is a jumbo-sized outside linebacker whose pass-rush game was ho-hum, but he was consistently physical.
The Giants’ star rookie had one of those halves that almost defy belief. We’re talking about his first half, where he recorded nine of his team-high 12 tackles, and two of his three sacks.
Some will like Reese’s blind-side sack, as thunderous a hit as you will ever see on a football field, while also forcing a fumble the Giants recovered.
Reese’s other first-half sack came off of a middle blitz on which he played contain. His third sack of the day came in the second half when Reese lined up over the guard standing up, beat him with a quick swim move, and then finished him.
Our favorite Reese play? A second-quarter outside run by Saquon Barkley that had opened up for the back.
Suddenly, out of nowhere, Reese flashes into the play and absolutely rag-dolls Barkley to the turf for no gain; it was one of the more breathtakingly violent takedowns and finishes that we’ve ever seen.
Reese made tackles this week in every imaginable fashion—in coverage, edge blitzes, inside pass rushes—you name it.
Playing him at off-ball inside linebacker was one of the smartest things this braintrust ever did. You can’t run and hide from a great off-ball inside linebacker. The field isn’t big enough.
The Giants lost veteran inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds several weeks ago, and this defense hasn’t skipped a beat. In fact, it almost feels like it’s getting stronger.
McFadden had a top-shelf game of his own today, recording nine total tackles, one sack, and a fumble recovery off an Arvell Reese sack.
On another day, we’d be raving about McFadden’s game and impressed by how perfectly this defense fits what he does best.
McFadden not only has a great nose for the football, but he’s also an excellent blitzer. He times things up very well, and he has a plan of attack on every single blitz, always attacking with aggressiveness and some surprising power.
He hasn’t been the great liability in coverage we expected him to be. The coaches just aren’t using him much in coverage; they are blitzing him instead.
It’s one of the things that he does best. Credit to the coaches for putting McFadden in positive positions, and to McFadden for capitalizing on these opportunities.
Coming off the three-year extension that the Giants gave him this past week, Newsome played a top-notch, all-around corner game, excelling in both press and zone coverages.
One of his deep coverages should have drawn an offensive pass interference flag, as Newsome’s positioning was textbook and drew multiple tugs and contact from the…

title: Giants Expect J.J. McCarthy and Cam Skattebo Back for Thursday Night vs. Commanders
full_text:
The New York Giants don’t have much time before they host the Washington Commanders in a critical Thursday night divisional game.
But Big Blue can at least take some solace knowing that two key injured starters, quarterback J.J. McCarthy and running back Cam Skattebo, both should be good to go for that game.
McCarthy was injured in the third quarter when Eagles linebacker Zack Baun hit him on the side. McCarthy went to the medical tent for evaluation before walking to the locker room with members of the team’s medical staff, presumably to have X-rays done.
McCarthy, who was replaced by Jameis Winston for a series in which Winston led the Giants to the go-ahead touchdown, later returned to the team’s sideline with renewed energy. He then went back in to finish the game.
“He’s doing well,” head coach John Harbaugh said of McCarthy. “We’ll find out more during the course of the day and in a couple of days, but it does look like he’s gonna play. We feel fairly good about that but don’t want to get out over my skis with it, but it seems good so far.”
Skattebo is also trending in the right direction, according to Harbaugh. The second-year running back has been nursing a hamstring strain suffered on his final run in the Giants’ Week 7 win over the Houston Texans.
He was close to playing against the Eagles despite not practicing in the week leading up to the game and being listed as doubtful.
Ultimately, the team decided that with the quick turnaround and Skattebo likely to be slightly limited, it made more sense to hold him out of the game against the Eagles and instead aim for him to be ready for the Washington game.
“We just decided not to take the risk that would go with it,” Harbaugh said. “There were some things he was gonna be limited just a little bit; maybe that we decided not to go down that road because of the short week this week.”
The Giants running game struggled against the Eagles, finishing with a dismal 2.6 yards per carry. While that was largely a result of the poo run blocking effort by the offensive line, not having Skattebo in the lineup certainly didn't help matters.
The Giants head coach added that Skattebo “should be full-go Thursday night.”

title: Giants-Jaguars Week 11 Game Flexed to National TV Spot
full_text:
Ah, the joys of playing winning football.
The New York Giants' Week 11 home game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, originally slated for a 1 p.m. kickoff, has been moved to a 4:25 p.m. start and will now be nationally televised, replacing the Eagles-Steelers game that was originally scheduled for the 4:25 p.m. slot and was to be nationally broadcast.
The Giants, who just beat the Eagles 19-11 in Philly to snap a 13-year losing streak at Philly’s home stadium, stand at 5-2-1 and are comfortably in control of the NFC East.  Meanwhile, the Jaguars hold a 6-2 record and first control of the AFC South.
The Giants and Jaguars have played each other eight times in regular-season history, with the series deadlocked at 4-4. The two teams last met at MetLife Stadium on September 9, 2018, when the Giants lost 20-15 in what was their first home loss to Jacksonville in series history.
More recently, the two teams last met on October 13, 2022, when the Giants won 23-17 in what was their first road win against the Jaguars.
Jacksonville has outscored the Giants 190-161 in the eight games played between the two teams.

title: Four Key Factors in Giants' 19-11 Win Over Eagles
full_text:
For the first time in 13 long years, the New York Giants breathed a sigh of relief as they walked off the turf at Lincoln Financial Field after a 19-11 road win against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Taking down their rivals in the Eagles’ fiery home environment was once again no easy task for John Harbaugh’s Giants. Still, the outcome carried far more significance than simply casting away the nightmarish matchups with their most hated opponents from before he arrived as head coach.
With a rare win on their return from a bye week, the Giants got nearly the perfect scenario they asked for in the lead-up to Week 9: they beat the Birds to add another important win to their division tally and saw two other NFC East members fall on Sunday.
The Giants will definitely celebrate their overdue occasion. Still, they know they have a lot to improve, with a short week ahead and a second duel with the Washington Commanders on Thursday night at MetLife Stadium.
In the spirit of recognizing what got them to 5-2-1 this week, here are the four things that defined a special yet gritty win for New York over the Eagles.
The Giants had their ups and downs on offense, but the defense had to have left defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson grinning ear to ear as his group put on a clinic against the Eagles’ offensive line.
In a game where points were at a premium and both teams’ offenses struggled to play complementary football, the Giants’ defense kept New York within striking distance of the lead with a total onslaught of pressure toward Philadelphia quarterback Joe Milton.
New York held the Eagles to 220 total yards on Sunday, the lowest total in a single game this season. Against the pass, Milton and company managed just 128 yards and were held out of the end zone, thanks to eight drives stalled in fewer than three plays.
Even on possessions where Philadelphia tried to make something happen, Milton barely had room to breathe as the Giants’ pass rush got home for a season-high eight sacks, plus five more hits and another season high of 25 total pressures .
The biggest hero of the day? None other than rookie inside linebacker Arvell Reese, who put forth arguably the best day of his debut year with three pressures, all of them sacks, and pressured Milton on a team-high 23.1% of his pass-rushing snaps.
Milton certainly won’t be forgetting the one blow he took from Reese on 3rd-and-5 from the Giants’ 42-yard line in the early second quarter, which jarred the football loose for Micah McFadden to recover and kept New York’s deficit at 8-6.
The Giants also did a solid job against the run, holding Saquon Barkley and the Eagles to under 100 yards, a modest average of 3.7 yards per carry and one touchdown in the first quarter.
Still, the pass-rushing department deserved all the praise for never giving Philadelphia a chance to really hurt the Giants through the air. Reese has been a true draft win for Big Blue, and the sky is the limit if he keeps performing at a high level.
There was real concern when J.J. McCarthy had to leave the game with what was reported as a right-side rib injury that affected his ability to throw clean passes on the sidelines.
The injury happened on the second play of the Giants’ first possession in the third quarter, when McCarthy pulled the football and took off downfield for a three-yard gain on a left-side quarterback keeper.
Eagles inside linebacker Zack Baun came up to make the big hit on McCarthy and stop a potential big conversion by No. 18. Still, the impact left the Giants’ gunslinger grimacing in pain as he tried to shake off the blow, forcing Harbaugh to turn to Jameis Winston.
It’s been a back-and-forth year for Winston, who was benched for McCarthy in Week 7 ahead of the game in Houston. Once again, the veteran reminded Giants fans why a demotion didn’t mean he wasn’t still valuable to the franchise.
Just the opposite: Winston led the huddle back out on the next possession and authored an impressive 14-play, 76-yard drive, connecting with five different receivers and even flashing his legs with a 10-yard scamper for a first-down conversion.
Despite fears the Eagles’ relentless pass rush would get home to a less mobile quarterback with ease, Winston’s poise under center paid off with a five-yard connection to a wide-open Isaiah Likely in the back of the end zone on 2nd-and-goal from the Philadelphia 5-yard line that put the Giants back up 13-8.
On the next drive, McCarthy was cleared to return to the game, and the Giants never gave up the lead the rest of the way. Winston salvaged what could have been a bad turning point for Big Blue, going 6-of-8 for 71 yards with the Giants’ lone touchdown pass to Likely, and was arguably the biggest difference maker in the win.
It could have easily gone the other way, but the Giants wanted to keep Winston as the initial backup signal-caller for a reason. That experience showed again as the Giants didn’t let a sudden injury derail their chances of winning a football game.
After watching their rookie struggle to cash in on opportunities during a three-week skid, Dominic Zvada was back to being rock solid in the Giants’ kicking department.
In his first four games, the undrafted kicker looked like he’d been doing it forever, converting all nine field goal attempts, including a perfect 3-of-3 from 40 yards or more.
The Michigan product’s first taste of adversity came against Washington, where he missed three from that range. It opened a rough stretch of five total botched kicks in two of the team’s next three contests, against the Saints and Texans.
Perhaps the bye week was just what the doctor ordered for Zvada, who stepped into an unfriendly environment in Philadelphia and was lights out.
He made all four of his field goal attempts, including two from 49 yards and one from a game-high 53 yards on the Giants’ first two possessions.
New York has had to witness some unfortunate kicking miscues inside Lincoln Financial Field during its 13 years of losing in that stadium. Still, Zvada wasn’t going to add his name to the list of misfortunes that cost his franchise.
Without his improved long-range performance, the Giants wouldn’t have walked away with the win, and their NFC East chase would look very different, with the Cowboys playing catch-up at 4-5 after their win over the Colts.
The big question is whether Zvada can keep his efficiency in Thursday night’s game against Washington. If he is called upon to help put up points, he can’t let what happened in Week 5 haunt his confidence in the rematch.
The lead-up to the NFL trade deadline has focused on whether Harbaugh and the Giants will target a big-name running back to strengthen their rotation for a deep season run.
The group’s limited effort against the Eagles didn’t quiet the noise. The running back room was pretty much down to Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers Jr., who was just picked up from the Chargers’ practice squad, backing up the veteran in the absence of Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy Jr.
Still, the pair of backs, joined by six combined keepers from McCarthy and Winston, couldn’t get the job done for New York. The Giants finished with 80 yards on 31 total carries for an average of 2.6 yards per attempt, the second-lowest in a game this season.
Many of the rushing woes could also be attributed to the utter dominance that Philadelphia’s defensive front displayed in clogging the interior lanes and pushing the offensive linemen back into the plays.
Beyond that, the Giants surely realized how much they missed Skattebo, whose aggressive running style is huge for shaking up early tackles and gaining extra yards that take pressure off the passing game to convert longer second or third downs and keep drives alive.
Skattebo was likely disappointed he couldn’t return to the same stadium where his rookie season was cut short by an ankle injury in Week 8 of 2025. Still, one could wonder how effective he would have been, given the run-stop success the Eagles produced at…

title: Giants Winners and Losers: Arvell Reese Dominates as Giants End Long Drought in Philly
full_text:
The Big Blue football world was a very different place the last time the New York Giants beat the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 27, 2013.
Eli Manning was still the starting quarterback and Tom Coughlin the head coach. The Giants were two seasons removed from a Super Bowl championship. Offensive lineman Justin Pugh was a rookie. Victor Cruz was salsa-ing his way into the hearts of Giants fans. And fans were getting down with JPP (Jason Pierre-Paul).
Yes, it’s been a long time, but the winless drought in Philadelphia is finally over for the Giants. Relying on old-school physicality and timely completions, Big Blue earned a 19-11 road win over their longstanding foe.
It wasn’t perfect, but it was the desired result. So let’s look back at those who really stood out and those who didn’t.
The No. 5 overall pick has emerged as the Defensive Rookie of the Year favorite before the Giants battled the Eagles. Still, he solidified himself as one of the league’s top linebackers this season after a dominant showing in Philly.
Arvell Reese was instantly labeled a draft-day steal not only because of his run-stopping ability, which he displayed again, but also because of his pass-rushing prowess. That was also on display Sunday afternoon.
Reese registered three sacks, 10 solo tackles and a forced fumble, posting the best game of a young yet highly promising NFL career. He continues to move with force and speed, a brutal combination that terrorized Joe Milton III and the Eagles’ offensive line.
Dennard Wilson’s defense was excellent overall, but No. 52 claimed most of the spotlight. When a 21-year-old with limited NFL experience can carry a unit to a divisional victory, the future should be bright. Heck, the present is already looking quite sunny, and Reese is a big reason why.
The 32-year-old defensive tackle who signed with the organization almost two months after free agency began has become one of the team’s most important players .
Reader has been a pillar of consistency for the Giants, and Week 9 was no different. He recorded his first sack of the year in the first quarter and had four total pressures , per Pro Football Focus.
Reader is helping New York’s run defense gradually leave the NFL’s bottom tier and inch toward adequate territory.
The veteran wide receiver’s stock has fallen since he joined the franchise, but he can still produce in spurts. Darnell Mooney was arguably the Giants’ most dependable and clutch pass-catcher against the Eagles.
The 29-year-old deep threat linked up with Jameis Winston for a critical 27-yard reception in the third quarter on what became the go-ahead drive. He finished with a team-high 54 receiving yards, averaging 18.0 yards per catch.
New York already feels good about Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely, and there is plenty to like about rookie Malachi Fields. If Mooney can occasionally do damage downfield, then a previously listless pass-catching group may actually be quite stout.
Fresh off signing a three-year, $46 million contract extension , Greg Newsome II made his presence known in coverage and against the run. He allowed two receptions on four targets for a measly 13 yards and posted three stops, according to PFF.
Newsome is showing great awareness on the field, staying close to WRs and adjusting as a tackler when necessary. No longer a question mark, the sixth-year cornerback is a stabilizing force in the secondary.
The unpredictable signal-caller was under center for only one complete series, but he maximized his playing time and delivered the difference-making drive.
While J.J. McCarthy nursed a hip injury , Winston gashed the Eagles’ defense. He made stellar throws to Mooney and Fields, did not get rattled, and found Likely for a five-yard touchdown.
His 71-yard outing gifted the G-Men a 13-8 lead, which is all a dialed-in defense needed to secure the W. There are obvious drawbacks to employing Winston as a regular starter, but at his best , he can make momentum-swinging plays. He might get the chance to do so again if McCarthy is forced to miss time.
We cannot overlook the undrafted rookie kicker. Dominic Zvada has been in the “Losers” lounge lately, but he showed incredible mental fortitude by bouncing back and converting all four of his field goal attempts.
Given the offense’s scuffles, New York would not have won without Zvada. He drilled a 53-yarder less than five minutes into the game and added two 49-yarders, the second of which put the Giants up two possessions with 4:24 left.
Few kickers can save themselves from free fall and enjoy a midseason turnaround. Zvada is back on an upward trajectory.
Jon Runyan Jr. is one of two guards in this category, but I need to make something clear. Almost the entire offensive line could be here. Even Andrew Thomas struggled to contain Philly’s front seven. The interior, however, had an especially tough time.
Runyan surrendered four pressures , three of which were hurries. His showing in fact continues to raise questions as to why the Giants inked him to a two-year, $22 million extension in September that included new money.
Backup quarterbacks and injury-ravaged backfields require more support from the O-line. Runyan was undoubtedly the biggest part of the interior offensive line that didn’t bring its A-game to the party this week.
After enjoying arguably the best game of his rookie campaign in Week 7, Francis Mauigoa struggled against the Eagles' more physically dominating defensive front.
He was overpowered at various points during this divisional clash. The 21-year-old right guard allowed one sack and one other pressure , but he still looked outmatched far too often. His run blocking, like that of his fellow interior offensive linemen, was atrocious, MAuigoa earning a season-low 39.9 mark from PFF.
Better days will come, just as one did in Week 7, but until then, Mauigoa will continue to experience growing pains.
The Giants hoped for the best with putting Jones out there despite the hand injury that kept him on the injury report all week.
The decision nearly hurt them. Jones failed to track a ball early in the second quarter, but he tried to catch it anyway. His bold attempt to salvage the play resulted in a muffed punt that gave the Eagles possession on the Giants’ 47-yard line.
Fortunately, a ford fumble by Arvell Reese spared Jones further embarrassment and kept New York within two points.
Jones is hurting, and the Giants are short on viable returners, so there may not be a quick fix. At the very least, they must keep the ball off the ground.

title: Jets Rookie & Sophomore Power Rankings: New Face Takes Over the Top Spot Before Week 10
full_text:
Unsurprisingly, the Jets' skid has reached four games after losing 35-12 to the Chiefs on Sunday . Questionable coaching decisions, poor execution, and failing to score a touchdown in the red zone were just a few of the ongoing issues that continue to show up in the team’s losses.
With the loss, New York drops to 2-7, and head coach Aaron Glenn is now 5-21 since taking over in 2025. With the playoffs out of the horizon and Glenn all but out of a job after the season ends, there isn’t much to look forward to other than the young players.
Speaking of which, several rookies and sophomores stood out despite the team’s loss . With that said, let’s take a look at where they rank heading into Gang Green’s Week 10 matchup against the Bills.
Note: Anez Cooper and VJ Payne are currently excluded from the list. Cooper is on injured reserve but is eligible to return after missing the first four games of the season. Meanwhile, Payne hasn’t played in a game.
Barring a Garrett Wilson trade request in the offseason, he should be among the Jets’ top receiving options in 2027, alongside Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell. Isaiah Williams could also be in the mix, but he’ll have to earn that spot. The same goes for Arian Smith.
Although he couldn’t prove his worth this season, Smith’s play was extremely underwhelming in his rookie campaign, recording just seven receptions for 52 yards.
With New York likely to strengthen the receiver corps in the offseason, Smith is unlikely to remain with Gang Green unless he makes significant progress as a receiver.
With each Jets loss, Cade Klubnik’s chances of playing this season increase. After Sunday’s defeat, his odds have reached an all-time high.
Even though Geno Smith wasn’t to blame for the loss, New York simply has no incentive to continue putting him out there. He’s shown that he can still play at a high level and lead an offense, but the Jets’ coaching and the team’s poor execution consistently let him down.
As long as Glenn remains head coach, they likely won’t turn to Klubnik anytime soon, as Glenn needs wins to secure his job. But if things continue as they have been, don’t be surprised if they name Klubnik the starter coming out of the bye week against Denver.
A five-game sample against some of the league's best defenses should give New York a better idea of what it has in him.
Kiko Mauigoa has been on the injured reserve since reinjuring his quad in Week 6 against the Patriots.
In the three games the former 2025 fifth-round selection appeared in, Mauigoa exclusively played on special teams, as New York has primarily stuck with two inside linebackers this season. But with the Jets continuing to drop games, there’s a chance Mauigoa could earn reps on defense if he returns this season.
With Demario Davis continuing to show that he’s regressed dramatically this season, it’s time the team tried someone else alongside Jamien Sherwood. Mauigoa could be an option.
Andre Cisco had been the Jets’ third safety behind Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick.
But things seemed to change on Sunday, when Malachi Moore received a season-high 17 defensive snaps against the Chiefs while Cisco exclusively played on special teams. While some may have viewed this as a reward for his incredible performance on special teams, posting eight tackles and earning a 79.9 special teams grade , per Pro Football Focus , it was actually an effort to keep Cisco healthy before eventually trading him to the Lions on Monday afternoon.
Playing his first defensive snaps since Week 5, the former 2025 fourth-round selection didn’t necessarily stand out, recording just one tackle and allowing a catch for 19 yards in 12 coverage snaps.
Even with Cisco gone, it doesn’t guarantee Moore as the backup safety. With rookie VJ Payne making his return to practice last week, Moore must continue to make the most of his opportunity.
The Jets’ usage of D’Angelo Ponds has been intriguing, to say the least.
Since returning from a calf injury in Week 3, Ponds has played sparingly, appearing in just 87 defensive snaps across seven games.
The former Indiana Hoosier played in a season-high 30 snaps in Week 7’s matchup against the Dolphins, playing particularly well against the run, before seeing just one snap against the Raiders last week
On Sunday, Ponds played 22 snaps, recording two tackles and giving up a touchdown. He also committed a costly illegal contact penalty on third-and-11; however, David Bailey forced a turnover two plays later.
Even though it was an underwhelming game from Ponds, we must cut him some slack. He’s transitioning from outside corner to nickelback, a position at which he lined up at just 28 times in college.
Ponds will experience more growing pains, and New York must learn to live with it by giving him consistent playing time. It's the only way he’ll develop.
Kenyon Sadiq was more involved in New York’s loss to Kansas City than he’d been the past few weeks, but not all of it was for the right reasons.
The former Oregon Duck hauled in all four of his targets for 49 yards, finishing second on the team behind Omar Cooper Jr.
Kenyon Sadiq makin it look easy 📺: #NYJvsKC on @NFLonCBS | @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/VzYXDSx5VU
The bad news is that Sadiq was penalized twice.
His first penalty came on the opening drive, where he committed a false start in Chiefs’ territory. This wasn’t costly, as New York came away with three points. Meanwhile, his second penalty did cost the Jets points.
On second-and-five with 53 seconds left in the first half at Kansas City’s 25, Sadiq was called for a facemask penalty, negating a seven-yard run by Breece Hall. Although the Jets still managed to stay in field goal range, Jason Sanders missed a 53-yard kick.
The two flags shouldn’t draw major concerns, but Sadiq must learn from his mistakes.
Mason Taylor played extremely well in his first three games back from a thumb injury, recording 12 catches for 114 yards and two touchdowns.
In the past two games, however, the former LSU Tiger has been quiet, posting just four receptions for 30 yards. Although Taylor wasn’t involved much in the passing game in the team’s loss to Kansas City, he ended up hurting the Jets with two costly penalties.
His first penalty was a false start in Chiefs’ territory, which stalled the drive and led the Jets to kick a field goal. Down nine in the third quarter, Taylor was called for an illegal shift on third-and-four, negating a 19-yard reception by Adonai Mitchell. On the next play, Smith was sacked on third-and-nine, and New York was forced to punt.
Although his penalties weren’t the reason for New York’s loss, Taylor must clean things up moving forward.
Despite playing a career-high 47 defensive snaps against the Chiefs, Darrell Jackson Jr. was relatively quiet, recording just three tackles and one pressure.
His presence in the middle is critical, with David Onyemata and T’Vondre Sweat on the injured reserve. However, Jackson and the Jets' defensive line struggled against Kenneth Walker and Kansas City’s ground game, which combined for 163 rushing yards on 32 carries.
Even though Jackson hasn’t consistently made noteworthy plays, he’s displayed flashes of being a quality rotational player. Between his run stuff on fourth down against Las Vegas last week and his two batted passes and a sack against the Browns, Jackson is a player worth keeping an eye on over the next few weeks.
After starting the season strong in coverage, Azareye’h Thomas’ play has taken a significant step backward over the past few weeks.
The former 2025 third-round selection struggled to cover Kansas City’s pass-catchers, allowing five catches (six targets) for 63 yards and earning a 48.3 coverage grade , per PFF . His worst play came on the first play of the Chiefs’ ninth offensive drive, where he got burnt by 37-year-old Travis Kelce for 38 yards.
Thomas wasn’t even close to Kelce when he caught it, and he just looked completely lost several times. He didn’t fare any better…

title: Jets Could Be Sneaky Winners After Falcons & Eagles Deadline Trades
full_text:
If the Jets decide to do nothing by the NFL's trade deadline , they will still be set up for success in a major way going into 2027 and beyond. That's what happens when you own three first-round picks in the upcoming draft.
But that also doesn't mean the team can't be affected by other trades that happen around the NFL.
The Falcons and Eagles made major headlines on Monday afternoon when they traded key pieces on their defense to the Jaguars. First, it was Jessie Bates leaving Atlanta for the top price of a second-round pick. Then, defensive tackle Jordan Davis was shipped out for a first- and second-round pick to Philadelphia.
The Jaguars aren't something the Jets will have to worry about come draft day, but the deals they made with the Eagles and Falcons could actually help Gang Green moving forward.
At first glance, the Eagles selling off top talent and acquiring an extra first-round pick can be seen as a problem for the Jets . Philadelphia could very well take a quarterback to restart their true rebuild and that takes New York out of the equation, especially with the Eagles slated for the fifth pick if the year ended today.
But if the Eagles' losses continue (almost a certainty due to their rash of injuries), the team's needs are a perfect pairing for a team like the Jets.
Philadelphia needs defensive line and offensive line help. With Jalen Hurts under contract and expected to return from his blood clots, the team could keep him on the roster in 2027 and punt their quarterback debate for 2028. Should that happen, the Eagles could simply trade back with their current top pick to a quarterback-needy team... like the Jets.
The same could be said about Atlanta as well. The Falcons do not own an additional first-round pick, so even if they finish ahead of the Jets in the 2027 draft order, New York has plenty of ammo to move up ahead of them.
In a race to get the top quarterbacks of this upcoming draft class, you want to be a team like the Jets with three picks slated in the top 15 overall picks compared to the Falcons or even the Eagles.
And if the Eagles keep losing, it's far more likely they trade out of their top pick to acquire more capital, which is perfectly fine for the Jets.
Much of these two trades have little to no effect on the Jets, but the biggest pieces of news surrounding these organizations that matter most will be the health of Hurts beyond his current blood clot problems.
The Eagles believe that Hurts will be back to 100% by the end of the year once he comes off blood thinners, but there's no guarantee that will solve the problem. The team could look to trade for a top veteran on the open market, but they could also draft a quarterback.
With the Eagles as bad as they are, the most important update for Jets fans and the organization will be about Hurts.
The good news for New York is that they remain in a strong position to draft a quarterback regardless of what Philadelphia does. Indianapolis continues to crumble and could trade Jonathan Taylor this afternoon, and Dallas has struggled with mediocrity throughout the season. Gang Green could be looking at three picks inside the top 15, and two inside the top five by season's end.
It's more than enough ammo to transform their roster going forward.

title: Jets NFL Trade Deadline Tracker: Trades, Rumors and Latest News

title: 3 Jets Most Likely to be Traded Next After Andre Cisco
full_text:
The trade deadline is almost here. The Jets remain steadfast in their belief in standing pat without trading key players who can make them better.
At least that's what their coaching staff said on Monday morning. Later in the afternoon, the Jets sent safety Andre Cisco to Detroit for a sixth-round pick in 2028. Cisco was on an expiring deal coming into the year and was benched halfway through the team's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
He may not be the only one on the move either. In fact, there are three other players who could end up being traded later this afternoon.
Phillips fits the mold that Cisco had: a player on an expiring deal who deserves to play for a Super Bowl contender. A defensive captain, Phillips has struggled mightily throughout the start of the season under head coach Aaron Glenn.
With the Jaguars already sending first-, second- and sixth-round picks for two defensive tackles, it's clear that there is a robust market for tackles around the league. Phillips won't command a lot, but he would be the kind of veteran move that the Jets should make for his sake.
No veteran should have to sit through a 2-8 season like this.
Unlike Phillips, McDonald has an extra year under contract and has already requested a trade.
New York doesn't have to move him, and has already spoken out about their desire not to. But if a team blows them away with an offer, especially one that rises to as high as a second-round pick, then the Jets should do everything possible to move the former first-round pick.
There will always be a market for players who can rush the quarterback. McDonald, despite a down year, has a 10-sack season under his belt. Moving on should give the Jets quality draft capital and give McDonald the change of scenery he wants.
For Brownlee, it really comes down to what the Jets plan on doing for the remainder of the year. Like McDonald, he has an additional year on his current contract, but unlike McDonald, he has already been replaced on the Jets roster.
New York started D'Angelo Ponds at nickel on Sunday in their loss to Kansas City. Because of that, it's fair to wonder whether the Jets will simply move on from Brownlee to allow Ponds to get full reps as the starter in the slot for the remainder of the year.
The reason why New York wouldn't make a move, though, is that Gang Green is willing to try Ponds on the boundary (his natural position) and wants to move Brownlee back into the slot.
That's for the next coaching staff to decide, though. For now, it seems Brownlee isn't part of the team's current or future plans.

title: Biggest Decision Aaron Glenn Got Wrong vs. Chiefs (And What Needs to Change in Week 10)
full_text:
Even though they scored on each of their first three possessions on Sunday, the Jets put together another blunder in a 35-12 loss to the Chiefs that produced their fourth consecutive loss and dropped their record to 2-7 this season.
Even though there were still some concerns on the injury report coming in with WR1 Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined, RB1 Breece Hall returned from a five-week absence due to a quad injury and rookie David Bailey (groin) responded from his one-game absence with a vengeance by recording nine tackles (five solo), two sacks and two forced fumbles, including this one on Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter (h/t SNY Jets).
David Bailey forces the fumble and the Jets recover! Patrick Mahomes walked off the field in pain after the hit pic.twitter.com/NQaGRnyR2N
Despite the strong first half from the run game and the efficiency that kicker Jason Sanders continues to display after going 4-of-5 and scoring all 12 of Gang Green's points on Sunday, the Jets were unable to keep pace for the duration of the game as head coach Andy Reid and the Chiefs adjusted accordingly and blew the game open in the second half.
While Sanders deserves some credit for keeping the Jets afloat in the game, head coach Aaron Glenn relied too much on him, as he appeared more intent on not losing the game instead of making the aggressive plays to win it. The Jets ran 44 plays to just 25 from Kansas City in the opening half of Sunday's game, only to settle for five field goals and commit a fumble on the first play of their fourth drive.
The decision by Glenn and offensive coordinator Frank Reich to kick field goals instead of putting the ball in QB Geno Smith's hands to make a play kept them from making the explosive ones needed to compete with the Chiefs.
Combine that with the undisciplined play in the second half, and it is clear why the Jets ended up getting blown out .
Sure, Reich is the one running this offense, but he and Glenn have got to do a better job collectively of making some on-the-spot decisions to be more aggressive when the opportunity arises. After all, the Jets marched down the field on a 14-play, 64-yard drive that took more than eight minutes off the clock on their opening drive, only to get down to goal-to-go territory and settle for the chip-shot field goal.
Granted, you can't argue with taking the points on a fourth-and-14 or a fourth-and-15 later in the half, but there was no reason to take the conservative approach from just five yards out in a game they were not expected to win anyway.
The same could also apply to the drive immediately following the forced fumble from the defense when the offense went three-and-out and took the points on a fourth-and-6 from the 30-yard-line. They also elected to kick a 54-yarder prior to the two-minute warning instead of going for it on a fourth-and-seven at the 36-yard-line.
Yes, Sanders capitalized on those opportunities and only missed one of his five attempts, but you would certainly like to see the Jets get aggressive in those spots and play to win the game, especially considering the direction their season continues to head. Nonetheless, the second half ensued and that lack of aggressiveness came back to bite this coaching staff .
After going 64 yards on their opening drive alone, the Jets only mustered a combined 46 yards of total offense in the second half and had no answers for what the Chiefs threw at them. The lack of adjustments to account for that forced the offense to abandon the run game and become more one-dimensional as the game started to slip away.
"It’s disappointing, the only thing we can do is go back to work and try to figure out how can I, as the head coach, get us to play two halves at a high level and not have a lull at any part of the game," Glenn said, per Jets on SI's Nick Faria . "That’s something I’ll think long and hard about to make sure I get that done. A lot of thinking to do. A lot of thinking to do. Just look forward to getting back to work."
As the Jets return home to MetLife Stadium to face the Bills in another divisional game on Sunday, another stiff test awaits against the league's highest-scoring offense (33.3 ppg). Considering the issues the Jets have had getting off the field and Glenn's 0-8 record against AFC East opponents, it is hard to envision anything close to a win taking place.
From the third-down struggles (2-of-12), red-zone issues and lack of protection with five sacks allowed, to the inability to get off the field defensively and the nine penalties for 57 yards, there were too many mistakes from this Jets team to have any business beating the Chiefs.
As the attention shifts to the Bills, the penalties have to be corrected, the red-zone aggressiveness needs to be dialed up and the efficiency on both sides of the ball must be cleaned up in order for the drives to be sustained offensively and for the defense to get off the field in third-down situations.
If the Jets are going to have any chance against Buffalo, there has to be better execution and timely coaching adjustments going into the second half. If that is not the case, it could go from bad to worse for a team that may want to just focus its attention on the draft at this point.

title: Instant Grade: Jets Trade Safety Andre Cisco to Lions
full_text:
With the Jets dropping to 2-7 after Sunday’s 35-12 loss to the Chiefs , it became increasingly clear that New York would be in selling mode heading into Tuesday’s trade deadline.
Breece Hall and Will McDonald IV are viewed as the Jets’ top trade candidates despite claims from head coach Aaron Glenn that the team isn’t interested in trading either player . With Glenn compiling a 5-21 record and New York on the verge of missing the playoffs for the 16th consecutive season, his word doesn’t carry as much weight as it once did.
Instead of Hall or McDonald being the first domino to fall, it was safety Andre Cisco whom the Jets decided to move on from, trading him to the Lions for a 2028 sixth-round pick early Monday afternoon, per ESPN's Adam Schefter
Trade: Jets are sending S Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions for a 2028 6th-round pick, sources tell ESPN. Cisco’s on an expiring contract. pic.twitter.com/BkN4GUcl7q
With the deal now official, let’s take a look at the grade New York deserves for moving on from the six-year veteran.
The Jets moving on from Cisco isn’t much of a surprise.
Cisco, 26, was in his second season with the Jets, serving as a backup after losing the starting safety job to Dane Belton in training camp. In nine games (191 defensive snaps), Cisco recorded 23 tackles, one sack, and one forced fumble.
Although he was relied on early while Minkah Fitzpatrick missed Weeks 2 and 3 due to a groin injury, Cisco logged just 23 defensive snaps over the last six games and played exclusively on special teams against the Chiefs.
His diminished role, expiring contract and rookie safety VJ Payne’s return made Cisco expendable .
Of course, a sixth-round pick isn’t exactly a significant return, but it’s better than losing Cisco for nothing. Given his lack of involvement on defense, this was likely the best offer general manager Darren Mougey could have received.
Cisco arguably had the worst season of his career in 2025. Although his campaign was cut short by a shoulder injury, he wasn’t great in coverage.
In just 265 coverage snaps, Cisco allowed 14 receptions (17 targets) for 189 yards and three touchdowns, earning a 54.5 coverage grade , per Pro Football Focus. He also missed nine tackles, posting an 18.9% missed tackle rate, the highest of his career.
Those struggles, combined with his lack of interceptions, explain why he fell out of the rotation and why the Jets didn’t get a better selection in return.
For now, his departure opens up an opportunity for Malachi Moore, who has impressed on special teams , and Payne to prove they deserve a spot in the rotation heading into next season. With New York likely to move on from Glenn, both young safeties have a chance to make a strong impression on whoever takes over as head coach in 2027
With the deal settled, New York now has eight picks in the 2028 draft , according to Spotrac . This provides Mougey and the Jets’ brass additional draft capital to either add a developmental player or use it as a trade piece to address other roster needs.
Efstathios is a writer for OnSI covering the New York Jets. With a B.A. in Journalism from Roger Williams University, he's been in sports media for the last two years. Efstathios is also a contributor for Fansided's Local Network.

title: Why I Fully Trust Jets GM Darren Mougey Ahead of the Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Jets have been a rough watch in 2026. The team is 2-7 through nine weeks and appears headed for an 11th straight losing season. Despite that, the New York team still has hope: draft capital. The Jets currently hold nine picks in the 2027 draft , three of them first-rounders.
That is general manager Darren Mougey's doing.
Jets fans should continue to have faith in the second-year GM. Gang Green will likely sell at the deadline— as proven by Monday's Andre Cisco trade with the Lions —and Mougey has shown he can make a deal with the best of them.
The Jets are in good hands in the roster-building department, despite it not carrying over in the win-loss column just yet.
Darren Mougey has sent three former first-round picks out the door in his time as the Jets' GM. Early on, it seems as though Mougey got every one of those decisions right. The Jets parted with Quinnen Williams, Sauce Gardner, and Jermaine Johnson II in the past year; all three left the Jets on the better side of those trades.
Pro Football Focus has Williams (23rd), Gardner (48th), and Johnson (59th) all ranked outside the top 20 at their positions, marks they had met when they were in New York. Mougey seems to have gotten rid of talent that wasn't producing at just the right time.
Williams and Gardner were seen as franchise cornerstones before their respective trades. Now the Cowboys and Colts may have buyer's remorse. Gardner is having one of the worst seasons of his career. Williams isn't doing much better . Mougey seems to have shed bloated contracts at the perfect time.
Mougey got rid of two players who are being paid top-five numbers at their positions and one who was toward the end of a rookie contract. None of those players are currently performing like top players at their respective positions. The Jets GM has had to sell, and he's done it at the perfect times. With the deadline looming, expect him to sell again at the right time.
Fleece. That is one word people have used to describe the Jets' trades over the past year. Thanks to Mougey, the Jets currently hold three of the first 13 picks in the 2027 Draft. Mougey has made the most of his blockbuster trades so far, and should be itching to see what he can accomplish during this year's deadline.
The Jets used the first-round returns from the Gardner and Williams trades to land Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper Jr., who have shown flashes of stardom in their rookie seasons. Mougey has not parted with players cheaply. Rather, he has gotten the best possible return for the team. Even the Johnson trade netted the Jets T'Vondre Sweat , who is grading higher than his predecessor , Williams.
If Mougey has shown one thing during his tenure at the helm, it's that he can win trades. The Jets are currently watching the Colts' and Cowboys' seasons slip away with a smile on their face knowing that every loss means better draft capital for the team. Jets fans can trust that their GM is dedicated to being on the winning side, even though a blockbuster trade this season seems unlikely
Mougey has been the most productive member of the Jets' organization during his tenure as the GM. The man has gotten rid of players who were not worth their contracts and gotten the best return possible for them. The Jets should trust the man who has been able to produce six first-round draft picks in two years' time.
The Jets look better than last year despite an ever-present uphill climb in the win-loss department. Mougey is a huge reason for that improvement. As the trade deadline looms, fans and the organization should be happy that the 41-year-old GM is at the helm.
