title: Faria's Focus: 5 Jets Thoughts Following 4th Straight Loss (Trade Deadline, Long-Term Plans & More)
full_text:
The numbers speak for themselves. The outcomes speak for themselves.
Aaron Glenn's Jets are a bad football team . They showed it throughout their 35-12 loss at the hands of the Chiefs on Sunday . Whether it was their nine penalties, turnovers, or inability to play complementary football to an almost comical level, what can go wrong will go wrong for this team.
As always, it's time to give some thoughts following their fourth straight loss, and seventh in their last eight games. From Glenn's future employment problems to lone bright spots, there's a lot to discuss about what this team is and will be going forward.
There are a lot of problems with New York's coaching staff. Glenn is at the top of the list . Even when the team makes the right call—like challenging the Chiefs' third-down fumble—there's little done afterward to build on it.
The problem there is the fact that the Jets are selectively aggressive. On the opening drive, they reached a goal-to-go situation and felt like taking the field goal was acceptable. They were so focused on just dinking and dunking down the field that the team refused to take shots against Kansas City's defense until it was too late.
If Glenn and his staff want to be successful, they need to actually choose what kind of staff they want to be. At this rate, though, it really doesn't matter. Glenn's job is all but gone after an abysmal 5-21 start to his run with Gang Green. His inability to stay aggressive, or even get aggressive in the first place, will be one of many reasons why it failed.
As the Chiefs were running down the Jets' throats in the second half, I was left with one major thought.
David Bailey is an awesome draft pick, one that the Jets actually got right at such a high selection. But if the team is going to watch him reach T.J. Watt or Myles Garrett-level effectiveness, they need to put him in a better defense for his skill set.
Bailey recorded two sacks and two fumbles forced in Sunday's loss. He's now up to 7.5 sacks and five fumbles forced in eight games played—second-most in that span, behind Julius Peppers with the Panthers.
"No surprise, that is who he is," Glenn said of Bailey after the game. "Each game, he is learning and getting better. It’s good to see that. We expect him to make plays like that. We expect him to be on the field as much as he can and to do that."
At the time of the 2026 draft, the Jets were choosing between Bailey and Arvell Reese. Reese is on his way to another excellent rookie season and will get plenty of flowers after his three-sack effort against Philadelphia.
But Bailey has been as productive, if not more, in his first year. The Jets just need to put him in the kind of wide-nine alignment that will get the most out of his skill set as a pass rusher and someone who sets the edge nicely in run fronts.
When the team inevitably makes a coaching change at the end of the year, they should find a coordinator who will fit Bailey into the right scheme.
During the Jets' loss to Kansas City, it was clear that frustration was boiling over on the sideline. Quarterback Geno Smith and right tackle Armand Membou were both seen throwing their helmets to the ground in frustration (h/t Glenn Naughton).
Now it's Armand Membou's turn.  Allows a sack on 3rd down.  It's the fifth sack the @nyjets have allowed today. pic.twitter.com/CDWrJRzkIq
After the game, Smith clarified that his frustration came from trying to be better for his team.
“I was just frustrated with not getting it done. I am always the type of guy that is going to look inward," Smith said. "I am really just looking at myself and figuring out how I can be better for the guys and the team so we can get it done.”
Then came the aftermath. Not even 24 hours after the Jets' loss, edge rusher Will McDonald requested a trade to a better situation —one where he will play over 50% of the snaps compared to his time with the Jets.
McDonald is a good edge rusher, but it's obvious at this point he's not a fit for the defense Glenn wants to run. Should the head coach boast that his coaching plan would set the former first-round pick back dating to last year? Absolutely. But it's no use crying over spilled milk.
At this rate, the milk is spoiled; players in need of new contracts are going to start wanting out.
Smith and Membou aren't on that list. But it's evident the Jets have reached a tipping point under Glenn. With eight games left in the regular season, this may get a whole lot worse before it gets better.
We've already mentioned McDonald's trade request, but it highlights the Jets' bigger problems as a front office. They don't have much top talent to ship off, and any deadline fire sale will only muster a couple of late-round draft selections.
That doesn't mean the Jets should stand pact with where they are.
New York is going nowhere this season. All the players brought in to fit Glenn's mold of what a team should look like have failed. The Jets and general manager Darren Mougey should look to sell off some of their talent and try to get as much capital as they can for the next coaching staff when they come in during January.
Among the names are McDonald, Harrison Phillips, Nahshon Wright and Jarvis Brownlee. Breece Hall will be another name that is talked about in trades, but I get the sense the team wants to keep their 1-2 combination with Braelon Allen intact.
It's hard to tell if the Jets will actually make a move at the deadline this year, but if the last few weeks are any indication, they absolutely should.
We're at the point in the season where the Jets' outlook will not be based on wins, but on the quality of play from their young performers and on how high a draft pick they will be able to obtain.
New York should not be making any legitimate coaching changes either. If the Jets lose to the Bills on Sunday (expected considering their current four-game losing streak), they will drop to 2-8 for the year. It wouldn't make sense to make a coaching change then—it would be best for the team to ride out the final months of the Glenn era and then make a move once the season ends.
At 5-21, there's little hope that Glenn can turn around the program. He's been given two years to show improvement and hasn't. But if the Jets can get a top pick, then this era will not be a complete loss. It will, at the very least, set the next coaching staff up for success down the road.
But that also means Glenn needs to stay on to complete the team's troubled run. Any change, and the Jets risk missing out on a top pick.

title: Aaron Glenn Address Jets' Deadline Uncertainty Following Will McDonald IV's Trade Request
full_text:
Jets edge rusher Will McDonald made some breaking news Monday morning with a reported trade request following the team's loss to the Chiefs.
The former first-round edge rusher out of Iowa State has just three sacks on the season and has played under 50% of the snaps for the defense. Once a 10-sack defender, McDonald has been relegated to a situational role at best.
And now he wants to go to a place better suited for his talents.
But with a year of team control, the Jets don't appear so willing to get rid of a player they still have high hopes for.
Speaking to reporters on Monday morning, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn was clear about the team's outlook with McDonald: they weren't going to give him away just because the edge rusher is frustrated.
"I just know we're in the business of keeping good players, so Will's going to be here," Glenn said.
Glenn also added that he and McDonald had a "productive" conversation following Sunday's loss to Kansas City as well.
Glenn's productive conversations with McDonald can go all the way back to when the coach was first hired last season. During training camp, Glenn was asked why the Iowa State product had not broken out in a major way as a first-round pick.
A year and a half in, it seems Glenn and his current staff simply aren't cutting it when it comes to getting the most out of the team's players. With the trade deadline drawing nearer, the team's coaching struggles have highlighted several players who may be on the move.
But like McDonald, the Jets seem comfortable keeping everything as the status quo.
All the talk will be centered on McDonald after his trade request, but the Jets also have players on expiring deals who could use a change of scenery. Veterans like Harrison Phillips, Jarvis Brownlee, Nahshon Wright and even quarterback Geno Smith have been names that have been floated around.
On Monday, though, Glenn cleared the air on the team's plan going forward.
Of course, it's fair to point out that the Jets are in the same situation they were in last year and ended up trading Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams. Will the same thing happen in 2026? New York was able to get top draft capital for their best players last year, but that same talent isn't available this year.
Unless a team is willing to overpay for any of New York's starters, the team may not be willing to part with players for the return of a day three pick. McDonald may end up being the only one worthy of an overpay.
Even then, there's no guarantee the Jets will budge.

title: 5 Jets Awards to Give Out in Blowout Loss to Chiefs: Stars to David Bailey and the Colts
full_text:
Tell me if you heard this before: the New York Jets were outcoached and outplayed when it mattered most in another loss.
Gang Green dropped their seventh game in their last eight tries, the latest coming in a 35-12 shellacking by the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. New York was shut out in the second half and did not score a touchdown in their fourth straight loss.
We have five awards to give out, so let's get to it now.
Every time the Jets coaching staff makes a good decision, it's followed up by mind-boggling calls that clearly hold the team back. Whether it was kicking field goals in goal-to-go situations when the team needed a touchdown, or trying hard not to turn the ball over against the blitz and taking bad sacks when they could least afford, the Jets made calls throughout the game that kept them from winning.
If anything, Glenn and his staff coached not to lose Sunday's game compared to being aggressive enough to go and win it.
Even more alarming is the fact that there were several Jets players who seemingly let their emotions get the best of them. Whether it was Geno Smith screaming on the sideline, or Armand Membou committing a personal foul penalty for slamming his helmet down on the field of play, New York is unprepared and undisciplined when it matters most.
It's the clearest indictment against Glenn at this point.
"It's all about our process, to be honest with you," Glenn said. "It gets tough, I know it does, but it's the belief. We've shown spurts that we can play at a high level."
One of the lone bright spots from the Jets on Sunday was rookie David Bailey. The second overall pick in the 2026 draft recorded two sacks and two forced fumbles on the day. While his run defense remained inconsistent, the Jets got him in situations to succeed.
Through his first eight games in the NFL, Bailey has recorded 7.5 sacks and five forced fumbles. He has the most sacks through his first eight games as a first-round pick since Julius Peppers. Considering Peppers is a Hall of Famer, Bailey's start has been nothing short of special.
"It's always a blessing just getting out there and just playing football, playing the game I love," Bailey said.
He is heating this defensive rookie of the year award list up.
In the first half, the Jets offense had gone up and down the field against the Chiefs' mighty defense. While they didn't score a touchdown, there was hope the talent level on the unit would be good enough to keep things competitive.
Things only got worse, though.
New York lost the second half 21-0, and recorded just 46 yards of offense in the second half. To put that into perspective, the Jets recorded 64 yards in their first drive of the game - and failed to get close to that point in the second half. After seeing three straight 100-yard rushing games from Braelon Allen, the Jets gave him just seven carries on the day, while giving more carries to Breece Hall.
Those adjustments didn't work. It only capped the offense further.
"It’s disappointing, the only thing we can do is go back to work and try to figure out how can I, as the head coach, get us to play two halves at a high level and not have a lull at any part of the game," Glenn said. "That’s something I’ll think long and hard about to make sure I get that done. A lot of thinking to do. A lot of thinking to do. Just look forward to getting back to work."
New York was abysmal on Sunday, but its uncompetitive offensive performance in the second half was the worst of the worst.
The good? New York forced two turnovers today courtesy of fumbles forced by David Bailey & a muffed quarterback sneak.
The bad? They should've had at least three more fumble recoveries and have gone five straight games without an interception.
New York's inability to fall on the football has been well documented. Some of it is just poor football luck as a collective franchise. In other cases, especially with their lack of interceptions, it's a coaching problem as well. The Jets don't do enough to force mistakes by the opposition. When they do, they are unable to take advantage of those opportunities.
At the end of the day, it's just a further reason why the current staff is not up to par.
As the Jets continued to struggle against the Chiefs during the second half, they did get good news throughout. The Indianapolis Colts ended up losing to the Dallas Cowboys at home, dropping their record to 2-7 on the year.
By virtue of the Colts' loss, the Jets continue to own three of the top 13 picks including two inside the top six overall selections. As New York and the Colts continue to lose, especially with games against the Dolphins and Chargers ahead on their schedule, it's clear the Jets are going to have plenty of chances to get top players in the 2027 draft.
Things aren't going well for the team right now. But the draft offers a bit of hope.

title: McMullen: Jordan Davis Trade Cements Why Howie Roseman Is One of NFL's Best GMs
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Actions always speak louder than words.
Eight months after Howie Roseman handed Jordan Davis a three-year, $78 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid interior defensive linemen in football, the Eagles shipped him to Jacksonville for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round selection.
That isn’t just a roster tweak. It’s a clear signal that Philadelphia would rather build around Moro Ojomo than live with the massive commitment they just made to Davis.
An NFL source confirmed to Eagles On SI what the market already suggested: the Jaguars checked in on Ojomo first. They were told he wasn’t available. From there, the talks evolved to the point that the Eagles were willing to part with Davis , as long as James Gladstone played into his reputation for the overpay.
Behind the scenes, the Eagles’ posture for weeks had been that Ojomo was staying. However, most considered that to be straight out of the Roseman playbook of shooting for the stars in an attempt to generate a second-round pick for the Texas product.
The trade of Davis confirms Philadelphia is choosing the younger, cheaper, more versatile player they can actually keep next to Carter long-term.
This is also a clear indication that the Eagles believe this will be defensive coordinator Vic Fangio’s last season in Philadelphia. Fangio always wants a pure nose tackle he can plug into variable fronts when needed.
Davis was that guy—the space-eating, two-gap presence who lets Fangio play the light-box looks and disguise coverages he’s built his reputation on. When the production didn’t match the contract this year, it makes sense that the organization decided it wasn’t worth locking into that personnel profile for the next three seasons if Fangio isn’t going to be the one drawing it up.
The disappointment in Davis’ 2026 tape is real. After a career year in 2025—career highs in sacks, tackles for loss, and overall disruption—the Eagles thought he had turned the corner as a more complete player. Instead, he’s been a solid-but-limited run-stuffer who has struggled to stay in ideal condition and has barely played on third down unless it’s short-yardage.
Through nine games, he ranked third among Eagles defensive tackles in snaps behind Carter and Ojomo. On obvious passing downs he has been a non-factor for most of his career.
That’s not the profile you pay $26 million a year to keep when you already have Carter locked up on a much bigger deal and a rising player like Ojomo ready to take a bigger role.
Roseman should take a hit for crafting the original extension but recovered quickly by continuing to tap into the same market inefficiency he’s exploited for years: the systematic devaluation of future draft capital.
The 2029 second-round pick is the kind of asset most GMs treat as monopoly money. Roseman treats it like currency .
Ultimately, Davis is a two-down player who generated a little less than what the Titans extracted for Jeffery Simmons—a more accomplished, higher-usage player who fetched two firsts and a fourth.
The Jaguars may win a Super Bowl this year after loading up with Davis, safety Jessie Bates, and defensive tackle Davon Godchaux. That doesn’t change the fact that this is one of the biggest overpayments we’ve seen in years. Jacksonville is paying a premium for a two-down player,
Former NFL executive Andrew Brandt noted that a general manager with a business and negotiating background like Roseman will continue to take advantage of GMs whose backgrounds are primarily scouting or personnel.
This trade seems to be the latest example of that.

title: Eagles NFL Trade Deadline Tracker: Trades, Rumors, and Latest News
full_text:
Before the 2026 NFL season, few people expected the Eagles to be in seller mode at the NFL trade deadline . After all, Philadelphia was coming off four consecutive 11-plus-win seasons, which included two Super Bowl appearances and one win. Fast-forward to Tuesday, though, and the Eagles are 2-7 and at the bottom of the NFC East, leaving general manager Howie Roseman with only one option this week .
It's rare that the Eagles are in a position to acquire so much draft capital, but doing so will put them in a solid spot to return to prominence next season. That's why Roseman & Co. must effectively figure out who no longer fits with the team's long-term plans and move on before it's too late.
Here's are the lates rumors and news surrounding the Eagles now that the NFL trade deadline is here.
UPDATE (Nov. 10, 12:28 p.m. ET): In a major twist, NFL insider Jordan Schultz is reporting that the Eagles-Bengals trade for Ebiketie will no longer be going through . Rapoport followed up by saying that Cincinnati called off the trade to avoid losing a compensatory pick.
The #Bengals have now called off this trade with an eye toward keeping a future comp pick they would've lost with this deal. Agreement was reached, but not official. https://t.co/Fhe51RD7TP
Just before 11 a.m. ET on Tuesday, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that the Eagles are trading veteran EDGE Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a 2027 sixth-rounder.
Sources: The #Eagles aren't done, trading edge Arnold Ebiketie to the #Bengals in exchange for 2027 6th round pick. pic.twitter.com/8EYzDf6px6
It isn't surprising to see Ebiketie go, as he was on a one-year contract and didn't exactly accomplish much in his brief time in Philly. The Temple/Penn State product has come off the bench in all nine of his appearances so far, recording only 11 solo tackles without a sack. His 52.4 pass-rush grade on Pro Football Focus is also a career-worst mark, a sharp drop-off from the 73.4 he recorded last season.
Given that the Eagles likely wouldn't have brought him back in the offseason, a Day 3 pick is a solid return.
The biggest splash that the Eagles might make this year happened one day before the trade deadline. On Monday, Philly cut ties with star defensive tackle Jordan Davis , acquiring a 2027 first-rounder and a 2029 second-rounder as they shipped him off to Jacksonville.
Blockbuster: the Jaguars are trading a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis, sources tell ESPN. This is the Jaguars’ third trade for a defensive player today while the Eagles now are poised to have 10 picks in the… pic.twitter.com/NTGnLf2MoT
Sports Illustrated 's Ed Kracz broke down the trade after it was announced, giving it an A+ for the impressive return the Eagles managed to recoup. Davis will be missed, no doubt, but it can also be said that trading him was the right choice to keep the team competitive for as long as possible.

title: 3 Eagles Winners & 2 Losers After Trading Jordan Davis to the Jaguars
full_text:
It wouldn't be the NFL trade deadline without blockbuster deals. The Eagles entered the fold by trading defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jaguars on Monday, according to ESPN 's Adam Schefter. Philadelphia received a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick in return.
It's a move that would've shocked fans before the season began. Davis was inked to a three-year, $78 million extension in March, and the Eagles had Super Bowl hopes. Philadelphia sits at the bottom of the NFC East, though, with a 2-7 record through nine weeks. The time has arrived to retool for the future .
Trades are always a double-edged sword in the NFL. In this case, the Eagles lose a vital run defender and locker room mentor. They also gain valuable draft assets and open up chances for others to earn more playing time. Here's a deeper dive into the Philly winners and losers of the Davis deadline deal.
There was chatter that Moro Ojomo would be the Philadelphia defensive tackle dealt at the deadline . Instead, he moves forward as one member of a dynamic duo with Jalen Carter before entering free agency next offseason. The 2023 seventh-round pick has worked hard to climb the depth chart.
Ojomo has showcased a high ceiling as a pass-rusher and run-stopper. He has logged 62 tackles, six sacks, and 10 tackles for loss since the start of 2025 (26 games). Consistent play down the stretch could lead to an extension for the 25-year-old. He'll have every opportunity to prove he's worth one.
The hole left by Davis' departure cannot be filled by one player. Ojomo is going to see his snaps increase, as should second-year pro Ty Robinson. The Nebraska product has played sparingly in his first two NFL seasons, tallying 10 tackles and one pass breakup in 20 games (13% of the defensive snaps).
. @T_ROB99 is COOKING rn pic.twitter.com/67Zm5ElLAT
A preseason sack against the Patriots showcased what Robinson can bring to the table. Strong hands helped him shed an initial block and work around the edge. Increased snaps will only help Philly's coaching staff determine what level of contributor Robinson can be in 2027 and beyond.
Howie Roseman is capitalizing on his chances to retool Philly's roster . The Davis trade follows a Cam Jurgens trade that netted a 2028 second-rounder and an A.J. Brown trade that netted a 2028 first-rounder. In total, the Eagles now own 10 picks within the first two rounds of the next three NFL drafts.
#Eagles upcoming draft picks: 2027 (9): 1st round, 1st, 2d, 3d, 4th, 5th, 5th, 5th, 7th 2028 (9): 1st, 1st, 2d, 2d, 3d, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th 2029 (8): 1st, 2d, 2d, 3d, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th
The picks give Roseman some much-needed flexibility. He could package them to acquire a superstar or move up in the draft. He could hold onto them and add exciting prospects to the Eagles' aging core. In any scenario, the picks provide hope that a complete rebuild isn't necessary in Philly.
One weakness has now grown weaker. The Eagles allowed at least 100 rushing yards in each of their first eight games for the first time since 1968, before they stifled the Giants' ground game in Week 9. Philly enters its bye week ranked a disappointing 24th in rushing yards allowed per game (126.1).
Losing Davis will take a physical and mental toll on the Eagles' rush defense. His massive frame (6'6", 325 lbs) erased running lanes and caused opposing backs to second-guess themselves. It'll be up to players like Ojomo and Robinson to make their presence felt on the interior of the defensive line.
The loss of a monster defensive tackle is never going to be a good thing for a defensive coordinator. Vic Fangio will have to make adjustments. Whether or not those adjustments will work is a question no one can answer. It's worth pointing out that Fangio reportedly considered retiring last offseason.
The Eagles went as far as checking in with former Philly defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz , per The Philadelphia Inquirer 's Jeff McLane. Davis is someone who fits in Fangio's scheme, but he's not someone who fits in every NFL defensive scheme. The trade could be a sign of eventual change.

title: 3 Eagles Who Could Be Traded Next After Jordan Davis
full_text:
Each NFL trade deadline is often filled with offers that some general managers simply can't refuse , and that appeared to be the case for Eagles general manager Howie Roseman on Monday.
With the defensive tackle trade market heating up, the Eagles pulled the trigger by trading star DT Jordan Davis to the Jaguars, according to ESPN 's Adam Schefter . Philadelphia acquired a 2027 first-rounder and a 2029 second-round pick in the massive trade, making it clear that Roseman & Co. are thinking about the future.
Blockbuster: the Jaguars are trading a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis, sources tell ESPN. This is the Jaguars’ third trade for a defensive player today while the Eagles now are poised to have 10 picks in the… pic.twitter.com/NTGnLf2MoT
Davis's trade could signal the start of the Eagles moving away from more veteran pieces, especially those with expiring contracts and unguaranteed futures in Philly. With action likely picking up even more as we get closer to the 4 p.m. ET deadline on Tuesday, a few more current Eagles might become part of the team's past sooner rather than later.
That said, to quote former WCW World Heavyweight Champion Bill Goldberg, "Who's next?"
If any team is looking to add a dependable tight end to their offense, there's a good chance the Eagles will field some calls for Dallas Goedert. The ninth-year TE is a standard rental option ( expiring contract, affordable $7 million cap hit , per Spotrac ), and with Philly not looking competitive, it might be worth sending him to a contender.
After all, Goedert remains a solid contributor at this stage of his career. The 31-year-old playmaker has converted 31 catches into 308 receiving yards and two touchdowns this season, all while drawing a 100.1 passer rating when targeted. It might not be a career performance for him, but the fact that he's averaging his second-most yards per game (44.0) over the last four seasons is pretty impressive.
Throw in the fact that he has 13 postseason games (11 starts) and a Super Bowl ring under his belt, and it's easy to see why the Eagles should be open to shopping him around.
This week not only marks the trade deadline but also the Eagles' bye. It's a good time to think about moving on from certain players, and Tanner McKee might fit the bill after being benched for Joe Milton in Week 9.
Milton's performance against the rival Giants wasn't perfect , but a lot of his struggles come from the rough shape that the Eagles' offensive line is in. He also didn't have a ton of time to prepare between being named the start and the game itself, which Sports Illustrated 's John McMullen made as clear as day on Monday.
Now that the bye is here, the Eagles can work harder to put Milton in a spot where they can take advantage of his big arm and mobility. At the same time, that could open the door to trading McKee, who's on an expiring contract and might not be re-signed in March. If the Eagles don't see him as part of their long-term plans anymore, why not trade him for something (even if it's a seventh-round pick)?
No one would blame the Eagles for starting their offensive line over from scratch after how this season has progressed. The group has already been hit by Lane Johnson's retirement and Cam Jurgens's trade, and even Landon Dickerson's name has picked up buzz before the deadline . That's why it won't be a surprise if Tyler Steen is the next departure.
Drafted 66th overall in 2023, the Alabama product hasn't been the same player he was last year for the Eagles. His 67.4 overall and 63.5 run-block grades on Pro Football Focus have regressed from last year's effort (73.3 and 73.0, respectively), and he's already allowed two sacks on 559 offensive snaps after allowing the same number over 1,080 opportunities in 2025.
Like Goedert and McKee, Steen will be an unrestricted free agent in March. With teams like the Vikings, for example, looking to strengthen their offensive line's interior, it's likely worth the Eagles' effort to see if they can get a decent return for a veteran who's potentially declining and out of time in Philadelphia.

title: Instant Grade: Eagles Trading Jordan Davis to Jaguars
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Jordan Davis certainly didn’t talk like he was a man about to be traded when he was one of the last players to leave the locker room on Sunday after the Eagles’ seventh straight loss .
He talked about the defense having a great week of practice, how they were challenged by defensive coordinator Vic Fangio to stop the run, and his plans for the bye week.
Less than 24 hours later, the Eagles have traded the 13th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft to the Jacksonville Jaguars, per a report from ESPN ’s Adam Schefter. In exchange for the defensive tackle, the Eagles are getting quite a haul—the Jaguars’ first-round pick in the 2027 draft and a 2029 second-round pick.
pic.twitter.com/LoVwKERPqP
Asked for his perspective about the locker room potentially looking different when the team returns to work next week, Davis didn’t sound like he thought it would be him who wouldn’t be here.
“ I think it's something that we really don't think about,” he said. “Obviously, if somebody does come or leave, it does catch a lot of people by surprise. But for right now, we just all have been worried about playing the game, playing the game with integrity and just enjoying the moment.”
This is an A+ deal for the Eagles. Davis was popular among his teammates, but the draft capital was too steep for general manager Howie Roseman to say no to. It is similar to the trade in early October, when the GM traded center Cam Jurgens for a second-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round selection next year.
The Jags are loading up for a Super Bowl run.  Davis was the third defender acquired by the Jaguars, so the pick in next year’s first round could be the final one of the round if they win the Lombardi Trophy.
Still, as it stands right now, the Eagles have 10 picks in the first two rounds of the next three drafts:
On March 10, Davis signed a three-year contract extension with up to $78 million , with $65M  guaranteed. The deal was supposed to keep him in Philly through 2029. The Eagles will save $1.2 million on the salary cap, per overthecap.com. He exits town with nine career sacks and 15 QB hits.
Davis and Jalen Carter are close friends, so it will be interesting to see how Carter feels about the trade. It will also be interesting to see if the Eagles now turn their attention to signing Moro Ojomo .
It was reported that general manager Howie Roseman told trade suitors that Ojomo wasn’t available, that the Eagles wanted to re-sign him when his contract expires at the end of the year.
Davis was asked how he planned to spend his bye week.
“Rest, recover, keep working out, keep doing the things that help me become a better football player,” he said. “I think a lot of people, not just me, but a lot of people need rest on this team, and we can get their bodies back right and be grateful that bye week fell in the middle of the season.”
Now, Davis won’t get that rest. The 6-2 Jaguars play in Tennessee against the Titans on Sunday.

title: 3 Eagles Might Be Due for Bigger Roles After the Trade Deadline
full_text:
Trades are being announced across the NFL. It's only a matter of time before Philadelphia gets involved before Tuesday's deadline. The Eagles have lost seven straight games and sit at the bottom of the NFC East. They are lined up to be sellers, with several players available at the right price.
There's an obvious focus on who will no longer be wearing midnight green after Philly's bye week. It's important to put focus on who will be, too. Making a trade usually opens a spot for someone lower on the depth chart to take over. It's an intriguing development during a retooling campaign.
Here's a look at three Eagles who might be due for bigger roles following the NFL trade deadline.
General manager Howie Roseman shifted from the norm when he selected Eli Stowers in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft. The John Mackey Award winner was expected to make an immediate impact on Philadelphia's offense, but has been limited by injuries and blocked by Dallas Goedert.
Goedert could be moved at the deadline , considering he is 31 years old and playing on an expiring contract. That would give Stowers a chance to handle a steady role in an offense in need of change. It would also give the Eagles a window to evaluate whether the rookie can be trusted as a starter.
Second week in a row we are seeing Eli Stowers (No. 87) give this kind of effort blocking a CB Baby steps! pic.twitter.com/l5FhR3fGRI
Stowers logged 53 yards on three receptions in Week 8 (13 offensive snaps) and flashed solid blocking skills in Week 9 (seven offensive snaps). There's no time like the present to expand his route tree and depend on him to secure running lanes along the edge. Stowers is healthy and ready to roll .
There's no questioning defensive tackle Ty Robinson's potential. He has the strong frame (6'5", 288 lbs) needed to push back offensive linemen and an explosive first step that catches opponents off guard. The Eagles will never know whether that potential can turn into reality if he isn't on the field, though.
Robinson has served as the fifth option in the defensive tackle rotation since being drafted in 2025. That could change after Tuesday. The defensive tackle position is in high demand. The Eagles can capitalize by dealing Moro Ojomo or Byron Young, both of whom will be free agents next offseason .
Robinson was praised as a "wrecking ball" in college. The former Nebraska standout is violent at the line of scrimmage and always plays through the whistle. Robinson could be the spark Philly is missing in its disappointing run defense. The Eagles rank 24th in rushing yards allowed per game (126.1).
This selection is a bit more intricate than the other two. Outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt is already a reliable player on Philly's defense. However, his role has been reduced behind Jonathan Greenard and Nolan Smith lately. Hunt has played in fewer than 45% of the defensive snaps in each of his last four games.
Roseman could swing big by trading Smith at the deadline . He has posted five sacks in eight games and remains under contract in 2027. It'd be a move that brings back valuable draft capital for the Eagles. In that case, Hunt would become Greenard's counterpart, wreaking havoc in the backfield.
Hunt has tallied eight sacks, 12 tackles for a loss and 33 quarterback hits in 41 career games. The 25-year-old has shown versatility with six pass breakups and four forced fumbles. The final eight games of 2026 could go a long way toward determining whether Hunt is eventually signed to an extension.

title: McMullen: Joe Milton Isn’t to Blame After Eagles Set Him Up to Fail in Week 9
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — In the thick fog that settles over an organization after a seventh consecutive loss, the usual postgame noise quickly transformed into apathy in the shadow of the Eagles' 19-11 setback to the Giants on Sunday .
At 2-7, the Eagles are past the stage of searching for a spark and into the quieter territory of just trying to get through the remaining weeks of the 2026 season before rebooting in the offseason.
Into that haze walked Joe Milton, three weeks on the roster and making his first NFL start. He inadvertently said the quiet part out loud. ⁠
During a desperate final drive with seconds waning and no timeouts, Milton noted he trusted the embattled offensive line and loved the communication he was privy to despite the year-long issue with unaccounted-for pass rushers.
It was the kind of honesty only extemporaneous speech provides.
“I will learn y’all verbiage. I will,” Milton told his bodyguards. “That’s something that I put on myself to do for sure.”
Three weeks to absorb an offensive line’s language—the calls, the slides, the checks, the ‘who’s got the free runner’ signals—and the promise he would catch up.
That is not a quarterback complaining. That is a quarterback admitting the assignment was heavier than the preparation time allowed. ⁠
The play that made it obvious came from athletic rookie Arvell Reese, who came free on the right side, breezing by fellow freshman Markel Bell before nearly splitting Milton in two.
Milton never saw Reese, who separated the QB1 from his senses for a moment and the football.
Afterward, head coach Nick Sirianni did what he usually does when the film is going to be ugly . He said he was not going to assign fault.
Then he walked through the accountability coaching checklist: anytime a guy is free, look at the coaches first; ask whether everything possible was done to help the players; both coaching and execution matter; it starts with him; every product on the field is his responsibility. Yadda, yadda, yadda.
Sirianni’s monologue and Milton’s admission are not necessarily in conflict. They describe the same problem from different viewpoints.
Milton was signed off the Cowboys’ practice squad on Oct. 16. By the time he took the first snap against a Giants team that blitzes often and had the quickly ascending Reese, who finished with three sacks overall, Milton had a limited number of practices in the scheme under his belt.
The offensive line has been a problem all year for the Eagles. Protections have been a problem all year. Putting a new quarterback behind that line and asking him to diagnose, communicate, and correct in real time did not give Milton a chance.
It was testing whether the young signal caller could survive while still learning the language the line already speaks.
Sirianni is right that he owns the product. That ownership includes the decision to start Milton when the verbiage was still unfinished business. It includes the protection packages that left Reese with a free run. It includes the cumulative reality that seven sacks and a lost fumble on an unblocked blitz happened on the first start of a player who had just promised the line he would get their calls down.
Milton put the learning curve on himself, as professional quarterbacks do. The organization put him in the game before the curve was flat enough.
The Eagles did not hand Milton a functional offense and ask him to elevate it. They handed him a protection problem that has gone unsolved for weeks and told him the answer was on the field Sunday. He did what he could with what he had.
The result was what the setup predicted.

title: Riq Woolen Makes Trade Deadline Hopes Clear as His Eagles Future Remains Uncertain
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Riq Woolen doesn’t want to leave. The cornerback wants to see the season through with the Eagles, but that's out of his control.
Woolen has struggled in his first nine games with the Eagles, but he is still an attractive trade candidate for teams that believe they can challenge for the Super Bowl. Like, say, the Bears.
It’s up to general manager Howie Roseman to find a dance partner as the trade deadline arrives at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday.
“It sucks as a human when you don't know the unknown, but you wanna know the unknown, you know what I'm saying?” Woolen said after the Eagles lost for a seventh straight time, falling to the Giants on Sunday afternoon .
There are other players who could be ex-Eagles by the time the trade deadline comes, including Moro Ojomo, Dallas Goedert, and maybe Landon Dickerson.
Could there even be a blockbuster for Jalen Carter?
It’s hard to do one deal, let alone two. Soon enough, we will find out how many times Roseman hits the dance floor.
For his part, Woolen is trying to stay focused on playing football, leaving the heavy lifting to Roseman and his agent on what his immediate future could hold.
“I'm gonna just leave it to them, and whatever I have to do, I still gotta suit up and play football, and I still gotta be able to provide for my family,” he said.
Even if it means he could be traded to a contending team?
“I mean, if you woke up every day with your friends, some of your close friends, and y'all worked hard as hell every day, and you just up and disappear when stuff got hard or when you just up and disappear, then it'd seem kind of weird, especially when it's on you, you know?” Woolen said. “If it's up to Howie and the GM and my agent, then I'm gonna leave it to them. But me as a person, I've worked hard with these guys, and I'd love to be here and stay here with them.”

title: Eagles Stock Market: New QB, Same Old Story With Milton After Giants Loss
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA—Another Sunday produced another loss that feels heavier than the final score.
The Eagles fell 19-11 to the Giants at Lincoln Financial Field, their seventh consecutive setback, and now sit at 2-7 heading into their bye week. Three weeks into his Philadelphia tenure, Joe Milton got the first NFL start, Saquon Barkley punched in an early score against his old team, and for a few minutes it looked like the offense might finally find a pulse.
Instead the second half turned into the same familiar grind: short drives, pressure, and a crowd that started leaving to beat the Olivia Rodrigo concert traffic that was looming across the street.
Here's our weekly Eagles' stock market:
The Eagles generated pressure, finished with five sacks, and made J.J. McCarthy uncomfortable before knocking him out for a short period with a hip injury. It wasn’t consistent all afternoon, but it was the clearest sign that the defensive front can still disrupt when it gets a chance. On a day short on bright spots, that was one of the few that actually pushed the other side backward.
Milton’s mobility gave the offense a different look. He picked up 64 rushing yards and converted the two-point conversion himself, creating a brief 8-6 lead. It wasn’t enough to sustain anything, but the mobility created a couple of positive plays that Tanner McKee, a pure pocket passer, hasn't produced in recent weeks. It's a small sample, but it was the one offensive wrinkle that didn’t immediately get stuffed.
In the same game Eagles punter Braden Mann had an 86-yard effort, the longest by an NFL player since the Giants' Rodney Williams' 90-yarder on Sept. 10, 2001 vs. Denver, the veteran also had one for minus-2 after mishandling a high snap from Rocco Underwood, and another for only 17.
There were no declarative statements about job security as the Eagles enter their bye week. Head coach Nick Sirianni is likely safe for now but scapegoat season could be ready to start earlier than expected with offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, offensive line coach Chris Kuper and run game coordinator Ryan Mahaffey all in some kind of peril.
"We'll talk," Sirianni said when asked if staff changes are on the table. "Obviously, right now my job is to be there for our guys and to go watch the tape and go look through everything. I think we always think -- we'll do everything. I'll do anything I can to help this team win football games. Like I said, I'll look at myself internally first and then go from there.
"My job is to coach the players and to coach the coaches, and anything I can do to help this team win games, we'll do. Everything can always be on the table, but I don't think you change just to change because that's what your record says that -- you've got to look at what's really real and not react to anything else. Again, I just don't believe you just change just to change. If you have a strong reason to do things in anything, not just change, but in anything and you're convicted on it, that's how we'll go about our business."
Milton the passer faded quickly, finishing 18 of 34 for 169 yards, while being sacked seven times and losing a fumble. Once the Giants adjusted, the rocket arm never found a rhythm and the protection broke down. The early spark was extinguished and by the second half the stock was trading like every other recent Eagles quarterback outing.
"For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better [at] this week coming up for sure.”
The offense after the first quarter was the clearest underperformer. Three points the rest of the way, repeated three-and-outs, and no sustained drives once the Giants got a beat on the tortured offensive system.
"Obviously, none of us offensively have done a good enough job," Sirianni said when asked about the embattled Sean Mannion. "We're not going to sit here as coaches -- and it's not Sean, it's all of us and it starts with me. I think the correct question there to me is, 'Do you think you've done a good enough job?'
"Obviously, I haven't done a good enough job. We all have things that we've got to get better at and we've got to figure it out on offense. I mean, I think our defense is playing solid. I think they're doing really good things and it's hard to keep the game there. I think we've got some things that we're doing on special teams that have been really good, and then we can be more consistent in that particular case, but we have to figure it out on offense. That's coaches, that's players, that's everybody.
"So no, I haven't done a good enough job yet. The only way you grow in the midst of adversity is to get up, keep fighting, and work and stick together because you need everybody to do that. But adversity gives you opportunities for growth that steady times never would, but only if you do all those other things. We'll fight and we'll keep going."
Unaccounted for rushers remain a weekly staple and a drain on the Eagles' offense. Milton was under constant pressure, the pocket collapsed on multiple series, and the line never established a consistent ability to communicate.  The lack of protection turned what started as a manageable game into the same stalled effort that has defined the losing streak. Until the offensive line stabilizes, the rest of the offense will stay limited.

title: Kracz: Nick Sirianni Looks Out of Answers as Bye Week Brings Decision Point on Job Security
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – It’s quite possible the Eagles end the season with a 15-game losing streak, a 2-15 record, and a top-five draft pick.
It’s quite possible Nick Sirianni won’t be around to see the Eagles threaten the NFL record for consecutive losses. The 2008 Lions and 2017 Browns both went 0-16, so 16 is the record.
It’s quite possible that Sirianni has coached his last game. With all eyes on Tuesday’s trade deadline, there will be some rubbernecking this week with all eyes on Sirianni as the Eagles take their bye.
Jeffrey Lurie fired Chip Kelly with one game left in the 2015 season, but he allowed Ray Rhodes to stay until the end of a 3-13 season in 1998, he allowed Andy Reid to complete a 4-12 year in 2012, and Doug Pederson to finish a 4-11-1 year in 2020 before dropping the guillotine.
It stands to reason that Sirianni will be allowed to finish this year, no matter how it ends. He has made the playoffs in all five of his seasons and has taken the Eagles to two Super Bowls, helping the franchise win its second Lombardi Trophy just two years ago.
For some reason, he doesn’t get much credit for all that because the assumption is that he was handed a championship roster, which is the wrong assumption. What coach does that without talent, and how many coaches fail to do it with all that talent?
You could make the case that Sirianni should be allowed to return for the 2027 season because, really, what team can survive 12 games without its starting quarterback? To run it back in 2027 is probably asking too much at this point, because the coach doesn’t seem to have any answers on how to end this losing streak.
Maybe the decision to relieve him of his duties has already been made. The coach was late to his press conference after Sunday’s 19-11 loss to the New York Giants—another game in which the offense was terrible.
It took about 75 minutes after the game ended for him to get to the podium. Asked about his tardiness, he said he had players stopping by his office to talk. There is speculation that maybe they stopped in to say good-bye, knowing he won’t be back when the team reconvenes after taking this week off.
Here’s what the coach said about keeping reporters waiting to fire questions at him: “Everyone puts everything they have into this, so I want to make sure I talk to every guy first of all after the game.
“Then a couple of the guys stopped in the office just to talk through it. That's not unusual. I appreciate the connection that we have there. But yeah, it was a little bit later because of that. So, I appreciate you guys waiting around and waiting on that because I'm always going to be there for my players first and foremost.”
The locker room isn’t a fun place these days, obviously. The mood is somber, almost funeral—no music, no smiles, just beaten-down players trying to find answers.
If one thing is clear at this stage, it’s that Sirianni has no ideas how to turn the team’s fortunes around.
He continues to talk about details and how everything is on the table, but that change for the sake of change isn't necessarily the answer. Of course, he said that last week too about Tanner McKee, anointing him “our guy” one day, then 24 hours later, changing his mind.
So, who knows what to believe from him anymore?
“We all have things that we've got to get better at and we've got to figure it out on offense,” he said. “I mean, I think our defense is playing solid. I think they're doing really good things and it's hard to keep the game there. I think we've got some things that we're doing on special teams that have been really good, and then we can be more consistent in that particular case, but we have to figure it out on offense. That's coaches, that's players, that's everybody.”
Eagles on SI followed up by asking why the offense has been so difficult to figure out halfway through the season.
His answer: “It's a little bit of everything and it starts with me, and I have to do my best and get everybody playing with the level of detail and coaching with the level of detail that has become our standard here for the Philadelphia Eagles. I'll fight like hell to do that.”
Nine games in it seems he has lost the fight.

title: Steelers Trade Rumor Tracker: 2026 Deadline News & Updates
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline mere hours away at 4:00 p.m. EST, the clock is ticking for the Pittsburgh Steelers to swing any deals.
Sitting in a tie with the Cincinnati Bengals atop the AFC North at 6-2, with a matchup between the two sides on Sunday Night Football in order in Week 10, the Steelers have an incentive to go out and add to their roster.
Whether it's for a wide receiver , which has long felt like Pittsburgh's priority, or even for a cornerback, it's no sure thing that general manager Omar Khan will find a suitable deal out there.
Khan has made trades in three of his four trade deadlines as the Steelers' GM, with the most recent example coming last year when he sent a 2026 sixth-round pick to the New England Patriots for safety Kyle Dugger and a 2026 seventh-rounder.
While Pittsburgh is on a four-game win streak as it exits its Week 9 bye and gets ready to face the Bengals on the road in primetime, an upgrade somewhere across its roster could do wonders for the team as it looks to cement itself as a top contender in the AFC.
With that, let's take a look at the rumors surrounding the Steelers before the deadline arrives.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the Jacksonville Jaguars plan on holding onto wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. through today's trade deadline after acquiring Jessie Bates, Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux on November 9.
"The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources," Fowler wrote. "They have relayed that to interested teams.
"Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise."
The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources. They have relayed that to interested teams. Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise. pic.twitter.com/0QxdybXqaN
Thomas Jr. was one of the top receivers involved in trade rumors over recent weeks given his dwindling role in Jacksonville.
The 2024 first-round pick, who had 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie, had been floated as a potential fit for Pittsburgh as it looks to upgrade its receiver room and generate more explosive plays in the passing game.
For now, though, it seems as though the Steelers won't have the opportunity to acquire him ahead of the deadline.
During an appearance on "The Aftermath" on November 9, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler stated that Pittsburgh "doesn't want to give up a lot of draft capital" in order to acquire a receiver while naming Tennessee Titans veteran Calvin Ridley as a player who might "make sense in that regard."
The Steelers have 18 picks between the 2027 and 2028 NFL Drafts, though their lack of a fourth-rounder in the first of those two years could hurt their pursuit of some of the top receivers on the trade block, such as Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts.
The names who could entice Pittsburgh at a cheaper price include Ridley, Jauan Jennings (Minnesota Vikings) and Keenan Allen (Colts).
In addition to their pursuit of a wide receiver, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported on November 9 that the Steelers also want a cornerback.
My over/under on trades by tomorrow is 10.5, and I’m taking the over. Here’s everything I’ve heard on who’s buying and which positions they’re targeting after speaking with sources: pic.twitter.com/KbrHfUNVLo
Pittsburgh could use another option on the boundary alongside the likes of Jamel Dean, Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette after previously trading Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4.
Riq Woolen (Philadelphia Eagles), Donte Jackson (Los Angeles Chargers) and Mike Sainristil (Washington Commanders) are among the top names to watch if the Steelers do go out and bring in a corner.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Lose WR Trade Target After Jaguars Decision
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- One of the Pittsburgh Steelers' top trade targets entering the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline was former Jacksonville Jaguars first-round pick Brian Thomas Jr.
Once a 1,100-yard receiver for the Jaguars, he now finds himself sliding down the depth chart, which made him a high-upside target for the Steelers to pursue. But as the final hours before the deadline passed, the Steelers received a disheartening update regarding Thomas.
According to a report from ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the Jaguars have communicated to interested teams that they will not be moving on from Thomas. Fowler provided the latest via his X account.
"The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline," he wrote. "Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise."
The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources. They have relayed that to interested teams. Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise. pic.twitter.com/0QxdybXqaN
The Steelers and the Kansas City Chiefs were the two teams most frequently linked to Thomas Jr. But after this latest report from Fowler, no team should feel surprised.
The fact of the matter is that the Jaguars are one of the top teams in the AFC and the entire NFL right now. They have quarterbackTrevor Lawrence playing at the top of his game, and they just acquired multiple defensive upgrades: safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Jordan Davis.
When you are a top team contending for a Super Bowl, you don't sell off your talented players. Even if they are underperforming and sliding down the depth chart, the Jaguars have no reason or incentive to move on from a 24-year-old receiver with a history of producing.
If anything, the Jags should feel even more encouraged to get the old Thomas back as they push toward the postseason.
The Steelers can't waste time crying over this update, however. The organization needs to focus on the players who were always more realistic targets.
The top name continues to be Indianapolis Colts pass-catcher Josh Downs. In the final year of his rookie contract and wanting out of his current team, he's a quick receiver who can create separation against man-to-man coverage.
Another pair of names to keep on your radar are Philadelphia Eagles receivers Dontayvion Wicks and Hollywood Brown. Both are players who would bring talent and speed to Pittsburgh's receiver group, and they would cost far less to acquire than names like Downs or Thomas.
There are also multiple veteran names that fit the mold of Steelers previous acquisitions. Those players include the Indianapolis Colts' Keenan Allen, the Tennessee Titans' Calvin Ridley and Jauan Jennings of the Minnesota Vikings.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Every WR Steelers Can Potentially Land at Trade Deadline
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers might not do anything before the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline.
It's a sad, but possible reality for the Steelers. With names like Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson hopefully returning to the lineup soon, the Steelers might not feel compelled to add before the deadline expires.
Regardless, the franchise has been tied to nearly every available (and not so available) wide receiver in the NFL. With the deadline just hours away, here's a rundown of each wide receiver the Steelers have been interested in or linked to.
The two names that stand out as the most impactful ones to wind up in Pittsburgh are Indianapolis Colts' Josh Downs and Dontayvion Wicks of the Philadelphia Eagles.
Downs has been repeatedly linked to the Steelers, and he remains the name most are pining for.
Meanwhile, Wicks is a name that fills a ton of holes for the Steelers and is under contractual control for the 2027 season. Both names make sense as a deadline addition.
Many believe that Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jacksonville Jaguars is a perfect change of scenery candidate. I'm not one of those people, but the intrigue is undeniable surrounding the former first-round pick.
Another former first-round pick, Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Quentin Johnston, is also a name that could be on the move. He's a poor fit for what the Steelers need, but he's still on the trade block and it wouldn't be surprising to see him moved before the deadline passes.
One "Plan B" name to monitor as the minutes tick down is Hollywood Brown, another member of the Eagles. He's bene a productive receiver across multiple organizations, and now that he's healthy, he could provide that for a new team.
The Steelers wouldn't be the Steelers if they didn't look into a few uninspiring veteran names to add to the roster. Both Jauan Jennings and Keenan Allen are frequently tossed out names in trade rumors. The Steelers have been tied to both players in previous seasons, and here comes the carousel once again.
Recently, Tennessee Titans veteran Calvin Ridley popped up in trade rumors. A multiple-time 1,000-yard receiver, he's become an afterthought in the Tennessee offense. Combine that with his expensive contract and a recent incident off the field, and it's hard to see why the Steelers would pursue him to upgrade the offense.
The two best names on this list are also the most unrealistic. Both Ladd McConkey and DeVonta Smith provide what the Steelers are missing - a truly dependable top of the depth chart wideout.
It will cost a pretty penny to acquire either, and that's what will likely drive the Steelers away.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Should Call Eagles About Fire Sale Trades
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are working the phones, trying to land someone before the 4 p.m. ET trade deadline passes. Wide receiver and cornerback are the two positions to watch, and the Philadelphia Eagles may be the team to call for general manager Omar Khan.
The Eagles are sellers at the deadline. With 2026 essentially over, the team is moving some key pieces as they stack draft picks for 2027 and beyond. So far, they've traded Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars, but that may just be the beginning as the 4 p.m. cutoff approaches.
For the Steelers, there are three names they can ask about - cornerback Tariq Woolen and wide receivers Marquise Brown and Dontayvion Wicks.
Pittsburgh's top priority is wide receiver, and Wicks and Brown fill that need. They don't want to spend a lot of draft capital acquiring anyone, and neither of these players will be expensive. They do want a separator who can help stretch the field on the outside, which both players are.
And while both can impact a team when called upon, neither is required to be a starter once they join the roster. Something Pittsburgh is keen on, looking to add depth instead of a "game-changer" at the deadline.
Wicks has tallied 19 receptions for 284 yards and a touchdown this season and is signed through 2027 with a $4 million cap hit next year.
Brown, who battled an ankle injury earlier in the season, has only caught five passes for 63 yards. His contract ends at the end of 2026, making him more of a rental option.
Both would likely go for Day 3 draft picks.
As for Woolen, that's a bigger name who's still likely cheap. The 27-year-old has started all nine games for the Eagles and has eight passes defensed on the season. He's a player who would come to Pittsburgh with expectations of contributing in a larger role on defense, likely being the No. 3 behind Asante Samuel Jr. and Jamel Dean.
And that works. Daylen Everette has impressed during his rookie season, but the third-round pick still isn't a player the Steelers want on the field in larger chunks. What they'd prefer is another option behind their starters to add more veteran capability to their secondary.
If they're not looking to spend much but still want to add a bigger name, Wollen is the easy answer.
It's an easy call to make for Khan, who should be trying to take advantage of the Eagles' fire sale. If they want to stock up on draft picks, Wicks, Brown and Woolen are all easy options to move on from.
And they are perfect fits for what the Steelers are looking for at the trade deadline.

title: Steelers Have Another Opportunity to Prove They're Real
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers don't have any time to catch their breath following their Week 9 bye.
Not only do the Steelers have to tend to business ahead of the November 10 trade deadline , but they also are preparing for a Sunday Night Football showdown on the road against the Cincinnati Bengals.
The Bengals, much like Pittsburgh, have won four games in a row. The two teams are now tied atop the AFC North at 6-2 as a result, and this week's bout could very well end up dictating who takes the division crown by the end of the year.
While the Steelers came away with a 30-27 win over Cincinnati in Week 3, sweeping the season series will be much easier said than done considering they're heading into a hostile environment in primetime.
Just two years ago, Pittsburgh also made waves around the league with a 6-2 start before entering Week 15 with a 10-3 record after Russell Wilson won six of his first seven starts for the team upon returning midseason from a calf injury.
Then, the entire foundation crumbled. The Steelers finished the regular season on a four-game losing streak, squandering the AFC North in the process, and fell to the Baltimore Ravens in the Wild Card round of the playoffs.
Some parallels have been drawn between the 2024 team and this year's Pittsburgh squad, though that doesn't feel fair.
Not only do the Steelers have an entirely new coaching staff headed by Mike McCarthy, but their defense is playing at a truly elite level under defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, as evidenced by the fact that they have allowed the seventh-fewest yards (305.6) and fourth-fewest points (18.0) points per game in addition to being tied for the third-most sacks in the league with 26.
The passing game is still a bit spotty at times and struggles to generate explosive plays, though Aaron Rodgers is playing about as well as he has in several years, while the offensive line is quickly becoming one of the NFL's more impressive units.
Jaylen Warren has been nothing short of spectacular too, with 998 yards and three touchdowns from scrimmage in what could potentially develop into an All-Pro type of season for the 28-year-old.
All of that is to say that this is the most complete team Pittsburgh has put on the field in quite some time, though this week's matchup with the Bengals is arguably its toughest test yet.
The Bengals are one of the league's hottest teams alongside Pittsburgh, and it's just about impossible to shut down their passing attack led by Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Though the Steelers defeated Cincinnati in Week 3, Burrow still threw for 287 yards and three touchdowns.
The Bengals are averaging the second-most points per game (30.0) for a reason, and it all comes down to that aforementioned trio since they have what's essentially a nonexistent run game.
Cincinnati feels like a pretty solid matchup for the Steelers because of how well the latter's defense has performed, and Pittsburgh has only lost on the road to the Bengals three times since 2014, but coming away with a victory this week won't be easy.
If the Steelers do win, though, they'd be a game up on Cincinnati while owning a 3-1 record in the division and emerging as the favorites to win the AFC North for a second-straight season.
On the flip side, though, a Bengals victory could spell trouble for Pittsburgh since it would be a game back and move to 2-2 in the division.
These are the types of wins the Steelers need to pick up if they want to be considered legitimate contenders in the AFC. They've already proven they have what it takes to hand a loss to Cincinnati this year, and while repeating that outcome will take an all-around effort on the road, doing so would help prove that Pittsburgh is for real and here to stay this season.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Mike McCarthy Addresses Steelers Trade Deadline Urgency
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy isn't wasting too much of his time or energy worrying about the impending NFL trade deadline, nor has he ever really done so.
During his press conference as the Steelers return from their Week 9 bye and get set to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football in Week 10, McCarthy joked that he didn't even know when the trade deadline was for a large portion of his time as a head coach.
"I spent a decade in my life as a head coach, I didn't know when the hell the trade deadline was. I just knew it was somewhere around the middle of the season," McCarthy said.
McCarthy, who was originally asked if seeing other contending teams like the Jacksonville Jaguars be aggressive on the trade market could motivate Pittsburgh to make some moves, stated that his focus is on the players currently in the building and that he has confidence in the organization's brain trust to handle all of the deadline activity.
"I get it, everybody wants to improve their roster, and I have great confidence in [general manager] Omar [Khan] and [owner] Art [Rooney II] if there's something there, we'll do the right thing," McCarthy said. "But I think it's very important for me as the head coach to keep my eye on the target, and that's the 68-plus [players] that are in the building. So if we add someone that's gonna help us win, everybody would be for that... The most important thing is, I've always done this, I worry about the ones that are here. Coach the ones that are here and keep building what we got going. We have a lot of positive energy going right now, and we got a big-time game, Sunday Night Football in Cincinnati."
As has been the case for over a month at this point, all eyes are on the wide receiver market for the Steelers.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler stated that Pittsburgh "doesn't want to give up a lot of draft capital" for a receiver during an appearance on "The Aftermath" and mentioned Tennessee Titans veteran Calvin Ridley as a player who might "make sense in that regard."
The likes of Josh Downs (Indianapolis Colts) and Brian Thomas Jr. (Jacksonville Jaguars) have been connected to the Steelers over recent weeks, though if the organization really isn't comfortable paying up for players in that sort of tier, they might have to settle for someone like Ridley or Jauan Jennings (Minnesota Vikings) in exchange for a late Day 3 pick.
Cornerback is another position to watch for Pittsburgh, though it's been a bit quiet on that front over recent days, and the team's priority at the moment appears to be adding a receiver rather than supplementing their secondary.

title: Steelers vs. Eagles Game Moved to New Time
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles has been flexed.
Originally scheduled to kick off at 4:25 p.m. EST from Lincoln Financial Field, the NFL has now moved the start time of the contest up to 1:00 p.m. EST, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.
A matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and New York Giants at MetLife Stadium will move back to the 4:25 p.m. EST slot that the Steelers-Eagles contest has vacated.
Flex: A Week 11 schedule change with the Jaguars-Giants moving to 4:25 p.m. ET, and Steelers-Eagles to 1 p.m. ET.
What initially looked like one of the tougher games on Pittsburgh's schedule at the onset of the season has now lost a good amount of its luster, even if the Battle of Pennsylvania is still sure to draw some level of intrigue.
The Eagles are currently mired in a seven-game losing streak, which has seen their record plummet to 2-7, while starting quarterback Jalen Hurts is also out for the remainder of the year due to blood clots in his lungs and hasn't played since Week 5.
While the Steelers are always a draw in terms of ratings and fan interest, and the same could be said for Philadelphia, there just isn't as much stakes on the line for both sides as originally expected.
It's still a big game for Pittsburgh , though, who is currently 6-2 and riding a four-game win streak as it comes off of its Week 9 bye and gets ready to face the Cincinnati Bengals for a Sunday Night Football  showdown on the road this week before facing the Eagles in Week 11.
If the Steelers don't find a way to win in Philadelphia this season, it's probably just not meant to be as a whole.
While the two teams don't face one another often due to the fact that they play in separate conferences, Pittsburgh has still played a total of 41 road games against the Eagles.
Philadelphia has completely dominated those matchups, going 30-9-2 while outscoring the Steelers 820-528 over that span (per The Football Database ). The last time Pittsburgh won in Philadelphia was all the way back in 1965, and it is 0-4 at Lincoln Financial Field.
The Steelers have a fantastic opportunity to finally break that skid this time around, though. The Eagles' defense still has its moments, as evidenced by the fact that they recorded six sacks in a Week 9 loss to the Giants, though the offense has completely sputtered with both Tanner McKee and Joe Milton III at quarterback in place of Hurts.
In a tightly-contested race at the top of the AFC North with the Bengals, who are also 6-2, Pittsburgh really can't afford a loss to Philadelphia in what's shaping up as one of the easier games left on its schedule.
