title: Josh Downs Performance Should End Steelers Trade Thoughts
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are in hot pursuit of a wide receiver to upgrade their offense. The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline is rapidly approaching, leaving general manager Omar Khan a brief window to bring a true offensive weapon to Pittsburgh.
The receiver most frequently tied to the Steelers is Indianapolis Colts pass-catcher Josh Downs. The 25-year-old has had two productive seasons in the NFL and is in the final year of his rookie contract, making him a low-cost option with upside.
Times are tough in Indianapolis. The Colts have sold off two key players already (Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner) and could make several more moves before the deadline passes. Downs makes a ton of sense for the Steelers,
Sadly, he demonstrated in the Colts' latest game that he has talent and potential, but he's not the answer for the Steelers.
The positives Downs brings are evident. He's incredibly quick and can create separation, two traits the Steelers desperately need more of in their wide receiver room.
But one play erased any of the upside that he might bring. The Colts took on the Dallas Cowboys in their Week 9 matchup. Downs has struggled over recent weeks, posting less than 50 receiving yards in five consecutive contests heading into the game.
Week 9 changed nothing for Downs or his trade stock. If anything, it plummeted it. On a third down play in the second quarter, the Colts needed eight yards to gain a first down.
Downs ran a simple hitch route that put him just short of the line to gain. The route was a perfect one for the defensive coverage the Cowboys played on third down, and quarterback Daniel Jones delivered a slightly off-target ball.
It wasn't a perfect throw, but it was a very catchable ball for Downs that could have easily gotten the Colts another set of downs.
Instead, Downs couldn't haul in the pass and the Colts' offense fled the field. NFL insider Ari Meirov shared a clip of the play via his X account.
#Colts WR Josh Downs dropped a pass, and his brother, #Cowboys S Caleb Downs, was right there to trash-talk him. 😂 pic.twitter.com/tWir58SXdo
A dropped pass isn't the end of the world, right?
Ordinarily, that is exactly the case. I would downplay concerns about dropped passes, but in this scenario, it was a flashing warning sign
The Steelers need a boost to their offense, but not just any addition. The offense needs a receiver who can come through in the toughest moments. Creating separation is one thing, but that receiver also has to earn the trust of one of the best quarterbacks in the history of the NFL.
The Steelers want to go on a long playoff run as Aaron Rodgers says his goodbyes to the NFL. Having another talented receiver helps, but it won't matter much if Rodgers doesn't trust him on third down.
That's who the Steelers need to acquire. Sadly, it's not Josh Downs.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Calvin Ridley Incident Could Complicate Steelers Trade Interest
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have just over 24 hours before the 2026 NFL trade deadline passes them by. The organization has multiple needs they will hopefully address before the deadline expires, but none feel more pressing than adding a wide receiver.
Because of that obvious need, the Steelers have been tied to nearly every possible trade candidate on the market. Whether it's the top name discussed, Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs, or veteran Tennessee Titans pass-catcher Calvin Ridley, the Steelers have been connected to all of them.
Ridley has suddenly become a more coveted trade target in the final hours before the deadline, but a recent incident during his bye week might complicate things too much for Pittsburgh's liking.
According to a report from WKRN , a Nashville publication, Ridley was involved in an undisclosed incident at Nashville International Airport. The team released a statement confirming Ridley's involvement, but did not provide any further details.
"We are aware of the incident and are in communication with Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority,” the team said. “We will not be able to comment any further at this time."
The team's interest in Ridley may not have him as their top target, but this news should end any thoughts about the possibility. No details are known about what transpired at Nashville International Airport, and that's perfectly fine. It's no one's business what happened.
Regardless, the Steelers should take any warning and sign of caution as encouragement to abandon any possible trade talks with the Titans.
The biggest reason for this is because the player is already a questionable target. Ridley is in his third season with the Titans, and each year has been another step backward for the veteran. His first season in Tennessee was a fantastic season, putting up 1,017 receiving yards and hauling in four touchdowns. Last season, injuries derailed his campaign, limiting him to just seven games with 303 yards.
So far in 2026, he's been an afterthought. He's played in seven games but has received only 13 targets. That's translated into six receptions for 91 yards and zero touchdowns.
That's a combined 49 receptions and 394 yards over his last 14 games played. The average yards per reception is exciting, sure, but it disguises the reality. Ridley is no longer the effective route runner and separator that made him a multiple-time 1,000-yard receiver.
Add in any sort of off-the-field issues, whatever they may be, and it's a bit of salt in the wound. Ridley was already a trade target who provided little excitement to the Steelers, and this latest incident only complicated the matter further.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Ladd McConkey for Roman Wilson? Steelers Trade Idea is Interesting
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are expected to be buyers at the NFL trade deadline and wide receiver is the position to watch.
As for who they are going to land, if anyone, it's still up in the air. Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts, Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jacksonville Jaguars and Calvin Ridley of the Tennessee Titans have all been floated as leading candidates. But there has also been some discourse about bigger names who may not be available, but teams may be trying to test the waters with.
Ladd McConkey has been one of those bigger names, being mentioned as a player teams like the Steelers may be interested in calling about. All reports claim the Los Angeles Chargers do not have interest in dealing their leading wide receiver, but that hasn't stopped conversations about opposing teams acquiring him.
CBS Sports' Bryan DeArdo was amongst those discussing the possibility, pitching a trade idea that lands McConkey and the Chargers' 2027 fifth-round pick in the NFL Draft in exchange for the Steelers' 2027 second-round pick and wide receiver Roman Wilson.
"It's possible that the Steelers wouldn't have to part with Wilson in this scenario, but if the Chargers want a replacement for McConkey, it would likely be Wilson, who had success at Michigan with Jim Harbaugh," DeArdo writes.
"The Chargers also probably don't want to part with McConkey, a former 1,000-yard receiver who is still playing on his rookie contract. However, getting another receiver — in addition to a second-round pick — could be enough for the Chargers to move McConkey."
It might. Wilson also has another year left on his rookie contract, so Los Angeles would be receiving a wideout who would stick around for longer than the season. Wilson is also in the midst of his first season as a real contributor to the Steelers' offense, catching 14 passes for 188 yards and two touchdowns in five games.
While Wilson is currently on Injured Reserve with a finger injury, he's eligible to return after Week 10 and has begun working with trainers on the sideline during practice, which is a good sign that he's getting ready to at least return to practice once eligible.
The Chargers would be more interested in the second-round pick over Wilson, but it might be the sweetener they'd need to actually consider trading McConkey.
As for the Steelers' side of things, there's no reason this trade wouldn't work. They should be willing to give up a second-round pick for a player who might take them to the next level offensively. Plus, McConkey comes with another year of play, meaning Pittsburgh could try to negotiate a long-term deal in the offseason without having to worry about losing him.
If it works out, he and Germie Bernard are an exciting duo to help welcome a younger quarterback next season and beyond.
Chances are, the Steelers have a much higher likelihood of landing Downs, Thomas, Ridley or a small name at the deadline . McConkey would be a game-changing move, though. And to give up Wilson and a second to land him and a fifth-round pick? It might be worth it.

title: Week 10 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Why Seahawks Are Down Despite Win vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are back over .500 after a 17-3 victory against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9 inside Lumen Field.
Their 5-4 record keeps them in the hunt for a playoff spot, but there are certainly causes for concern. Here's a look at where the Seahawks stand in power rankings across the internet.
Ranking: 12 | Last week: 6
Conor Orr moved the Seahawks down six spots despite their win, which is more of a sign as to where the team stands with their quarterback situation than anything.
"It’s the Drew Lock show for Seattle once again," Orr wrote. "I think it’s time to revisit a Sam Darnold column we wrote at the beginning of the season. How soon before we have the conversation about Seattle’s QB situation?"
ESPN moved them back one more spot after going down three spaces last week, which shows that winning isn't everything when it comes to the power rankings.
The power rankings also highlight the team's Week 12 contest against the San Francisco 49ers, citing it as the most important game in the second half of the season.
Ranking: 11 | Last week: 9
Josh Kendall and Chad Graff worked together for The Athletic and says the Seahawks need to start stacking some wins as they go into the second half of the season.
"They’re still weathering the storm of Sam Darnold injuries (and now Drew Lock may have to play through an injury), but the defense remains a top-five group, and there’s hope for what the running game will become now that Jadarian Price is back. Still, they haven’t won consecutive games since the first two weeks of the season," The Athletic wrote.
Ranking: 12 | Last week: 13
Bleacher Report contributor Moe Moton highlighted the team's inconsistencies on offense as the reason why they aren't higher, even though they take one step forward in the website's power rankings.
"Entering Week 10, Darnold is nursing quad and rib injuries, and Lock has an oblique injury. With so much uncertainty at quarterback and the passing game's recent limitations and inefficiencies, it's hard to feel confident about the Seahawks' short-term outlook," Moton wrote.
Ranking: 14 | Last week: 14
Pete Prisco has Seattle at No. 14 for the second straight week, but he thinks things could turn around in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
"They are fighting through quarterback injuries, but it looks like Drew Lock will play against the Raiders this week. The Raiders might be the perfect tonic to get the offense going," Prisco wrote.
No matter how good the Seahawks' defense is performing, the team will always be looked at for their quarterback situation. As long as Darnold is underperforming, the Seahawks will not be viewed as a true Super Bowl contender in the NFC.
This year, there are several teams in the NFC that have improved from a year ago, and the Seahawks aren't one of them. That said, if they can stack some wins in the second half of the season and stay healthy after their bye week, they should be a team nobody wants to face come playoff time.

title: Mike Macdonald Discusses Seahawks Plan at Quarterback
full_text:
After a 2025 season where the Seattle Seahawks were almost entirely without quarterback drama, 2026 has been the exact opposite.
As of this moment, both Sam Darnold and Drew Lock are nursing multiple injuries. A couple days ago, there was even a moment where it looked like Jalen Milroe was in line to start. So, where do things currently stand?
It was fairly clear days ago that Darnold was unlikely to be healed up in time for the Las Vegas Raiders game. Lock suffered an oblique injury during the Arizona Cardinals game on top of his elbow problem, so his status was initially unknown. However, according to Lock himself and head coach Mike Macdonald, he should be available this week.
After that, the Seahawks have their bye week, giving them extra time to sort things out. And yesterday afternoon during his typical Monday press conference, Macdonald indicated he believed that Darnold would be ready to play on the other side of that bye. He stopped short of making any promises, but it sure sounds like the starting job is going back to Darnold.
Assuming that is the case, then I can certainly understand the decision. Macdonald isn’t going to be in a hurry to ditch the quarterback that helped him win a Super Bowl just nine months ago, and Darnold’s play against Kansas City reminded everyone that high-level play is still within his abilities. But does that make it the right decision?
I’m not so sure. We have a pretty decent sample size, going back to last season , of Darnold being a below average quarterback with occasional flashes of greatness here and there. For the most part this season, he’s been downright bad. Lock has played a much more complimentary style of football that I think serves this team better.
Beyond my own personal beliefs about who the better option is right now, however, there’s another layer. Lock has started two games, both against the Arizona Cardinals, and gets a third start this week against the Las Vegas Raiders. Very poor defenses, the kind that any competent quarterback can produce against.
If Darnold comes back after the bye, he jumps right into a matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, who have one of the NFL’s better defenses. It’s a circumstance that does feel like something of a setup that makes Lock look better. It also continues something of a pattern to this season so far, where Darnold gets saddled with the harder matchups.
If Lock does well this week and Darnold struggles in Week 12, well, the discourse is only going to get hotter. Darnold does get the Dallas Cowboys the following week, at least, but even if Darnold gets his starting job back I find it hard to believe he has an infinitely long leash. This controversy isn’t going anywhere anytime soon, is what I’m getting at here.

title: Seahawks NFL Trade Deadline Primer: What to Watch
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks and the other 31 NFL teams are going into a day like today with an objective.
Some want to make their rosters better for a playoff push. Others want to swap good players that don’t fit into their timeline for draft capital and cap savings. Not every team will be able to achieve their goals today, but the ones that do may determine who wins it all, so let’s run it down.
Officially, the NFL Trade Deadline is today at 1 p.m. PT. Any deals that teams want to make need to be completed by then. That being said, remember that it takes time for a trade to go from the NFL office to beat reporters, so a trade could still be revealed some time in the following hour or so. Often, trades are leaked before they’re finalized, so even this is unlikely.
Once the deadline passes, the only way for NFL teams to improve themselves is to sign players out of free agency, and even that has some restrictions. Today serves as a last call for any team that believes themselves to be ready for a title run but needs one last piece. The Seahawks have been very involved in the deadline each of the last three years.
Typically, trade deals are initially broken on X by the Adam Schefter’s, Ian Rapoport’s, and Tom Pelissero’s of the world. They put it out there, and it propagates out to ESPN and NFL Network. This page will cover any trades the Seahawks specifically are involved in, of course. One way or another, whatever happens will spread through the general public quickly.
Also expect to see plenty of buzz and implication as the minutes tick down towards the deadline, as teams often work towards trade deals that never get completed. Often, deadline day comes with at least a couple of stories about how Team X was very close to acquiring Player Y from Team Z, but just couldn’t quite get the compensation right.
There were a fair few trades yesterday, including three from the Jacksonville Jaguars, so there’s a chance that some of the fireworks have already launched. But the general sense is that there’s going to be a lot of action today, as there are many teams that need to take that one extra step towards true contention and others that need to strip down a bit more.
The Seahawks, specifically, are believed to be on the hunt for a wide receiver , so we’ve got that. There’s no guarantee they find one, of course, but I’d be very surprised if they weren’t also sniffing around for an edge rusher. They have draft picks to give up to be sure, but note they already expended some capital for Quenton Nelson, so the big move has been made.

title: Seahawks Week 9 Snap Counts: Charbonnet, Price Flip Roles
full_text:
Despite missing several key players, the Seattle Seahawks pulled out a home victory over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Seattle has now won 11 straight games against the Cardinals, dating back to 2022.
The absence of some starters let more players see the field, which is a good thing when the team can avoid a loss. That was apparent in the Seahawks’ total snaps on both offense and defense this week, with multiple backups getting their most extensive action of the season.
Here’s a look at how the Seahawks’ snap counts shook out in their win over the Cardinals.
* All snap count statistics are courtesy of Pro Football Reference
RG Anthony Bradford (67; 100%), LG Grey Zabel (67; 100%), C Jalen Sundell (67; 100%), RT Abe Lucas (67; 100%), LT Josh Jones (67; 100%), QB Drew Lock (67; 100%), WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (51; 76%), WR Cooper Kupp (49; 73%), TE AJ Barner (48; 72%), WR Tory Horton (41; 61%), RB Zach Charbonnet (38; 57%), TE Eric Saubert (32; 48%), TE Nick Kallerup (27; 40%), RB Jadarian Price (24; 36%), FB Brady Russell (12; 18%), WR Montorie Foster Jr. (5; 7%), T Bobby Hart (3; 4%), Olu Oluwatimi (3; 4%), RB George Holani (2; 3%)
The running back split between Charbonnet and Price flipped against the Cardinals, as the former saw more snaps in his second game back from a torn ACL. Charbonnet carried or caught the ball on 44.7% of his snaps, while Price’s usage rate was about 54.2% when he was on the field. This is unsurprising, as Charbonnet is a better pass protector and was always going to retake the lead running back role.
Barner, Saubert and Kallerup all saw significant snaps, as the Seahawks ran heavy sets much of the game. That could continue now that the running back room is healthy and offensive coordinator Brian Fleury tries to establish Seattle’s run game.
The Seahawks’ offensive line, which featured backups Bradford and Jones, all played every snap. That will look much different once Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross return, as Zabel will go back to the left side of the line.
LB/DB Nick Emmanwori (53; 100%), S Julian Love (53; 100%), LB Ernest Jones IV (53; 100%), S Ty Okada (53; 100%), CB Devon Witherspoon (52; 98%), CB Josh Jobe (52; 98%), LB Drake Thomas (42; 79%), DL Byron Murphy II (40; 75%), OLB DeMarcus Lawrence (39; 74%), DL Jarran Reed (32; 60%), DL Rylie Mills (31; 58%), OLB Derick Hall (29; 55%), DL Mike Morris (17; 32%), CB Nehemiah Pritchett (12; 23%), OLB Dante Fowler Jr. (12; 23%), OLB Connor O’Toole (11; 21%), LB Patrick O’Connell (1; 2%), S Rodney Thomas II (1; 2%)
Emmanwori has been trending toward being an every-down player for multiple weeks, and he played that role against the Cardinals. Love, Jones and Okada have routinely played every snap when healthy, and that continued in Week 9. Emmanwori playing more drove down the amount of snaps that Drake Thomas played in this one.
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald dug deep in his front-seven depth, playing nine different defensive linemen and edge rushers. That was to make up for the absence of Uchenna Nwosu, Leonard Williams and Brandon Pili.
Pritchett continues to get some opportunity, but his usage has fluctuated from game to game. He still remains the No. 3 cornerback behind Witherspoon and Jobe.

title: Seahawks in the Market for a Wide Receiver Trade, per Sources
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are not waving the white flag on the 2026 season, despite some clear setbacks. Per Jordan Schultz, John Schneider is on the prowl for a wide receiver, specifically to complement Jaxon Smith-Njigba . Let’s take a look at the circumstances the Seahawks face as they try to find such a trade, and then look at some candidates to acquire.
First, the report from Schultz specifically said they wanted someone to complement JSN, which presumably means they want someone with a different skillset. I’d focus on bigger receivers who can win 50/50 balls and make catches in the redzone. That removes players like Josh Downs, who is a nice enough player, but would be the smallest WR on this team.
Remember that the Seahawks have very little cap space, around $3-4 million, so unless they pull some other levers they can’t really trade for a veteran on a bigger contract. That would make Rashod Bateman a tough sell. Also, since Cooper Kupp is probably in his final season , the team should prioritize getting a younger, long-term player here anyway.
Let’s start with the 2-7 Jets. The big name right now is Garrett Wilson, but he would be extremely expensive and I don’t think we’d get the most out of him. I’d rather cast my gaze at Adonai Mitchell, a decently-sized receiver with a lot of talent who is still on his rookie deal and under contract through 2027. There are some problems, but he’s flashed plenty.
Quentin Johnston, if the Los Angeles Chargers ever want to join the party, would be fascinating to me. Despite his bad reputation, he had back-to-back 700 yard seasons recently, is still on his rookie deal, and has the size to contrast JSN. It would be a very fun reclamation project for someone that is very talented, and is a free agent in a few months if things don’t work out.
Finally, and this one is a sleeper, I’d take a look at DeVaughn Vele with the New Orleans Saints. The Saints are still in the thick of the division race, but they’re still a bad team, and they barely use Vele. It should be cheap, and Vele is one of the biggest receivers in football at 6’5. His rookie year in Denver was pretty solid, so there’s something here.
All this being said, I’m not convinced trading for a wide receiver is the right move unless Rashid Shaheed’s injury is long-term . You could argue making a trade for anyone is a questionable idea, with the team sitting at 5-4 and staring at a very challenging wide card race, but a receiver in particular gives me pause. In an offense like this, how much can a receiver help?
This Seahawks team, in theory, is a run-first team. When they throw it, they throw it to JSN constantly. That leaves very limited opportunities for other receivers. To my eyes, players like Shaheed and Tory Horton are getting open at a good rate, and not getting the ball. Any receiver you trade for could easily end up doing the same. But, if you insist, those are my targets.

title: Why the Seahawks Could Trade for Jets' Edge Will McDonald IV
full_text:
It won't be long until the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline passes with teams making big statements. The Seattle Seahawks (5-4) already made a big move to improve their roster by trading for eight-time guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts to dramatically help the running game. After an early move to help improve the offense, the Seahawks could look to improve the defense.
​ There aren’t many reliable defensive options available , but more players are demanding. One player who might be available within the Seahawks’ reach is former first-round pick and edge rusher Will McDonald IV, who might be a risky, but potentially underrated deal.
McDonald has requested a trade from the Jets after he insisted he isn’t playing much with the Jets. ESPN insider Ian Rapoport said the former first-rounder wants more opportunities . The Seahawks can give him opportunities to see the field, considering they are experiencing some injuries and a need for some explosiveness off the edge.
​McDonald has been seeing less than 50% of the defensive snaps played in six of the nine games played this season. In the nine games played sparingly, he has accumulated 16 total tackles, seven quarterback hits and three sacks. In the last two seasons as a starter, he has accumulated 58 total tackles, 21 tackles for loss, 18.5 sacks and 43.5 quarterback hits.
​The Seahawks would be upgrading a pass rush unit that isn’t getting much of its edge rusher group consistently. Their four sacks are defensive tackle Byron Murphy II, linebacker Ernest Jones IV sent through blitz, an injured defensive tackle Leonard and edge rusher Derick Hall. Veteran edge rushers DeMarcus Lawrence, Dante Fowler Jr. and Uchenna Nwosu (who is also injured) have combined for three sacks.
​The Seahawks’ biggest draft needs in the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft should be edge rushers . Nwosu and Fowler are in the final year of their deals with the Seahawks and Lawrence has stated he is retiring at the end of the season. That only leaves Hall, who was extended before this season.
​If the Seahawks trade for a young, former first-round pick, they get an eager pass rusher who looks to make an impact as much as possible. The Seahawks would likely get McDonald on a cheap trade deal that is likely a day-three pick. That would shift the immediate draft focus to other positions on the team like wide receiver, center/guard or quarterback, if necessary.
​The biggest downside is trading for McDonald’s contract, which includes a $14.48 million team-option hit in 2027 that the Jets already exercised . If the Seahawks trade for McDonald, he would have to be a key focus moving forward. There is a lot of risk with his potential and the salary cap hit in 2027, but trading for a talented player and then using the early picks for other positions has great benefits.

title: The Seahawks Dark Side Defense Has Destroyed The Cardinals Yet Again
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks limited the Arizona Cardinals to under 200 yards of offense. They averaged 3.9 yards per play and 4.5 yards per pass.
And somehow, you can actually make an argument that they have something to celebrate, because all of that was a significant improvement over what happened back in Week 2 . The only thing that was missing was points.
Let’s understand exactly how remarkable an accomplishment this is for the Seahawks. Arizona ran a total of 98 offensive plays across the two games this season. Their season totals stand at: 10 points, 349 yards (229 passing and 120 rushing), 23 first downs, and 7/25 conversions on third down. Not only is that single-game production, it’s bad single-game production.
Remember also that the Seahawks did not have Ty Okada or (basically) Nick Emmanwori in the first game, or Leonard Williams and Uchenna Nwosu in this second bout. The Cardinals’ offense went through radical changes across the two games, with pieces swapped out at almost every position. Neither iteration was able to do anything.
The Cardinals are not a good team. But their offense has generally done a good job moving the ball and throwing some points up on the board. Their season low outside of the Seattle games in yards is 270 against the New York Giants, and they’ve gone over 327 in every other game. They’ve also scored at least 16 points in their non-Seahawk games.
It’s a team that you might beat, but it’s not a team you turn the lights out on offensively. Overall, it seems like Mike LaFleur has done fairly well in imparting his wisdom and making improvements into his offense during his first season. So this achievement is no small thing, and it should be taken as a testament to how great this defense is right now .
Football is a game of matchups. Certain players do well against other certain players for some hard-to-define reasons, and some systems and schemes work great against others. So when you’re looking at a Cardinals-Seahawks game, you’re also looking at the early pattern of how Mike LaFleur and Mike Macdonald match up against each other.
How that matchup squares up will go a long way in determining how the next several years of this rivalry will go. And if these two games are indicative of what we can expect between those two, then that’s a big advantage towards the Seahawks. Macdonald didn’t just win this round. He scored an early knockout.

title: Seahawks Were on the Right Side of Two of NFL's Worst Deadline Trades
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks general manager John Schneider is one of the longest-tenured GMs in the league. He's been in charge in Seattle since 2010 and has led them to plenty of success throughout his career, including building two championship teams.
Part of what makes Schneider so good is his ability to pull of big trades that benefit his team . He's hopeful that his recent move for guard Quenton Nelson could be the missing piece on their offense. If so, it could go down as a major win for the Seahawks, but it won't necessarily be his greatest pre-deadline deals.
That's because Schneider has fleeced teams in the past. That includes being on the right side of two trades that Bleacher Report's Brent Sobleski named among the 10 worst deadline moves over the past decade .
After being unable to come to terms with Duane Brown on an extension, the Houston Texans sent Brown, along with a 2018 fifth-round pick, to Seattle inexchange for a 2018 third-round pick and a 2019 second-round pick. As Sobleski says, the Texans thought they were getting excellent value for a player set to decline, but instead, they gave Seattle a stud who made two Pro Bowls in four seasons.
"The Houston Texans thought they were getting a premium return for a declining veteran. They were wrong," Sobleski wrote. "Duane Brown was 32 years old when the Texans shipped him to the Seattle Seahawks. Brown would go on to play seven more seasons, including four and a half in Seattle."
Following his stint in Seattle, Brown signed a two-year deal with the New York Jets. He retired following the 2023 season, playing until he was 38.
Brown isn't the only veteran who was sent to Seattle only to surpass expectations. Schneider landed Leonard Williams during the 2023 season in exchange for a 2024 second-round pick and a fifth-rounder in 2025. Considering he was on an expiring contract, plus the fact that the Giants were rebuilding, it made sense to move Williams. That said, the return wasn't enough, according to Sobleski, considering what Williams has done in Seattle.
"In retrospect, the Giants didn't get enough in return for Williams, who has been dominant with the Seahawks. Granted, landing second- and fifth-round picks for an expiring contract is usually viewed as an excellent return. In this case, it wasn't.Williams has since been named to two Pro Bowls and a second-team All-Pro. He won a Super Bowl in 2025 as Seattle's best defensive player," Sobleski wrote.
Williams admitted that he was considering ending his career, but fell in love with the game again in Seattle. The culture, and of course, the winning has him focused like never before and he's been one of the more prominent leaders of the Dark Side Defense.

title: Seahawks Get Drew Lock Injury Update After Cardinals Game
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock is recovering from an oblique injury that he suffered in Week 9 against the Arizona Cardinals.
There was a question mark surrounding whether Lock's injury was serious or not. However, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed on Seattle Sports 710 AM that Lock's injury isn't considered serious and that he could still start in Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald told @BrockHuard and @TheMikeSalk on Seattle Sports 710 ESPN that he is ruling out Sam Darnold for this week’s game vs the Raiders. But tests on Drew Lock’s oblique injury were “good”, and they believe he can start vs. the Raiders. pic.twitter.com/mba3rSJrZt
Getting Lock back for Week 10 is important, especially because Sam Darnold's status is also up in the air as he is dealing with quad and rib injuries. During Lock's start against the Cardinals in Week 9, he completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown.
Bucks are 2-0 at the start of this season, and the team really appreciates what he is able to do in a backup role when he is called upon in case of an injury.
"He's a beast. He just threw it around. Just went after it," Macdonald said via the team's website .
"I think our medical people deserve a shout-out too for putting a great plan together and treating Drew, and Jalen Milroe too, operating our offense when he took the snaps that he took and being ready to play in case Drew couldn't go or couldn't finish. Really a great team effort, but Drew, I don't know how you can get any tougher. Both guys, just tough as nails."
The Seahawks will monitor Lock's entry throughout the week, but if he is unable to go, they will try to see if Darnold can make a return. There is reason to believe, however, that Darnold will miss this upcoming game as well.
The Seahawks' bye is in Week 11, so giving Darnold extended rest to fully heal from his quad and rib injuries is important. This means the team will likely look to Milroe to make his first career start. The 2025 third-round pick has been planted behind Darnold and Lock on the depth chart, but the team may have to turn to him if both Darnold and Lock are injured.
The kickoff between the Seahawks and Raiders is scheduled for Sunday at 1:05 pm PT inside Allegiant Stadium in Sin City. Fans can watch the game on CBS or stream it on the Paramount Plus app.

title: 3 Reasons Why Seahawks Should Trade Sam Darnold
full_text:
Hear me out on this one. I know it’s a little nutty, and if there’s one thing this world doesn’t need more of, it’s nutty NFL trade propositions.
But after the Seattle Seahawks' Week 9 game against the Arizona Cardinals , where an injured Drew Lock was able to play the sound, fundamental, functional game that Sam Darnold hasn’t been able to recently, I just feel like we’ve got to play with it for a few minutes.
Maybe this is a little harsh. But I think it’s accurate. The Seahawks have eight games plus the postseason remaining, and Darnold is currently sidelined with multiple injuries . His play to this point has been bad, and if/when Darnold returns he will still be working with the flailing Brian Fleury as offensive coordinator. So righting the ship this season is highly unlikely.
So then you’re in the offseason. Darnold will be on the last year of his deal, which has a cap hit of $41.9 million. Extending him, even with his poor play, will put a heavy weight on the cap for the foreseeable future. As Baker Mayfield can attest , you often get paid based on your best work, not your most recent work, as an NFL quarterback.
And John Schneider has already shown that he’s very hesitant to give out the quarterback mega-deal, so the odds of him playing along are low. So, with all apologies to Sam, who will always be remembered fondly in this fanbase, it’s very difficult for me to imagine any other way for this to go. One way or another, he’s not around next season.
The Vikings, who play a big game tonight, are one piece away from a clear super bowl contender. Unfortunately, that one piece is a quarterback. It’s a team that is swimming with talented players and brilliant coaches, but is stuck choosing between Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz to line up and take snaps every week. They have to do better.
Normally, they couldn’t do better. Acquiring a new quarterback midseason is almost impossible. On top of finding one available for trade, there’s the issue of learning a new offense with new teammates after the trade. It takes months to really fit into an NFL offense, especially as a quarterback. But guess who already knows the Minnesota offense?
I don’t mean that in a general sense. Darnold was literally the starting quarterback for the Vikings two years ago, under Kevin O’Connell and many of the still-present assistant coaches. He even knows quite a few of his potential teammates. This might just be the one exact circumstance where a quarterback could slot right in on a new team.
During that 2024 season, O’Connell was able to get a full season of quality play out of Darnold, with the meltdown hitting at the very end. Despite the evidence that Darnold isn’t a great quarterback , it’s entirely possible that he could look like one in the Minnesota offense. And that’s a lot more than you can say for Murray or Wentz so far this season.
It all comes together, doesn’t it? Assuming that the Vikings don’t get good quarterback play tonight, and are staring down the possibility of wasting this remarkable team, you call them up for a trade. Maybe you can get Minnesota’s second round pick? Could you get their first if you offered to send back a third? It should be a seller’s market here.
I will offer up the one obvious counter, which is that the Seahawks shouldn’t be helping an NFC rival get better when they themselves are still in the fight. That has to be weighed here. It’s just hard for me to worry about that when I envision in my mind what Brian Fleury’s offense would look like against Brian Flores, regardless of who their quarterback is that day.
If we end up getting bounced from the playoffs by Darnold in a Vikings uniform, people will certainly have their laughs. I just don’t think that possibility is enough of a deterrent when compared to the definite value of extra draft capital you could get. And if it helps the Vikings beat the 49ers or Rams in January…well, that’s something too, isn’t it?

title: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey Sets Historic TD Record vs. Raiders
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers can confidently say they've got the very best out of running back Christian McCaffrey.
McCaffrey has played in San Francisco for four years now and has been extremely influential. His individual honors of winning Offensive Player of the Year and Comeback Player of the Year in 2023 and 2025, respectively, are both campaigns that should go down as some of the best for a running back.
Yet, in 2026, as McCaffrey enters his 30s, an age when running backs typically begin to experience a decline in performance, he continues to produce at an exceptionally high level. Against the Las Vegas Raiders, he made history by setting a record unlike anything seen before.
That achievement saw McCaffrey record his 37th career receiving touchdown, the most by any running back in the Super Bowl era. In doing so, he surpassed the legendary Marshall Faulk to claim the top spot on the all-time list.
It may have been just a 12-yard touchdown, but that isn't the point. The significance was that McCaffrey surpassed another of Faulk's records while also reminding San Francisco of the value he can offer as a receiving threat.
With the 49ers short on options at wide receiver, McCaffrey's ability to make an impact through the air should arguably be utilized even more so right now. The touchdown marked his 19th receiving score in a 49ers uniform and his ninth game for the franchise in which he recorded both a rushing and a receiving touchdown in the same game.
San Francisco has done a solid job of reducing McCaffrey's workload as a runner, and it's an easy cheat code for him to wrap up touchdowns from close range, which seems to be doing the job.
He has almost matched last season's touchdown tally; in fact, he's one away, and averaging 4.5 yards per carry is an improvement from last year. That's hardly surprising because he was used way too much .
His may well be starting to decline in his production, but he's still delivering. And that's the great thing about McCaffrey.
The days of 2022 and 2023 are behind him, but the 49ers are being smart with his usage, which means he's still setting truly historic records.
His usage as both a receiver and a runner makes him such an impressive player, and the 49ers trading for him only adds to the remarkable nature of what McCaffrey brings to the team. He just needs to keep producing and, barring any significant drop-off, there is every chance more records will be set, some of which could prove incredibly difficult to beat.

title: Why 49ers LB Fred Warner Deserves to Win Defensive Player of the Year
full_text:
It's only eight games into the season, but conversations surrounding San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Warner and his potential candidacy for Defensive Player of the Year need to start.
It's fair to say that his season-ending injury in Week 6 of 2025 left him hungry to get back on the field and prove himself again. He wasted no time at all as he became the franchise's all-time leading tackler , surpassing Patrick Willis in Week 1.
In fact, just look at the level he's performing at in 2026. So far, it's been all business from Warner : 77 total tackles, 36 solo tackles, 41 assisted tackles, half a sack, five forced fumbles, one fumble recovery and three passes defended. He has also registered 5.5 stuffs and nine stuff yards.
Those stats at the halfway point of the regular season are extremely impressive. He's producing these numbers without carrying an excessive workload, ranking 19th among linebackers in total snap counts. He's the best linebacker in the league for a reason.
Warner's first half of the season serves as a reminder of just how much the 49ers missed when he was sidelined last year. It also makes their run to the playoffs last season even more impressive, considering what they managed without such an influential defensive presence.
This year, his return has highlighted just how important he is to the team, with his leadership and production helping San Francisco to a 7-1 record. Injuries across the defence remain prevalent, but it can be argued that Warner's availability makes him the most important piece of the entire unit.
These are all the reasons to be in the conversations for the Defensive Player of the Year conversations.  An incredible stat line is one contribution, but he alone raises the standard for everyone, too.
There's plenty more football to be played before the DPOY candidates become more obvious, but favourable fixtures ahead and San Francisco's current standing in the NFC suggest the playoffs are on the horizon. One game at a time, though.
Warner has done more than enough to put his name into the DPOY conversation, but the challenge now is to maintain that momentum. There is still room for further improvement, and the opportunity to build on his already impressive numbers is there for the taking.
Given his mentality, attitude and importance to the 49ers, Warner will approach every game with the same mindset: doing everything he can to help his team prevail.

title: Kyle Shanahan Reveals Plans for 49ers' Starting Three Safeties
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers had a tough decision to make at safety coming out of the bye. They had three players with starting capability and two starting spots to fill. Instead of making a firm decision, the 49ers decided to rotate Malik Mustapha, Marques Sigle, and Ji’Ayir Brown in their Week 9 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
Head coach Kyle Shanahan admitted that right now he does not have a strong end goal or hope for how things will turn out in the room.
“I don't think we know what the end goal is,” said Shanahan in a conference call on Monday. “We got three good guys that are playing at a very high level. So, you just play that till it plays itself out.”
The 49ers started the season with Ji’Ayir Brown starting next to Marques Sigle. However, as Shanahan noted, that was mostly because third-year starter Malik Mustapha was hurt in the summer leading into the season.
Sigle was playing too well to bench. When Sigle got hurt, Mustapha came back. Now, he is playing too well to bench, according to Shanahan.
“Just like Malik hurt his playing time just because of injuries in training camp,” admitted Shanahan. “Then kind of the same thing happened to Sigle, who was also playing at a real high level before he was hurt. And Tig's been the one who stayed consistent and healthy. So all three of those guys have been going.”
So, according to Shanahan, the team does not plan to bench any of them as of now. They will rotate the group. So, Mustapha plays with Brown, Brown plays with Sigle, and Sigle plays with Mustapha. Shanahan said that if they separate themselves, that is great, but he does not need to see that.
“I think it's been if two separate themselves way over another, then obviously we would keep those guys out there longer,” added Shanahan.  “But we'll just keep doing it week to week, and we'll see what it ends up. But it's a pretty good problem to have.”
Shanahan appears to have no intention of making a firm decision anytime soon. Mustapha led the way with 41 snaps in Week 9. Brown had 31 and Sigle had 22. We will see if they change the rotation in Week 10 when the 49ers take on the Dallas Cowboys.

title: The NFL Just Reinstated Brandon Aiyuk and the 49ers Should Keep Him
full_text:
The Brandon Aiyuk Saga keeps getting more interesting.
Now, the NFL has reinstated him merely one day before the trade deadline, which means he almost certainly will play this season, assuming he still can play at an NFL level.  We haven't seen him on a field in two years.
In addition, the 49ers have given the 49ers a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk, which means he can be an extra player on their team. But if he's on their roster at 1:00 pacific on Tuesday, then the 49ers will owe him a game check for the week, according to Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio.
I sincerely doubt that the 49ers intend to give Aiyuk any more money just before they trade or release him, considering they've already given him millions just to walk away from the team for a year. Why would they give him a parting gift when they hate him?
I'm guessing the 49ers would like to trade Aiyuk, and they have until tomorrow to do so. And considering his guarantees have been voided, his base salary is $1.2 million this season, and half the year is already over, he is extremely tradeable. A team could send the 49ers a seventh-round pick, pay Aiyuk roughly $500,000 for the rest of the season, and then release him after the season, or keep him if they like him.
It's possible that Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, already has found a team that's willing to trade for Aiyuk, and a tentative deal between that team and the 49ers is in place. That team could be the Kansas City Chiefs, who desperately need a wide receiver.
If the 49ers were to trade for a wide receiver of their own, say George Pickens or Brian Thomas Jr., then by all means, trade Aiyuk. Give him a fresh start elsewhere. Move on.
But if the 49ers don't trade for Pickens or Thomas or some other young potential No. 1 receiver, they should keep Aiyuk. They currently need a wide receiver as desperately as any team in the league. Relying on Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Watkins is not smart. Because Evans is old and breaking down, and if he misses a playoff game, the 49ers will lose.
Unless they have Aiyuk. We know he has terrific chemistry with Brock Purdy. So why just give him away for next to nothing? Why not keep him until the end of the season, and then cut him?
Let him earm some of those millions the 49ers feel he stole from them.

title: 4 Pivotal Plays That Helped the 49ers Beat the Raiders
full_text:
Defeating the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 proved to be a little challenging for the San Francisco 49ers , as it got a tad messy in the third quarter.
That is where four pivotal plays that helped them beat the Raiders took place. Without those plays, it would have been a much closer game. Let's dive into what those four pivotal plays for the 49ers were.
JADEN SAID MINE ☝️ 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/a5Qu8O0ACx
The Raiders opened up the second half with the ball trailing 21-10. They needed to put together a touchdown-scoring drive to get back in the game.
But on the very first play of the third quarter, rookie Jaden Dugger received a gift from Kirk Cousins. I'm not sure if Cousins tried to throw away a pass or was inaccurate, but he threw a layup to Dugger for an interception.
The rookie took it back for a 35-yard touchdown, putting the 49ers up 28-10.  Dugger will never receive an easier pick-six than the one Cousins gifted him. The first one of his career.
Trailing 28-17 at the 5:30 mark in the third quarter, the Raiders started their drive at the 49ers' 40-yard line after stopping them on fourth down.
Right off the bat, Cousins connects with his receiver Tre Tucker for an 18-yard gain. Two plays later, he hits tight end Michael Mayer for what was close to being a touchdown.
However, Upton Stout did his best Fred Warner impression by punching the ball out from Mayer. Warner would recover the fumble in the endzone, causing a touchback.
The Raiders were poised to score on that play, if not one of the next. Stout made an amazing play to deny the Raiders points, which would've made it a four-point game.
Fred Warner STOPS the QB sneak attempt @49ers 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/OuE87DqSfK
After the 49ers extended their lead to 35-17, the Raiders were once again putting together a promising series. They were poised to score six, but at the 12:39 mark of the fourth quarter, they were denied at the one-yard line.
Warner blew up Cousins' sneak, which should've been automatic. He perfectly timed the snap to catapult himself over the offensive line to stop Cousins.
That allowed Dre Greenlaw to push through and tackle Cousins. The play resulted in a loss of two yards, placing the 49ers in a better position to deny a touchdown again.
Two plays after Warner's super hero act, Renardo Green proved yet again that he's leaps and bounds better than he was last season. On 2nd-and-13, Cousins took a corner end zone shot for Tucker.
He thought Tucker was open, but little did he know Green baited him into the throw. As soon as Cousins began his wind up, Green bailed to the receiver and perfectly high-pointed the ball for the pick.
At that point, the game was over. The Raiders needed a touchdown with only 12 minutes left in the game. Green was playing chess, not checkers on that one.

title: 4 Winners, 2 Losers From 49ers' Win Over Raiders: Jordan Watkins Flashes
full_text:
For most of the game, the San Francisco 49ers had an easy go of it against the Las Vegas Raiders.
It went as expected, with the 49ers winning 38-17 to get back on track after the Bye. So, who were the winners and losers from the 49ers' expected win? We break it all down below.
Have a day, Jordan Watkins. The second-year receiver made a nice impact in this game, tallying four catches for 86 yards and a touchdown. Three of his four catches went for first downs.
He also ran a team-high 26 routes. Watkins got his opportunities in this game and delivered. That is certainly going to go a long way with Kyle Shanahan.
Watkins came close to having a breakout game in Week 7 against the Falcons, but couldn't secure a couple of big-time catches. This time, he made sure to seize his opportunities. His stock is up.
This was one of Fred Warner's best performances of the season. As usual, he forced a fumble, his fifth of the year and a career-high for him in a season.
No one executes the "peanut punch" as perfectly as Warner does. But his most impressive play came in the fourth quarter, when he stone-walled Kirk Cousins on a goal-line quarterback sneak.
Warner continues to prove why he's a cut above the rest. He's trekking towards earning the Defensive Player of the Year award. If there were midseason awards, he'd win it right now.
The yips may have disappeared for Eddy Pineiro , as he nailed every single one of his extra-point (5) and field-goal attempts (1) in this game. That will go a long way for him.
It proves that he's greatly benefiting from the Bye Week. The only way he would shake off the yips was by getting away and clearing his mind. After one game back, it looks like he's succeeded.
One question entering this game was how the 49ers would integrate Marques Sigle. He's been out for the last three games with an ankle sprain, but he was playing well before his injury.
The 49ers couldn't deny him snaps, which means one safety had to cede playing time. Sure enough, the 49ers had Sigle take some snaps from Ji'Ayir Brown, which was the right call.
Sigle saw 28 snaps, while Brown saw 32. This is a great sign for Sigle that he still has the coaching staff's trust and that there's a world where he can supplant Brown.
One reason the 49ers couldn't enjoy the win against the Raiders was that rookie Gracen Halton suffered a season-ending broken ankle. Halton got rolled up by teammate Keion White.
You have to feel for Halton. He was killing it this season and was arguably the 49ers' best rookie. Now, his promising season comes to a halt, and the 49ers lose an impactful defensive lineman.
Kirk Cousins was fairly comfortable whenever he had to drop back to pass. That's because the 49ers' pass rush only pressured him nine times on his 32 dropbacks, with zero sacks.
It was a pitiful display considering they got Nick Bosa back and reunited with DeForest Buckner. The 49ers' pass rush didn't look any different than it did against the Falcons.
This should be cause for concern. Maybe it pushes the 49ers to make a trade for another defensive lineman, especially after Halton's injury.

title: 5 Notable Lineup Changes the 49ers Made in Week 9
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers came out of the bye week and had a few notable lineup decisions to make. What were some noteworthy differences coming out of the bye week?
Demarcus Robinson returned to the lineup, and was second amongst the wide receivers in snaps. Brandin Cooks went from a starter to the 49ers' number three. Jacob Cowing went from an increasing role to fading out of the picture. Perhaps more notable is that Jordan Watkins still led the team in snaps and receiving production. When Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans come back, there is a chance that Watkins joins them as the top three , and Robinson is a fourth man.
The team added DeForest Buckner, and he stepped into a normal starter's workload of snaps. That meant that rookie Gracen Halton was going to play less. He went from getting the bulk of the snaps on the defensive front to being the third man and playing less than 20 snaps. He was already going to play a career-low in snaps, but an injury made that official. Halton left the game on a cart with an air cast on his leg.
The team was not going to lean on him as much, but now they might not have him for the foreseeable future. James Thompson and Sebastian Valdez went from rotational contributors to being out of the mix.
The team got Nick Bosa back. He led the way for the group. Then, the team mostly had Mykel Williams and Romell Height rotate based on down, distance, and personnel. Keion White mixed in for Bosa and also got a few snaps, mixing in with Williams and Height. Bosa finished with 30 snaps; the other three were all under 20.
Marques Sigle returned after missing two weeks. However, Malik Mustapha might have been the 49ers' best safety when he was gone. So, the team decided to rotate all three safeties. Mustapha played with Sigle. Mustapha played with Brown. Then, Brown played with Sigle. They rotated all three throughout the game. The 49ers should eventually settle on a pairing, but it's smart to use this time to see what works best.
The 49ers saw Renardo Green leave with what could be a serious injury. Rookie Ephesians Prysock stepped in for him now that they had released Jack Jones .

title: How the 49ers' Trade Deadline Plans have Shifted After Their Week 9 Win
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 to move to 7-1 just two days before the NFL trade deadline. Returning from the bye week, the game has changed the team's trade deadline needs.
The talk of the 49ers adding to the offensive line or a skill player like a receiver seems to be gone. Connor Colby has been up and down and appears to be matchup-dependent. Still, he has shown that he is a capable enough starter, even if they could improve the spot.
At receiver, the 49ers got Demarcus Robinson back healthy. Jordan Watkins has strung three solid games together. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel will be back soon, as will De’Zhaun Stribling.
All of a sudden, it does not look like the team needs a wide receiver as much as they have in recent weeks.
Nick Bosa returned from injury but looked a bit slow as he is still working himself back from a calf injury. Former first-round pick Mykel Williams had the bye week to reset and came out flat. Rookie Romello Height has not seen enough consistent growth, and Keion White is a rotational runner.
With DeForest Buckner added to the interior, it is starting to look like the biggest need right now is an edge rusher. Khalil Mack has been speculated to the 49ers for weeks. Sitting at 0-8, the Los Angeles Chargers might finally be ready to make a trade.
If the 49ers cannot add to the front seven, they need to find a way to add to the secondary. Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir might be back soon, but both suffered injuries in Week 9. With Jack Jones cut and Nate Hobbs inactive, the team was quite thin at cornerback.
Hobbs might be getting a helmet soon, and Ephesians Prysock is being eased in. Still, another cornerback would not hurt.
The team could also add a safety. They rotated three safeties and mixed and matched who played with each other. Malik Mustapha was benched to start the year. Marques Sigle was benched last year. Ji’Ayir Brown has been benched throughout his career.
The team has three options at safety, and at the same time, they do not have a long-term option at safety. It is an underrated need.

title: 49ers Grades After 38-17 Win Over the Raiders: Kyle Shanahan Makes Key Adjustment
full_text:
SANTA CLARA -- The 49ers just beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 . Here are the 49ers' grades for this performance.
Brock Purdy played well, but hasn't played like an MVP candidate since Mike Evans went down. Today, he scrambled extremely well, but that's partly because he didn't trust his receivers, with the exception of Jordan Watkins (more on him in a minute). Purdy usually lets it rip before receivers have made their breaks. Now, he's holding the ball longer than ever and using his legs more than he probably would like to. Because when he does let it rip, and Evans isn't on the field, Purdy often gets intercepted. Either Evans needs to come back soon, or the 49ers need to trade for another wide receiver. Otherwise, Purdy will struggle against decent defenses. Fortunately for him, the Raiders' defense is laughable.
Christian McCaffrey averaged just 3.8 yards per carry against a horrendous run defense, but he also scored two touchdowns -- one on the ground and one through the air. And he wasn't even the 49ers' leading rusher. That was Kaelon Black, who averaged a whopping 6.4 yards per carry. The more the 49ers give him the ball, the better their offense performs, because the 49ers are a run-first offense, and they can't control the game with their rushing attack if they use just one running back. Today, they ran the ball 43 times. They couldn't have done that without Black.
Jordan Watkins committed two penalties and still was the only good wide receiver in the game for the 49ers. He caught four passes for 86 yards and a touchdown, and looked like a quality complementary receiver, but not a go-to guy. Not someone who could catch 10 passes in a game. Against better defenses, the 49ers will need Mike Evans or some other wide receiver they could add via trade in the next day or two (George Pickens? Brian Thomas Jr.?). Demarcus Robinson certainly doesn't count. Neither does Deebo Samuel.
George Kittle had four catches for 58 yards. Luke Farrell had zero catches yet again. Hard to believe the 49ers gave him a three-year deal just to make no impact. Thank goodness they still have Kittle.
They gave up just one sack and helped pave the way for the offense to gain 190 yards on the ground. Still, they got stopped on a quarterback sneak because Jake Brendel and Dominick Puni generated no movement at the point of attack against a junior varsity defensive line.
The 49ers' defensive linemen recorded four tackles for loss and helped shut down the Raiders' anemic run game, but they never sacked Kirk Cousins, who is extremely sackable. Fortunately for the D-linemen, Cousins threw three bonehead interceptions. Still, the 49ers probably were expecting Nick Bosa and DeForest Buckner to superchange their pass rush, but they didn't. Neither made a big impact, and the 49ers now haven't recorded a sack in their past two games. In addition, they lost rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton to a season-ending leg injury with fewer than four minutes left in the game while leading by 18 points. That hurts. The 49ers might need to trade for another pass rusher before Tuesday's deadline.
Fred Warner might be the best player in the NFL. Today, he recorded just 5 tackles, but he forced a fumble, recovered a fumble, and jumped over the pile at the goal line to stop a quarterback sneak for a two-yard loss. That final play was one I've never seen a linebacker make. I didn't know it was physically possible to stop a quarterback for a two-yard loss on a sneak. Warner invents new ways to be great every week. And he isn't the only good linebacker on the team. Dre Greenlaw had three tackles for loss, and rookie Jaden Dugger had a pick-six.
Renardo Green and Malik Mustapha each intercepted Cousins once, which is impressive considering Cousins wasn't under much pressure. Still, Cousins gift-wrapped those interceptions. Collectively, this group gave up 7 catches for 111 yards and a touchdown to Brock Bowers, the only legitimate weapon on the Raiders. You'd like to think a Super Bowl-caliber defense could shut down one player, even if he's great. In addition, the 49ers gave up 3 catches for 37 yards to backup tight end Michael Mayer, who fumbled at the goal line and was flagged for a ticky-tack offensive pass interference penalty in the end zone that negated a touchdown catch. The 49ers seem to have issues covering quality tight ends. Something to monitor the rest of the season.
Eddy Pineiro made all of his field-goal attempts and extra points, but the kickoff coverage team gave up a 54-yard return. Unacceptable.
Raheem Morris' defense forced five turnovers, but most of them were gifts from the Raiders, who stink. It's alarming that Morris' defense generated minimal pressure on Cousins and struggled to cover the Raiders' two tight ends, even when they lacked a viable threat at wide receiver and running back. The 49ers should consider trading for a safety before the deadline because Ji'Ayir Brown is a liability.
On offense, Kyle Shanahan won the game because he committed to the run game and finally trusted his young weapons, unlike two weeks ago when the 49ers lost to the Falcons, who are worse than the Raiders. In that game, Shanahan refused to feature Watkins and Black, and so the 49ers lost. Today, Watkins was the leading receiver, and Black was the leading rusher. And as a result, the 49ers offense scored 31 points. Good to see Shanahan honestly size up his performance during the bye week so he could improve. Now, he needs to make another trade.

title: Promising 49ers Rookie Suffers Season-Ending Injury
full_text:
Injuries continue to pile up for the San Francisco 49ers .
This time, it is rookie Gracen Halton. He broke his ankle in the 49ers' Week 9 38-17 win against the Las Vegas Raiders. He's expected to miss the remainder of the season.
Brutal. Just brutal for Halton. His season-ending injury has made it tough for the 49ers to enjoy their win. Halton was having a strong, promising season. He established himself as a key player on the defensive line in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks.
Halton broke out massively in that game with a sack and a forced fumble that he recovered for a touchdown. He was elite in that game, but has been solid in every other game.
The 49ers drafted Halton for his pass-rushing skills, and he's lived up to the bill. However, he's been a surprising help defending the run, too. Halton's been an impactful player through and through.
His loss will sting the 49ers and his development. This makes acquiring DeForest Buckner look even better. They reunited with Buckner to give them a premier interior presence.
But it was also to strengthen their defensive line depth. Now, their depth takes a hit with Halton ruled out for the rest of the season.
Second-year defensive tackle C.J. West will be back soon, which will help their depth a bit. But West isn't good. Not even a little bit.
He will fill Halton's spot in name and nothing more. Mykel Williams will need to be the player that steps up and finally prove the 49ers right for drafting him No. 11 overall.
Williams was quiet in the win against the Raiders. He made zero impact in the game. That needs to be the last time he tursn into a ghost with Halton out.
Sebastian Valdez will need to step up as well. If not, the 49ers can always consider a trade. The deadline is in a couple of days.
Another defensive tackle or an edge rusher would go a long way for the 49ers. They have an amazing defense. It would be a shame if they didn't maximize it by trying to make their pass rush come alive.
Surprisingly, they've performed better against the run than rushing the passer. The 49ers will have much to think about over the next 48 hours.

title: Buccaneers Lineman Calls Out Bears’ Jeffery Simmons for Dirty Play
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers dropped their Sunday Night Football game to the Chicago Bears 27-24, and with that, they were unable to take the outright lead in the NFC South.
The story of the game was Tampa Bay's considerable number of turnovers on defense, getting five off the Bears, and considerable ineptitude on offense. The Bucs only scored 10 points off of five turnovers, and quarterback Baker Mayfield even threw a pick-six that saw Chicago add seven points to the board.
One of the biggest challenges the Bucs faced was Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who Chicago acquired right before the trade deadline. But when asked about him after the game, Bucs tackle Luke Goedeke said that some aspects of Simmons' tool kit have "no place" in the game.
Goedeke told ESPN writer Kalyn Kahler that he thought Simmons was both holding too much and also launching himself at his head at various points in the game.
“I mean, you’re holding me on one, you came right at my head,” Goedeke said . “I mean, that’s always fun. He’s known for it on pass pro, just holding the tackle so that the DE can run free, so I got that twice. So that’s always a good one. But, yeah, just kind of going back and forth. I mean, respect the guy, but some of the stuff he can really take out of his game. It’s just kind of old, to be honest.”
Goedeke elaborated further, saying that the tactics Simmons used during the matchup have no "place in the game".
"There's no reason to just come out on a TE and just drill a tackle in the side of the head," Goedeke said. "[There's] really not a place in the game for that, to be honest with you."
This wasn't the only grievance that the Bucs had with the Bears. Quarterback Baker Mayfield also told reporters that the Bears were calling out Tampa Bay's snap counts during the matchup, which should have been enforced as a penalty if that claim were true.
Bucs QB Baker Mayfield says he doesn’t know what went into the O-line having five false starts Sunday night, though he says the last one came about because the Bears were “barking out the cadence,” which you can’t do. Acknowledges that it’s tough for the refs to call that one,… pic.twitter.com/cMsobPlg1y
Goedeke also isn't even the first Bucs lineman who has had some beef with Simmons. When the Bucs and the Tennessee Titans held joint practice together in 2025, and during that practice, lineman Cody Mauch got into with Simmons after a rep against him.
It’s getting chippy early between Bucs-Titans 👀 Cody Mauch and Jeffery Simmons getting after it with one another leading to both teams having some words. I’ve missed you football. pic.twitter.com/bVCXe9btHd
Despite all of this, though, the Bucs lost that game against the Bears — and their offense floundered while doing so. Tampa Bay has plenty it needs to figure out over the bye week, and it will certainly need to fix some of its offensive woes when it faces off against the Detroit Lions in Week 11.
The Bucs are 3-6 and half a game out of the NFC South lead. They'll have to string together some wins to take the NFC South, and to do that, the offense simply must be better.

title: Grading Every Buccaneers Position Group After Loss to Bears
full_text:
CHICAGO — Another primetime game for the Bucs in the books — but this time, they couldn’t come away with a win.
The Chicago Bears' offense had some sloppy play throughout, with Caleb Williams having a rough night with four interceptions, but poor execution offensively by the Buccaneers meant that they never could really take advantage.
Let’s take a deep dive into each position group and give our report cards out to each one of them. Some of them are not too bad, but some are not too pretty.
It wasn’t a great game from Baker Mayfield. Two interceptions, some off throws, holding onto the ball too late — it just felt like a mess at times. It didn’t help that some of his playmakers couldn’t catch and execute on their own end, either.
Mayfield admitted after the game that turnovers are something he has to clean up, certainly when one of them went straight for six points for the Bears. This offense has to once again turn it around and, it starts with QB1.
Bucky Irving is playing at phenomenal level right now. He's making guys miss, he's hard to tackle and he fights for every extra yard. He’s been the bright spot of this team and the top weapon offensively for weeks. Kenny Gainwell had a big 44-yard play that helped the Bucs get into the red zone.
With solid blocking up front, I thought both running backs took advantage of the holes when they were there.
This group has been a major letdown going into this season.
Injuries certainly aren’t helping, but when the wideouts are on the field, simple catches and important ones alike are being dropped. Ted Hurst got benched after his drop Sunday night. Tez Johnson had two drops, too, but stayed in the game because of his experience.
This group has to do better mixed in with better play from QB1.
This group isn’t much of a threat in the passing game, and I don’t know if it’ll ever be under Zac Robinson. For the most part, the blocking has been the best part of this unit.
There were some targets to Cade Otton in this game, but Mayfield couldn’t hit him on the throws. Blocking surely helps, but the pass-game threat needs to show life here soon.
This unit did the best they could with how well Chicago’s front seven has been playing as of late, certainly with the addition of Jeffery Simmons.
There were holes for Irving and Gainwell and a good amount time for Mayfield in the pocket. Penalties hurt this grade a tad, but overall, play-wise, not too shabby.
Interior Defensive Line: B
I really liked what I saw from this room along with the pass rush off the edge. They were able to get movement up front and get Williams moving into uncomfortable positions. This certainly helped with the four interceptions on the night in the secondary.
For the most part, this group was finding a groove all throughout the night.
Without having Yaya Diaby in the mix, David Walker, Anthony Nelson and Al-Quadin Muhammad had to step up. Luckily, once again, Rueben Bain Jr. continues to grow. He had a huge play tackling Luther Burden III and causing a fumble, which was recovered by safety Ifeatu Melifonwu.
There were a few plays where things went sideways for Alex Anzalone and Josiah Trotter. I noticed from the press box that Anzalone had to call out Trotter on a missed gap assignment that allowed the Bears to get a first down.
Eye discipline was good, though, with Trotter having a few plays rushing after Williams and not allowing for easy dump-offs. Anzalone grabbed his third interception of the season after having two last week against the Falcons.
It wasn’t a pretty start for the cornerback room, primarily for Zyon McCollum, giving up a touchdown and surrendering wide-open Bears players. He turned around his play by grabbing two interceptions, reaching a career season high of four. McCollum's tackling stood out as well, and he's looked strong in that department all season.
Jacob Parrish tipped a ball off Williams' and helped Anzalone have a takeaway, giving Tampa Bay's offense great field position.
Antoine Winfield Jr. left the game fairly early with an ankle injury after colliding with Calijah Kancey on a tackle. Tykee Smith grabbed an interception, and overall, the unit did fine with the help of the Bucs’ pass rush. Melifonwu picked up a fumble in Bears’ territory, allowing Tampa Bay to tie the game.
Overall, this unit played well.
The kickoff team almost gave up a touchdown, but luckily a holding penalty was called, killing that chance. Kevin Knowles, primarily a gunner on punt teams, had impressive plays throughout the game. He was a fantastic addition right before the season began from Kansas City. Chase McLaughlin is Chase McLaughlin — always a trusted source.

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Close Loss to Bears
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers kept it close against the Chicago Bears, but in the end, they weren't able to get a big win in the Windy City.
The Bucs fell to the Bears 27-24 on Sunday Night Football, dropping them to 3-6. It was a game where Tampa Bay's defense dominated once again, netting five turnovers and holding Chicago's offense at bay for most of the game, but the Bucs were unable to get anything going on offense and they couldn't get the win as a result.
As always, we're giving our overreactions to this matchup — here's how we're feeling after Tampa Bay's loss:
The Buccaneers' offense is a mess almost everywhere (we'll talk more about that later). But perhaps the most pressing need the team has is at wide receiver, and that showed itself in a big way on Sunday night.
Tampa Bay's wide receiver corps had numerous drops on the night — rookie Ted Hurst was benched because he had one, and Tez Johnson had two drops across the night. Once again, tight end Cade Otton dominated the target share with eight of them, and outside of a huge bomb to Johnson that saw him net 76 yards on the night, no other Bucs receiver had over 40.
Chris Godwin remains an ineffective part of the offense despite being on a $22 million deal. Emeka Egbuka was drafted by the Bucs in the first round last year, and he has not looked like a WR1.
The Bucs really, really feel the absence of Mike Evans. They need a definitive WR1 on the team, and they need it badly if the passing game is to repair itself in future seasons.
But for right now, though...
The Bucs have had a strong run game with Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell, but that cannot carry the entire offense. The Bears proved that.
Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson's passing schemes have struggled all year, and they've continued to flounder when they've actually been needed. The aforementioned wide receiver issue continues to persist, and on top of all that, Tampa Bay's quarterback hasn't played up to standard at all.
Baker Mayfield is making $55 million a year on his extension, but his pressure-to-sack ratio is just under 32% (that's bad) and he threw a backbreaking interception that went for a pick-six, giving the Bears seven points in a game where the defense was holding them at bay. Mayfield has thrown three touchdowns and four interceptions, and his 32.4 QBR is 30th in the NFL.
The Bucs need the passing game to thrive. It doesn't look like there's a way it gets any better this season, and Tampa Bay will continue to lose games as a result.
Despite all that, though? This defense is elite. They generate more turnovers than anyone else in the NFL, they remain stout against the run and the pass, and they have multiple All-Pro-level players on the team this year who are showing out.
That will be enough to win the NFC South. The Carolina Panthers, Atlanta Falcons and New Orleans Saints don't have offenses half as potent as the Bears do, and Tampa Bay should muster enough wins in their next four NFC South matchups to win the division and make the playoffs.
The team isn't good enough to beat good teams and win a playoff game. But they are good enough to win the division and get there.
And if that happens, the Bucs have an interesting question to ask — What happens next?
